items.desc:
Our Mission
Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.

We are hiring an AI Researcher (f/m/d) to join our Pre-training team and help advance the architecture and training of our next generation of foundation models. If you are excited about how large models learn, want to run experiments that feed directly into production training runs, and want hands-on time on large-scale clusters (thousands of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs), we would love to hear from you.

Team Culture
We foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose. We collaborate closely on complex technical problems, working in pairs or using mob programming to resolve challenging issues. New team members learn through real work: from your first weeks you will pair with experienced researchers on live problems, and take on more ownership as you grow into it.

About the Role
As an AI Researcher in Pre-training (f/m/d), you will work on the technical levers that determine the success of our next-generation models: architecture, optimization, stability, and scaling.

Working at the intersection of research and engineering, you will learn to translate mathematical reasoning and empirical observations into principled training decisions, from small-scale proxy experiments to multi-thousand-GPU runs. You will start with well-scoped problems alongside senior researchers and progressively take ownership of larger parts of the training recipe.

We are looking for someone with strong fundamentals, sharp experimental instincts, exceptional skills, and the drive to go deep fast. You learn as much from a failed run as from a paper, you write code others can build on, and you want to become an expert in large-scale pre-training.

Your Responsibilities

 - Recipe & Architecture Experiments: Design and run ablations on core elements of the training recipe (optimizers, schedules, initialization), and implement PyTorch-based architectural changes. Evaluate their effect on convergence, stability, and training efficiency.

 - Scaling Experiments: Run and analyze small-scale proxy experiments, and contribute to the hyperparameter scaling laws and scale-up methods we use to predict behavior at multi-thousand-GPU scale.

 - Run Monitoring & Debugging: Help monitor large-scale training runs and investigate convergence issues such as loss spikes and divergence. Work with the team to track down distributed training failures.

 - Research to Practice: Follow the literature, reproduce promising results at small scale, and bring ideas worth testing to the team.

 - Cross-Team Collaboration: Work with the Compute Performance, Data, Evaluation, and Post-Training teams to understand how hardware constraints and the rest of the model lifecycle shape pre-training decisions.

Core Qualifications

 - You are proficient in Python and have hands-on experience with PyTorch.

 - You have a strong foundation in machine learning, shown through research (e.g., a PhD, a strong MS'c thesis, or publications), open-source contributions, or substantial professional or substantial personal projects.

 - You have a solid mathematical background (linear algebra, probability, optimization) and enjoy reasoning formally about why models train the way they do.

 - You understand how transformers work and have pre-trained LLMs from scratch yourself, even at small scale.

 - You design experiments carefully, report noisy and negative results honestly, and can explain clearly what your evidence does and does not show.

 - You have a track record of picking up unfamiliar technical areas quickly and going deep, for example by reimplementing papers, ramping up on a large new codebase, or debugging a problem well outside your comfort zone.

 - You write clean, maintainable code and care about reproducible experiments.

 - You communicate clearly, raise problems early, and actively seek out and act on feedback.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Distributed Training: Experience training models on multi-GPU or multi-node setups, or familiarity with distributed frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, torchtitan) and parallelism strategies (data, tensor, pipeline, expert).

 - Training Dynamics: Familiarity with scaling laws, hyperparameter transfer (e.g., µP), or recent work on optimizers and training stability.

items.desc: About us We are building a global leader in physical AI, anchored in Europe’s strongest robotics heritage. Founded by entrepreneurs with backgrounds in scaling digital products and advanced robotics, the team is bolstered by senior leadership from top-tier AI research labs and industrial tech companies. Driven by a mission to create versatile and trustworthy embodied AI for physical labor, we fuse deep engineering mastery in AI and mechatronics with a rapid-execution culture. We are addressing the labor shortage by closing the gap to production-grade deployment. This means building the trusted alternative: robots that are safe, secure, and engineered to automotive standards of scale and durability. We are well-capitalized and now assembling our team. Our Locations: Vesoma has two main locations: Munich, Germany and Limassol, Cyprus. This pan-European setup represents our core ambition of building a European technology leader, gives us a great talent base and a strong corporate structure. Your mission The role As an AI Engineer for Large-Scale Pre-Training, you enter as a key member of the early AI team. You will work directly with our AI leadership and researchers to define the infrastructure we use to train large-scale robot foundation models on petabyte-scale datasets across our GPU fleet. This infrastructure is a critical part of our research and development cycle: it must strike the right balance between stability and velocity, enabling fast research iterations based on reliable results. This is a full-time, permanent position. Your profile Key responsibilities Scalable Training Infrastructure: Develop software infrastructure to train multi-billion-parameter robot foundation models efficiently on large video datasets across multi-node GPU clusters. Data Pipelines: Build high-throughput, reliable data pipelines that stream, decode and preprocess petabyte-scale video datasets, keeping our GPUs fully utilized and supporting deterministic, resumable training. Experiment Management: Build the tools to organize, monitor and optimize large training workloads and model sweeps. Remove bottlenecks in our training pipelines and make sure all our runs maintain the highest possible goodput. Who we are looking for We seek people who embrace the empirical nature of AI research and want to accelerate our research velocity with best-in-class tools - so that we can all make breakthroughs faster, together. Experience: 3+ years of hands-on experience training multi-billion-parameter models on multi-node GPU clusters, including supervising long-running experiments, in-flight debugging and optimizing goodput and MFU. Core Skills: Deep expertise in distributed training and training efficiency at scale. In detail: Distributed Training: Data parallelism and sharding (DDP, FSDP/FSDP2, ZeRO), tensor, pipeline and sequence parallelism, and frameworks such as Megatron-Core, DeepSpeed, TorchTitan or JAX/GSPMD. Training Efficiency: BF16/FP8 mixed precision, activation checkpointing, FlashAttention, and profiling with PyTorch Profiler or Nsight Systems. Fault Tolerance: Distributed and asynchronous checkpointing, automatic recovery, and diagnosing NCCL and hardware failures. Core Stack: Python, PyTorch and/or JAX, CUDA, NCCL, and cluster orchestration with Slurm or Kubernetes. A plus: High-throughput data pipelines for large video datasets (WebDataset, Mosaic Streaming, Ray Data, DALI/NVDEC); custom kernels in Triton or CUDA; familiarity with multimodal or robot foundation models (VLAs, video transformers, diffusion/flow-matching policies); experiment tracking and sweep infrastructure (Weights & Biases, MLflow, Hydra). Mindset: You balance the agility of a startup with the professional rigor required for a global industrial player. You are a curious builder who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced research environment, and an engineer with a research mindset who understands the workflows of cutting-edge AI research and supports them with rigorous software engineering. Why us? The Team : Work alongside leadership with a proven track record of building unicorn-scale companies and defining global robotics standards. Smart Strategy : We operate as disciplined fast followers. Capital is timed to the deployment inflection point, avoiding early-mover dead ends to scale fast on proven foundations. Resources : We are substantially internally funded and attract top-tier investors to avoid any capital constraints for our mission. Historic Opportunity : Join at the dawn of a new industry comparable to the rise of the automobile. Help shape the European champion in this trillion-dollar market. We are an equal opportunity employer. Legal notice · Privacy policy

items.desc: Job Details Section Institute of Sound & Vibration Research Location: Highfield Campus Salary £37,369 per annum Full Time Fixed Term until 31/01/2029 Closing Date: Wednesday 16 December 2026 Interview Date To be confirmed Reference 3556226DA Overview We are seeking a Research Fellow to join LungSight, a multidisciplinary project developing low-cost, non-invasive audio-visual AI for earlier identification of chronic lung disease. The project aims to support a shift from reactive, clinic-based diagnosis towards proactive home screening using everyday devices such as smartphones, tablets and home computers. Based in the School of Engineering at the University of Southampton, you will lead the research engineering clinically informed acoustic features for fine-tuning machine learning models of respiratory health. You will work with large-scale real-world recordings of speech, breathing and cough, developing acoustic features that are robust to noise, demographic variation and different recording environments, predictive of early-stage chronic respiratory conditions and explainable in terms of the natural history of disease. You will also contribute to development of machine learning models and to the integration of audio with visual and clinical information. LungSight is a multi-university collaboration also involving Manchester Metropolitan University, the University of Cambridge, the University of Leicester, the University of Leeds, and the University of Sheffield alongside NHS and third-sector partners. This post will work particularly closely with a complementary PDRA at the University of Sheffield, whose research will focus more strongly on development of machine learning models while the Southampton post has a stronger focus on acoustic features and clinical knowledge mapping. The role offers opportunities for high-quality publications, open research outputs, clinical and stakeholder engagement, and career development at the interface of AI and healthcare. Main duties and responsibilities Develop and evaluate acoustic feature sets predictive of respiratory health using speech, breathing and cough recordings. Curate, pre-process and analyse large-scale real-world audio datasets, including sensitive healthcare and helpline recordings processed within appropriate secure data environments. Fine-tune and validate models on labelled respiratory datasets and clinically relevant downstream tasks, assessing accuracy, generalisability and clinical utility. Investigate potential confounding factors, demographic bias, background-noise effects and effects of recording environment, to support feature robustness and equitable model performance. Contribute to development of self-supervised models, working closely with the Sheffield PDRA who will lead complementary machine learning research; investigate how engineered physiological features can be combined with learned representations from the Sheffield machine-learning work. Collaborate with project researchers to develop multimodal approaches combining acoustic, visual and clinical information for respiratory disease screening. Work closely with researchers across the LungSight consortium, including Manchester Metropolitan Sheffield, Cambridge, Leicester and Leeds Universities, as well as clinical, NHS, patient/public and third-sector partners; participate in project meetings, joint research activities and dissemination. Lead and contribute to high-quality research publications and presentations, support project reporting, and contribute to the supervision and development of students where appropriate. You should hold hold a PhD (or equivalent research experience) in Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, Speech/Audio Processing, Machine Learning, Biomedical Engineering or a closely related discipline, with research experience in speech, audio, acoustic signal processing or closely related time-series analysis. Working at the University of Southampton: Check out the staff benefits and why you should join us at The University of Southampton. As a university we aim to create an environment where everyone can thrive and are proactive in fostering a culture of inclusion, respect and equality of opportunity. We believe that we can only truly meet our objectives if we are reflective of society, so we are passionate about creating a working environment in which you are free to bring your whole self to work. With a generous holiday allowance as well as additional university closure days we are committed to supporting our staff and students and open to a flexible working approach. Apply by 11.59 pm UK time on the closing date. For assistance contact Recruitment on +44(0)2380 592750 or recruitment@soton.ac.uk quoting the job number.

items.desc:
About us
 Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence
PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.
 Note: We are currently recruiting for multiple levels and positions, however please only apply for the role that best aligns with your skillset and career goals.
 Geometry is at the heart of how we think about engineering. You will work at the frontier of 3D geometry representation and generation, with a focus on making both of these ready for engineering. You will also work on closing the coupling between geometry and physics, towards generating shapes that are driven by physical objectives.
 What you will do 
 Own a research work-stream: set its technical direction, align priorities with internal and external stakeholders, and apply judgement and taste to drive progress.
 Design and train generative models over 3D geometry — representations, latent spaces, and the objectives that decide whether generated geometry is physically usable rather than merely plausible.
 Work against production numerical solvers, so model quality is measured in validated physics rather than proxy metrics.
 Work with our ML engineers, simulation engineers and customers to turn engineering challenges into mathematical formulations.
 Champion research directions valuable to the company, nurture more junior colleagues, and publish for both academic and non-academic audiences.
 What you bring to the table 
 PhD in CS, ML, mathematics, physics, engineering or a related field, with demonstrated expertise in generative modelling or learned representations of 3D geometry, covering one or more of:
 generative models for geometry — VAEs, diffusion and flow matching, autoregressive latent models, scaled to large datasets;
 geometric deep learning and 3D vision over point-cloud, mesh, voxel or implicit-field data, including sparse convolution and sparse attention;
 neural fields and shape autoencoders.
 Relevant experience in industry or a research group of comparable intensity, instrumental in: building models and pipelines in PyTorch/CUDA; bespoke problem settings involving geometric or 3D data; iterating on architecture and inductive bias; combining theoretical reasoning with empirical intuition; running experiment pipelines that produce comparable results.
 Ability to scope and deliver projects, with strong problem-solving skills.
 Enthusiasm for deep learning and probabilistic methods applied to science and engineering.
 Publications at premier conferences: SIGGRAPH, SIGGRAPH Asia, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML or ICLR, and relevant journals: TOG, TPAMI, JMLR.
 Desirable: operator learning or probabilistic methods for PDEs; self-supervised pretraining for 3D vision and/or physics surrogacy; generative inverse design linking geometry to physics objectives..
 What we offer 
 Build what actually matters 
 Help shape an AI-native engineering company at a formative stage, tackling problems that genuinely matter for industry and society. This is work with real-world impact - and something you can be proud to stand behind.
 Learn alongside exceptional people 
 Work with a high-caliber, collaborative team of engineers, scientists, and operators who care deeply about doing great work, and about helping each other get better. We come from diverse backgrounds, but we share a commitment to operating at the highest level and addressing some of the most complex challenges out there. If you’re ambitious, thoughtful, and driven by impact, you’ll feel at home.
 Influence over hierarchy 
 We operate with a flat structure: good ideas win - wherever they come from. Questioning assumptions and challenging the status quo isn’t just welcomed, it’s expected.
 Sustainable pace, long-term ambition 
 Building meaningful technology is a marathon, not a sprint. We believe in balancing focused, ambitious work with a life beyond it. Our hybrid model blends time together in our Shoreditch office with work-from-home days, giving you the flexibility to work sustainably while staying connected in person.
 And it doesn’t stop there … 
 🚀 Equity options - share meaningfully in the company you’re helping to build.
 🏦 10% employer pension contribution - because investing in future matters.
 🍽️ Free office lunches - to keep you energised and focused.
 👶 Enhanced parental leave - 3 months full pay paternity and 6 months full pay maternity leave, to …

Every Boltz model starts here, and the open release is what 100,000+ scientists build on. You will work closely with the Pre-training team's
items.desc: About Boltz Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible. Boltz began as an MIT spin-out. items.desc: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About The Role As a Machine Learning Intern, you join the team to explore framed topics, assess their relevance and feasibility through proofs of concept, and help the strongest ideas reach production. You own your project end to end, from literature review and scoping to implementation and benchmarking, on topics shaped by live projects and production needs. You work in a fast-paced engineering team with an industrial, production-first mindset, on cutting-edge research topics in an emerging defense company where the stakes are high. You are a full member of the team, with visibility on how the company and its products evolve and a direct impact on what we ship. Responsibilities Run literature reviews and state-of-the-art analyses on computer vision and machine learning topics framed by the team. Scope projects, define tasks, and decide which approaches to benchmark, from baselines to the most prominent algorithms. Build experimentation plans and define implementation architectures for novel approaches. Collect, prepare, synthesize, and augment data for model training and evaluation. Implement, train, and benchmark models across topics such as foundation models, knowledge distillation, CNNs, transformers, and embedded models. Explore multi-sensor fusion and the processing of temporal data where projects call for it. Evaluate results rigorously with task-specific metrics to judge relevance and feasibility. Develop proofs of concept and support the transition of promising ones towards production. Present concepts, results, and project status to the team and to wider audiences, and join team meetings to learn from other projects. Candidate Requirements Currently pursuing an MSc in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field. Hands-on experience with ML projects involving model training and evaluation, ideally across different tasks and architectures such as CNNs and transformers. Ability to select the best-performing model for a use case and to choose suitable task-specific evaluation metrics. Familiarity with computer vision and image processing is a plus, such as classification, detection, tracking, segmentation, depth estimation, or 3D vision. Awareness of model scale trade-offs, from large multi-GPU architectures to small optimized models on embedded platforms. Motivated, autonomous, and proactive, with the ability to own a project and communicate results clearly. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

items.desc: Full-time (100%), permanent Location: Zurich, Switzerland Employer: Tufa Labs AG Start Date: 1 March 2027 or by agreement About Tufa Labs Tufa Labs is building frontier AI systems with a focus on abstract reasoning, scalable model training, and reinforcement learning. We work on problems at the intersection of foundation models, reasoning benchmarks, distributed systems, and scientific experimentation. Our goal is to develop methods that improve the reasoning capabilities of AI systems while building the infrastructure required to train and evaluate them at scale. We are looking for an AI Research Engineer who enjoys moving fluidly between research and systems engineering: designing experiments, training models, analysing results, and building the tooling that makes large-scale research possible. The Role You will contribute directly to our research on abstract reasoning benchmarks such as ARC-AGI and related environments, develop pre-training and reinforcement learning approaches for large language models, and improve the infrastructure used to train, evaluate, and deploy those models across GPU clusters. This role combines hands-on research with practical engineering. A typical week may involve implementing a new reinforcement learning method, running large-scale experiments, designing evaluation suites for reasoning tasks, profiling distributed training bottlenecks, or extending internal tooling used by researchers across the company. Responsibilities Conduct research on abstract reasoning and generalisation in AI systems, including work related to ARC-AGI and successor benchmarks. Design, implement, and evaluate novel training methods for large language models. Develop reinforcement learning pipelines for post-training and alignment. Run large-scale pre-training, fine-tuning, and evaluation experiments. Build and maintain infrastructure for distributed training on GPU clusters. Improve reliability, monitoring, scheduling, and observability of research workloads. Collaborate with researchers and engineers to convert ideas into reproducible research systems. Essential Qualifications Degree in computer science or at least 5 years of equivalent professional experience in Machine Learning or a related field. Experience training, fine-tuning, or evaluating large language models. Practical experience with reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or related optimization methods. Experience working with distributed systems and multi-GPU training environments. Ability to independently design and execute research experiments. Desirable Qualifications Experience operating GPU clusters and associated infrastructure. Contributions to machine learning research, open-source projects, or competitive benchmark efforts. Strong interest in reasoning, abstraction, program synthesis, planning, or AGI evaluation. What We Offer Permanent full-time position. Opportunity to work on frontier research problems in reasoning and model training. High degree of autonomy and ownership. Access to substantial compute resources and research infrastructure. Small, technically ambitious team with rapid decision-making and minimal bureaucracy. Opportunity to help shape the future direction of the company’s research agenda. To apply, please send your CV and a short description of relevant work to hello@tufalabs.ai

items.desc: We are looking for a Computer Vision Engineer / Machine Learning Engineer to join our Graphics team located in Helsinki. In this role, you will work alongside experts from diverse backgrounds to shape the future of on-device AI across mobile platforms (phone, PC, tablet, and automotive), redefining how people interact with the physical and digital world. Your core mission is to research and develop generative and 3D spatial AI that runs efficiently on-device — enabling machines to understand the real world and generate high-quality images, video, and 3D content in real time, under tight compute, memory, and power constraints. What You'll Do Research and develop on-device generative models for image, video, and 3D content creation and editing Build algorithms for 3D reconstruction, depth estimation, and spatial/visual understanding Optimize models for edge deployment: quantization, distillation, pruning, and NPU/GPU acceleration Take ideas from prototype to shipping product, working with hardware, platform, and product teams Qualifications PhD in Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Computer Graphics, or a related field Proven ability to turn research concepts into state-of-the-art techniques that hold up against real-world complexity Strong background in one or more of: diffusion / flow-matching / autoregressive generative models; depth estimation and 3D scene - reconstruction (NeRF, 3D Gaussian Splatting); 3D generative AI; multimodal LLMs and visual understanding; neural networks and transformers Experience with efficient inference and model compression for resource-constrained hardware is a strong plus Core programming: primary development in C++ with GLSL/HLSL compute shaders (Vulkan, OpenGL); Python, PyTorch, and CUDA for research and proof-of-concept work Familiarity with mobile inference stacks (e.g., TensorRT, CoreML, QNN, ExecuTorch, NCNN) is a plus Employement type and Locations: This is a full time employee position, based on Helsinki/Tampere office in Finland. Graphics Team Vision AI will transform every stage of the Human–Machine Interaction pipeline, evolving today's predefined user interfaces into intelligent, adaptive, and highly personalized experiences. AI + Understanding: On-device computer vision models will understand and interpret on-screen content, enabling context-aware interactions and intelligent assistance. AI + Generation: On-device Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) will generate high-quality animations and videos from a single image, unlocking richer and more dynamic user experiences. AI + Rendering: Neural rendering will progressively replace traditional mobile rendering pipelines, delivering higher visual quality, improved efficiency, and new graphics capabilities. AI + Modeling: Learning-based 3D/4D modeling approaches (e.g., VGGT and Trellis) will dramatically simplify content creation by reducing manual input and enabling intelligent scene reconstruction and editing. items.desc:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!



Role overview:

We are looking for talented individuals to help us develop state-of-the-art models for information retrieval as part of our Search team. This group is working on a range of tasks including training our embedding and reranker models. You'll have the opportunity to revolutionise people's search experience by contributing to building an intelligent, efficient and precise search system and you would have a lot of opportunity to try new things out, innovate, and productionize your ideas.

Your work will specifically focus on advancing semantic search techniques to improve accuracy and efficiency, involving working with a wide range of novel technologies and collaborating with other teams to integrate your work into our search infrastructure.

We're looking for someone who is passionate about search and has a strong background in information retrieval. Candidates should have experience working with a wide range of technologies and have worked collaboratively with other teams in the past.



Key responsibilities:

 - Design, train and improve upon cutting-edge search models.

 - Gather high-quality retrieval datasets and optimize data pipelines for model training and evaluation.

 - Work closely with the model serving team to ensure that inference is fast and stable.

 - Collaborate with product teams to develop solutions.

 - Engage in research collaborations with our partner organizations and academic affiliations and publish your work in top-tier conferences and journals.

 - Join us at a pivotal moment, shape what we build, have a strong ownership mindset, and wear multiple hats!



Qualifications:

 - Proficiency in Python and related ML frameworks such as PyTorch, Tensorflow, TF-Serving, JAX, and XLA/MLIR.

 - Familiarity with training and using various information retrieval models.

 - Experience leveraging Large Language Models as part of training data or evaluation pipelines.

 - Strong communication and problem-solving skills.



Bonus points for:

 - Experience building training and/or evaluation datasets for practical use cases.

 - Proficiency in other programming languages, such as C++ or Golang.

 - Experience using large-scale distributed training strategies with GPUs.



Working location:
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices for applications such as context understanding, dynamic awareness, augmented hearing and ones we haven’t yet imagined. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop audio understanding algorithms that enable devices to recognize what is happening in the world around them. Areas of interest include sound event detection and localization (SELD), acoustic scene understanding, unusual or anomalous sound detection, and multimodal context understanding from audio, video, and motion sensors. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel audio understanding models, from early experiments through real-time deployment on devices. Develop robust methods for sound event detection/localization, acoustic anomaly detection, and context-aware audio interpretation. Explore multimodal approaches that combine microphone signals with video, IMU, or other sensor data when useful. Build and curate datasets and data piplines, evaluation protocols, and demonstrations that measure accuracy, robustness, latency, and compute cost. Work with DSP and software engineers to integrate models into proof-of-concept systems and product platforms; communicate results and contribute to patents or conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Skills Strong hands-on experience with modern audio understanding models, including sound event detection, SELD, acoustic scene analysis, or anomaly detection. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience developing and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; strong Python skills. Understanding of audio representations, DSP, and evaluation metrics for detection, localization, and generalization. Experience with multimodal fusion (video, IMU, or other sensors) for context understanding is a plus. Experience with efficient inference, causal ML, ONNX/TFLite, embedded ML, or C/C++ is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves. ‎

BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over **** staff from 60 countries. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. Context And Mission The Machine Translation group at the AI Institute develops open translation models and the data and training pipelines behind them, including the SalamandraTA model family, and takes part in international shared tasks and European and national projects. You will join a collaborative team developing Physical AI and TinyML technologies, bringing together AI, sensing, embedded systems and hardware to create intelligent devices that interact with the physical world. You will work with researchers and students across the lab, contributing to the EPSRC TinyML UK Network, the EPSRC Green+ Network and other projects. The role combines practical engineering, research and collaboration. Activities will include developing and evaluating AI tools for edge devices, building working prototypes and demonstrations, leading and contributing to research publications and proposals, coordinating and supporting events and collaborative activities. You will collaborate with academic and industry partners, consortium members and stakeholders, and international collaborators. Support workshops, demonstrations and other activities across the EPSRC TinyML UK and Green+ networks, including hackathons and development camps. Collaborate with researchers, students, industry partners and project stakeholders. Contribute to developing research proposals and funding applications, including shaping research ideas, drafting technical content and coordinating input from project partners. You will have strong programming skills in Python and C or C++, experience developing embedded systems and integrating sensors and hardware, and experience building, training and evaluating machine learning models. An understanding of deploying AI on resource-constrained devices and a sound mathematical foundation are essential. Familiarity with TensorFlow Lite or Pytorch Executorch for Microcontrollers or comparable frameworks, risk-v robotics, neuromorphic computing, hardware acceleration, or Android and Flutter development would be advantageous. items.desc: About Inscribe At Inscribe, we're on a mission to catch fraud with confidence. In 2017, we set out to build the first document fraud detection product. Today, we process millions of applications each year and work with many of the leading fintechs and banks across the U.S. We believe the game of cat-and-mouse in fraud requires a fundamentally new approach. With care for our customers, attention to detail, and grounded execution, we’re reimagining how fraud is detected and prevented. Inscribe is trusted by leading banks and fintechs, including Coinbase, Plaid, Bluevine, and Ramp. Inscribe is backed by Threshold Ventures, Uncork Capital, Y Combinator, Crosslink Capital, and Foundry, and is headquartered in San Francisco, CA. The Opportunity Fighting fraud is a continuous battle. We’re hiring a Research Scientist to develop our fraud detection capabilities by investigating new methods, improving the ones we have and, most importantly, turning research ideas into production algorithms. The documents that pass through Inscribe are many and varied in content and format. Images are a particularly tricky file type and we are always looking for ways to extend our catch rate on them. We look for someone eager to quickly test prototypes, solve issues as they come, learn on the go. Research at Inscribe is not a siloed function but it sits at the heart of our tech team and collaborates very strictly with engineering: anyone is empowered to come up with ideas and try them, fraud fighting is a shared goal. Research informs what we do, rigorously tests ideas, quickly discards those that don’t work and communicates findings in an approachable way. Responsibilities Own research problems in document fraud detection from start to finish Help build detectors for fraud detection algorithms, with a special focus on image file types, such as edited or tampered images, JPEG manipulation and AI-generated documents. Combine classical forensics, deep learning and VLMs. Design rigorous evaluation: sampling strategies to estimate recall on unlabelled production traffic, ground-truth labelling, precision/recall trade-offs at low fraud rates, backtesting and shadow experiments. Find and sort failure modes by digging into real customer documents, and turn them into labelled datasets and new detection work. Work on LLM-based fraud detection: model and tool evaluations, agent and prompt experiments, customer-level analysis and reactive fixes. Reduce false positives by understanding what drives them, then tuning thresholds, detector combinations and per-customer configurations. Analyse our production data to detect anomalies and emerging trends in how fraud techniques change across customers and markets, and turn those insights into new detection work and product features. Shape the research roadmap: follow the literature, propose new detection bets, and decide what to stop as well as what to start. Partner with fraud analysts, product and engineering so research gets to production and changes customer outcomes. Write clear research docs and share findings in the research syncs. Tech Stack These are the main technologies we work with. We are not looking for someone with experience in all these as we believe in learning on the go, we require however candidates to have production experience with Python, SQL and AWS. Languages : Python (Django), SQL Cloud : AWS (RDS/Aurora, ECS, S3, Bedrock, etc.) Observability : Datadog, Grafana AI Platforms : Anthropic, AWS Bedrock About You Essential 3+ years applied research, ML or data science in industry, with models you built running in production. An MSc or PhD in a quantitative field (CS, statistics, physics, maths or similar), or equivalent experience. Strong statistics and experimental design: working with data from real scenarios, with missing labels, errors and biases. Ability to run experiments and evaluate results, to know what numbers matter and how to communicate them. Hands-on experience with computer vision and image analysis. Practical experience with LLMs and VLMs: evaluating and comparing models, building pipelines around them, and being able to tell when they are not the best choice. Good Python (PyTorch, NumPy, pandas) and SQL. You’re comfortable working in a production codebase and shipping with engineers, not handing off notebooks. Strong data intuition: you look at raw examples, find patterns and failure modes, and don’t trust a metric you haven’t checked against real data. A pragmatic, business-aware approach: you ship small improvements often, connect research to customer impact, and explain results clearly to non-technical people. Highly sought Experience in fraud, risk, anomaly detection or other adversarial domains. Image forensics: tamper detection, compression artefacts, or detecting AI Generated images. Experience with document data parsing: OCR, layout models, object detection, bonus if applied to financial/identity documents Experience building data-labelling pipelines. …

items.title: Data Scientist / Computer Vision Engineer — AI Skin Analysis
items.card: About the role You will help take the model from research and development through evaluation and integration into our platform. Working with our founder, developers and dermatology advisers, you will assess what can be reliably measured from photographs and build a practical approach to skin analysis. Our areas of interest include visible blemishes, redness, texture, pores, oiliness, dark circles and signs
items.desc: About Teen Skin Teen Skin is a UK skincare platform helping teenagers and parents make informed decisions about skincare through education, personalised guidance and technology. We are looking for a hands-on Data Scientist or Computer Vision Engineer to develop and improve our AI face-scan model. The feature will analyse facial photographs to provide understandable information about visible skin characteristics and support personalised skincare guidance. About the role You will help take the model from research and development through evaluation and integration into our platform. Working with our founder, developers and dermatology advisers, you will assess what can be reliably measured from photographs and build a practical approach to skin analysis. Our areas of interest include visible blemishes, redness, texture, pores, oiliness, dark circles and signs associated with dryness. A key part of the role is distinguishing features that can be assessed visually from those that require additional information or clinical assessment. Key responsibilities Review the existing AI work, available data and technical infrastructure, then propose a development roadmap. Develop, train and evaluate computer vision models for facial skin analysis. Assess suitable pretrained models and compare them with custom approaches. Establish data collection, annotation and quality-control processes using appropriately sourced and consented images. Collaborate with dermatology advisers to define meaningful labels and evaluation criteria. Build image-quality checks for lighting, blur, camera angle, filters, makeup and facial obstructions. Evaluate performance across skin tones, age groups, devices and real-world photography conditions. Define confidence scores and identify when the model should decline to provide a result. Explore how questionnaire responses can complement image analysis. Work with developers to integrate model inference into the platform. Document experiments, limitations and deployment requirements. Optimise inference costs, speed and ongoing model monitoring. Essential requirements Practical experience in data science, machine learning and computer vision. Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow. Experience training, fine-tuning and evaluating image-analysis models. Understanding of dataset quality, annotation, class imbalance, data leakage and model generalisation. Ability to evaluate model performance beyond headline accuracy. Experience deploying models through APIs or collaborating with developers on production integration. Clear communication and the ability to explain technical choices to a non-technical founder. A thoughtful approach to privacy, sensitive imagery and working with data involving young people. Desirable experience Facial image analysis, dermatology, medical imaging or skincare technology. Image segmentation, object detection or severity estimation. Evaluating fairness and performance across diverse skin tones. Model calibration, uncertainty estimation and out-of-distribution detection. FastAPI, Docker and cost-conscious deployment. Working with early-stage businesses and delivering against project milestones. What success looks like An agreed, achievable model scope; a documented data strategy; reproducible experiments; clear evaluation results; and a working model that can be integrated into the platform, with its limitations communicated honestly. The feature is intended to support skincare education and guidance. Applicants should understand the distinction between cosmetic skin analysis and medical diagnosis. What we offer Flexible remote working. Direct collaboration with the founder and input into product development. A practical opportunity to build AI with a clear user purpose. Project milestones and compensation agreed before work begins. Potential for a longer-term technical partnership. How to apply Please apply through Indeed with your CV, availability, preferred rates and examples of relevant computer vision projects. In your application, briefly explain your role in a model you have built, how you evaluated it and whether you have experience deploying it for real users. Links to a portfolio, GitHub or published work are welcome, where shareable. Pay: £35,400.00-£106,000.00 per year Work Location: Remote

items.desc: We build fast, modern developer tools in Rust, and a surprising amount of serious software runs on them. Pixi, rattler and rattler-build are open source and used by hundreds of thousands of developers: quant teams in finance, physicists at CERN, biotech labs, and humanoid robot companies you've probably seen videos of. We are also core maintainers of conda-forge, one of the largest open source package ecosystems, and we maintain RoboStack, which gets ROS running on any OS from a single lockfile. When that much software flows through your tools, security stops being optional. Every package that ends up on a laptop, a server or a robot should be traceable back to the source and build that produced it. We're building that for conda today, and we want to extend it to AI models. The engineering team is spread across Europe (Netherlands, Germany, UK, Moldova). This work is based in Berlin, and so is this role. The work Robots increasingly run learned models: vision transformers, RL policies, LLMs. Today those models are usually copied onto machines as large opaque files, with little record of where they came from or what changed. We think models should be shipped like packages: versioned, signed, verifiable, and updated efficiently. You'll work on two related areas. Package security. Signing and verification for conda packages with Sigstore, provenance from source to build to install, SBOMs, and mapping known vulnerabilities onto the packages people actually use. This work goes into Pixi, rattler and conda-forge, and is used by a lot of people. AI models as packages. Taking the same ideas to model artifacts. That includes: A provenance chain from training through packaging to deployment, with signatures that can be verified offline on air-gapped robots A model SBOM format, building on CycloneDX's ML-BOM Delta updates between model versions (full models, fine-tunes, LoRA adapters, quantized variants), so robots don't download gigabytes for a small change Compression that combines model techniques (quantization, pruning, distillation) with what package managers already do well (zstd, content-addressable storage), tuned to the target hardware and network Managing models that get fine-tuned on the robot itself: tracking where those variants came from, validating them, and syncing them back Testing the whole pipeline end to end on real models and real hardware, and measuring latency, bandwidth and model quality A lot of this is new. Part of the job is figuring out which approaches work, measuring them honestly, and writing up what you found. What we're looking for You don't need years of experience. You do need solid fundamentals, curiosity, and the patience to get security details right. Rust, or a strong background in C++, Go or Python and the wish to switch Interest in software supply chain security. Bonus if you've worked with Sigstore (Cosign, Rekor, Fulcio), TUF, in-toto, SLSA or SBOM formats Familiarity with ML in practice: you've trained or fine-tuned a model, know what a LoRA adapter or a quantized model is, and have used PyTorch or similar Basic understanding of cryptography as an engineer: signatures, hashes, certificates, and what they do and don't guarantee You like measuring things and are honest about results that don't work out You live in Berlin or are willing to move here It's a plus if you know package managers from the inside, have worked on model compression or edge inference, have robotics experience, or have contributed to open source. None of this is required. What we offer You'll work on problems few people have solved yet, together with the people who created Mamba, Pixi, rattler and RoboStack. Most of your work will be open source and used by a large community from day one. We pay a competitive Berlin salary, with 30 days of vacation, the hardware you want, a conference budget, and time for upstream open source work. We help with relocation within the EU.

items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices. You will build agentic tools and automation that make our audio ML research dramatically faster and more reproducible. The focus is on orchestrating training, evaluation, experimentation, and reporting across many types of AI models, using on-premise and/or cloud GPU infrastructure. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Design and implement agentic workflows that plan, launch, monitor, diagnose, and summarize audio ML experiments, with appropriate human oversight. Automate data preparation, model training, hyperparameter searches, benchmarking, regression testing, and result comparison across research projects. Build reliable tooling for on-premises GPU scheduling and utilization, experiment tracking, artifact management, and reproducible execution. Connect LLM-powered agents to scripts, repositories, datasets, evaluation suites, and compute resources through well-defined tools and safeguards. Partner with audio researchers to turn repetitive experiments into reusable workflows and clear dashboards or reports. Education Degree in computer science, machine learning, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Skills Strong software engineering and Python skills, with hands-on experience building LLM agents or agentic workflows that invoke tools and execute multi-step tasks. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience with ML training and evaluation pipelines, PyTorch, experiment tracking, and automated testing. Practical experience operating on-premises Linux GPU machines, including CUDA environments, containers, job scheduling, and resource monitoring. Working knowledge of audio ML and DSP, including common datasets, audio metrics, and model development workflows. Experience with orchestration frameworks, distributed training, CI/CD, or MLOps is a plus. Ability to build reliable, observable systems and communicate effectively with research scientists. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves. ‎

items.desc:
WHO WE ARE

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08328-6 cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics https://www.oxcan.org/news/prior-labs-and-oxford-cancer-analytics-partner-to-advance-liquid-biopsy-and-clinical-decision-making-in-lung-disease to preventing train failures with Hitachi https://siliconangle.com/2025/12/01/prior-labs-debuts-tabular-ai-foundation-model-scales-10-million-rows/. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ https://priorlabs.ai/about with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter https://www.linkedin.com/in/frank-hutter-9190b24b/, Noah Hollmann https://www.linkedin.com/in/noah-hollmann-668b9010b/, and Sauraj Gambhir https://www.linkedin.com/in/sauraj-g/, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP https://priorlabs.ai/blog-posts/priorlabs-sap as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.






ABOUT THE ROLE

You will have ownership over designing, building, and scaling the core systems that bring Prior Labs' foundation models to the world. This is a unique opportunity to make fundamental architectural decisions, establish engineering best practices from the ground up, and profoundly shape the technical direction for serving state-of-the-art AI.

TabPFN does its learning in the forward pass, and it now handles datasets in the millions of rows. Making that fast, reliable, and affordable is an exciting engineering challenge.

You'll work directly with world-class AI researchers, translating cutting-edge models into scalable production systems. This role offers significant autonomy and impact, with clear paths to specialize in areas you're passionate about (like inference optimization and core backend systems) or grow into a technical leadership position as our team expands. You won't just be implementing features; you'll be building the backbone of our company.



What you'll work on:

 - Own Inference: Own the serving path end-to-end: latency, throughput, batching, memory behavior on large inputs, and cost per prediction. Our models serve through our managed API, inside customer VPCs, and as self-hosted open weights, and you’ll have an impact across the board.

 - Architect & Design: Design robust, scalable, and secure backend systems and production-grade APIs for serving our foundation models.

 - Build & Implement: Develop high-quality, maintainable code for core backend services.

 - Own Infrastructure: Design, deploy, and manage core infrastructure on cloud platforms, focusing on reliability, monitoring, observability, and cost-efficiency.

 - Ensure Compliance & Security: Implement secure, GDPR-compliant systems, including data storage, access control, usage tracking, and quota management.

 - Champion Best Practices: Drive high standards for testing, CI/CD, documentation, and security within the engineering team.
   
   

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 3+ years of professional experience in machine learning and backend engineering, with a proven track record of managing production infrastructure.

 - Proven experience deploying and operating machine learning models in production, with a strong understanding of how models behave and fail under real traffic.

 - Strong, hands-on experience designing and building production-grade APIs and backend services.

 - Significant experience building and operating services on cloud platforms, with GCP preferred.

 - Strong, hands-on experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools like Terraform.

 - Significant experience with containerization and orchestration technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).

 - Proficiency in Python.



What sets you apart

 - Experience building or managing infrastructure specifically for machine learning (MLOps, model serving frameworks, feature stores, data pipelines).

 - Deep experience with inference optimization (quantization, compilation, dynamic batching, caching strategies, interplay with distributed computing).

 - Experience with PyTorch and FastAPI specifically.

 - Contributions to relevant open-source projects.

items.desc: The Optics and Sensing Laboratory at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Tübingen has an open position for a Research Engineer for Statistical 3D Model of Quadrupeds (f/m/div) to join the ongoing research efforts in the development of statistical 3D models of Quadrupeds. About Us We are creating the world’s most realistic human and animal avatars for use in research, film, virtual reality, biology and medicine. Using unique 3D & 4D capture facilities, machine learning, computer vision and advanced graphics, we are modeling every nuance of how humans and animals look and move. We develop algorithms to estimate human shape and motion in images, videos, RGB-D sequences, etc. Our approaches define the current state of the art, and we are constantly pushing these methods and systems in order to achieve a better accuracy and greater usability. Department website: https://is.mpg.de/oslab/ The Project Horses are one of the most beloved animals. They are beautiful in shape and motion, they have been used for carrying people, goods, for helping in farming, for racing, and also for therapy. We are interested in capturing horse motion from motion capture data, with the goal of building marker-less motion capture systems for horses. We are collaborating with the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences and IMATI-CNR in developing a system for the markerless motion capture of horses. Our approach is based on creating a highly realistic 3D articulated model of horses from data. To this goal, we need to capture partial 3D scans of real animals and register them to a predefined horse template. Doing this enables us to model the shape of real horses and the shape variability across a range of individuals with different characteristics. In this research context, we are looking for talented research engineer to pursue the project. Figure: a) Data capture setup, b) 3D Scan of horse, c) Model fit of scanned horse Roles & Responsibilities Investigation, implementation and evaluation of potential model improvements, for example: skeleton/joint paradigms, shape space encoding variations, pose dependent deformations, etc. Conceptualization and development of model evaluation procedures, including quantitative and qualitative metrics. Development of various Minimum-Viable-Product pipelines, including image/video mesh recovery models and use-case applications (e.g. body conformation scoring from model outputs). Enhancement of the process for re-training and establishing a continuous learning pipeline. Improvement of established robust method for registering 3D parametric model templates to cleaned 3D scans. Project management: definition and evaluation of projects steps and directions. Education & Experience Experience with 3D parametric body models (i.e. SMPL/MANO/ATLAS/VAREN/etc.) Experience in Computational Geometry, Computer Vision and Deep Learning Accepted publications in one of these fields is a big advantage Good programming skills in Python or C++; PyTorch (or similar) experience Project management experience and the ability to work independently in dynamic environments Experience in one or more of the following: Point-cloud libraries, OpenCV, 3D rendering pipelines and deep-learning frameworks Good oral and written communication skills in Englis Enjoyment for collaborative work and multidisciplinary projects A minimum of a Master’s degree is required Experience writing production level code is a plus Our offer In this working environment, you will be exposed to cutting-edge technologies related to computer vision and multi-sensor systems. The MPI for Intelligent Systems is one of the world's leading research institutions for machine learning, computer vision and robotics, and studying the concepts of intelligence and autonomous behavior in artificial systems at different length scales. The position is ideally suited for candidates looking to extend their scientific and cultural horizons particularly in the area of 3D Motion Capture. You will be a part of a dynamic team of international scientists, engineers, and administrative staff. The Max Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society seeks to increase the number of women in its workforce in those areas where they are underrepresented and therefore explicitly encourages women to apply. The position is available as of now and limited to 1 year with a possibility of extension and the expected starting date is as soon as possible. items.desc: GROUPE CALCUL Le groupe Présentation Le Réseau métier Le RT Paysage du calcul Actions RT Actions réseau Nos cafés Offres d'emploi Suivez-nous Offres d'emploi Online Learning of Generative AI models for turbulent flow inpainting Proposée par Luciano DROZDA, le 16 novembre 2026 Stage Toulouse, France CERFACS 6 mois Email Web Fichier Suivez la liste Context The Algo team at CERFACS has conducted research in hybridizing solvers of Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with AI models in order to counter theoretical limitations of classical PDE solvers (e.g., regular sampling of space and time domains, solution regularity) towards practical applications of relevance to Cerfacs industrial shareholders (see [1] and [2], for instance). Beyond hybridization, AI-based surrogate modeling presents itself as a much less expensive potential alternative to numerical simulations of interest to Cerfacs industrial shareholders (e.g., turbomachinery flows, flows over airfoils). The main technical challenge to training these AI-based surrogate models is the prohibitive high-quality training data storage requirements. For instance, in [3], an industrial Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) of compressible flow over a low-pressure turbine blade required over 11 billion degrees of freedom (DoFs) per equation. One can then estimate the size of a dataset composed of 1,000 snapshots of such a DNS to require around 1.1e10 (number of mesh points) x 5 (number of conserved variables per point) x 8 (number of bytes per DoF considering double precision) x 1,000 (number of snapshots)  440 TB for a single operational point of this blade. To circumvent the issue of prohibitive storage requirements, a training procedure referred to as online learning can be employed, where training data is generated on-the-fly as several numerical simulations run concurrently (see [4]). In this context, we aim to develop Generative AI models for turbulent flow inpainting via online learning. Inpainting consists here in filling in masked flow fields output by running instances of high-fidelity physical solvers conditioned by the rest of the flow. It allows to train AI models on large volumes of data in a self-supervised way (i.e., without the need of human labeling). In [5], a Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) was (pre-)trained to reconstruct parcels of physical fields stemming from a myriad of PDE solvers via online learning. Reconstruction distinguishes itself from inpainting through the lack of physical field conditioning in the former. Given that turbulent flow modeling essentially revolves around predicting the effects of unresolved scales conditioned by coarse-grained information, inpainting presents itself as a (pre-)training task more suited towards practical applications of AI in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) such as subgrid-scale and wall modeling, super-resolution, and sparse-sensor reconstruction. items.desc:
WHO WE ARE

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08328-6 cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics https://www.oxcan.org/news/prior-labs-and-oxford-cancer-analytics-partner-to-advance-liquid-biopsy-and-clinical-decision-making-in-lung-disease to preventing train failures with Hitachi https://siliconangle.com/2025/12/01/prior-labs-debuts-tabular-ai-foundation-model-scales-10-million-rows/. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ https://priorlabs.ai/about with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter https://www.linkedin.com/in/frank-hutter-9190b24b/, Noah Hollmann https://www.linkedin.com/in/noah-hollmann-668b9010b/, and Sauraj Gambhir https://www.linkedin.com/in/sauraj-g/, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP https://priorlabs.ai/blog-posts/priorlabs-sap as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We spend tens of millions per year on GPU compute to train tabular foundation models. That's not a target, it's what we're running today, and it's growing. The person who owns this infrastructure makes decisions worth millions of dollars: cluster architecture, scheduling efficiency, provider strategy, hardware selection.

Today we run on Slurm across multiple clusters. We're scaling to multi-cluster, multi-provider infrastructure using SkyPilot and evaluating new hardware generations as they come online. You own the full stack, from cluster orchestration and cost optimization to CI/CD, automation, and the tooling that keeps researchers moving fast. You work directly with the research team and understand what they're doing well enough to make infrastructure decisions that actually help them.

What you'll work on:

 - Own and evolve multi-cluster GPU infrastructure, from Slurm and SkyPilot on GCP today to multi-provider orchestration and new GPU generations tomorrow. Drive architecture, automated provisioning, workload scheduling, reliability, cost optimization, and capacity planning against growing compute demands

 - Build the developer productivity layer: CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, reproducible environments, experiment tracking, and internal tooling that keeps research iteration speed high

 - Improve infrastructure reliability through monitoring, observability, infrastructure as code, and automation. Reduce operational toil and make complex systems easier to manage.

 - Help guide compute spending decisions. You understand cost per FLOP across providers and hardware, and you hate wasted compute

Tech stack: Slurm, SkyPilot, GCP (+ AWS and Azure to come), Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Python, uv, wandb

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 3+ years building and operating production infrastructure at scale, ideally involving compute clusters, distributed training systems, or HPC

 - Hands-on experience with cluster management and workload orchestration systems such as Slurm, Kubernetes, or similar technologies. You've debugged scheduling failures and operated infrastructure where downtime has real cost

 - Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and reliable build and deployment workflows

 - Strong systems engineering fundamentals: Linux, networking, storage, and distributed systems. You're comfortable debugging complex infrastructure problems across the stack.

 - Strong Python skills and enough familiarity with training to profile a run and tell whether the bottleneck is data loading, communication, or compute

 - Track record of making infrastructure decisions that measurably improved reliability, developer productivity, or cost efficiency

 - Strong AI tooling skills. You use Claude Code, Cursor, or similar fluently to move fast without sacrificing quality

Bonus:

 - Familiarity with GPU infrastructure, PyTorch, GPU profiling, and distributed training

 - Experience operating at tens-of-millions-scale compute spend

 - Multi-cloud or hybrid HPC/cloud infrastructure experience

 - Experience scaling from single cluster to multi-cluster orchestration

 - Background building experiment tracking, model registries, or ML pipeline tooling
