items.title: Research Engineer
items.card: You will be at the forefront of applying cutting-edge AI, advanced agentic workflow and static analysis techniques to complex source code. Your work will directly shape our core products—ensuring both AI-generated and developer-written code meets rigorous enterprise quality and security standards. If you are driven to turn state-of-the-art research into practical, high-impact solutions, this is the role for you.
items.desc:
Who is Sonar?
Sonar enables organizations to ship agentic code with confidence. Code creation is abundant, but confidence is scarce. Our core platform, SonarQube, verifies over 750 billion lines of code every day, delivering agentic verification and governance for all code. Trusted by more than 7 million developers and 75% of the Fortune 100, including teams at Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company, Sonar enables organizations to reduce outages, improve security, and lower the cost and risk of agentic software development.

Founded in Geneva and now headquartered in Austin, Texas, Sonar has a global team working across offices and hubs, including Silicon Valley, London, Bochum, Barcelona, Singapore, Tokyo, and the Washington, D.C. area. At Sonar, we’re enabling enterprises to build agentic software factories that can move quickly while maintaining the control, consistency and evidence required to ship with confidence. 


Position description
At Sonar, we are seeking an innovative Research Engineer to join our Data & Agentic team and pioneer the next generation of our code analysis and verification engines. You will be at the forefront of applying cutting-edge AI, advanced agentic workflow and static analysis techniques to complex source code. Your work will directly shape our core products—ensuring both AI-generated and developer-written code meets rigorous enterprise quality and security standards. If you are driven to turn state-of-the-art research into practical, high-impact solutions, this is the role for you.


 

What you will do:
Create & Innovate: Actively participate in the conceptualization phase. Brainstorm novel ways to improve our products and provide immediate, practical feedback to steer exploratory research toward paths that are both impactful and engineering-feasible.
 Develop Agentic Workflows : Design, prototype, and validate intelligent agentic systems and automated workflows that facilitate writing clean code, identifying root causes of system issues, and remediating complex bugs and vulnerabilities.
 Develop Pragmatic Prototypes: Build hands-on prototypes that prove the viability and scalability of research concepts. Proactively identify engineering bottlenecks or scalability limits and propose effective mitigations early in the research phase.
 Evaluate & Benchmark: Drive the rigorous evaluation of new product features. Construct high-quality datasets, define relevant success metrics, and implement comprehensive benchmarks leveraging Sonar’s existing IP alongside third-party and open-source AI tools.
 Engineer Data Pipelines : Build and manage robust data pipelines to gather, process, and version massive code-centric datasets required for training and evaluating specialized models at scale.
 Translate Prototypes to Products : Collaborate closely with engineering and product teams to integrate successful prototypes into Sonar's cutting-edge products, ensuring they meet the needs of our global user base.
 Communicate and Evangelize : Clearly articulate and document complex technical concepts and research findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Experience and qualifications:
Must have:
 Advanced academic background in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related quantitative field.
 Strong software engineering experience (minimum 2+ years in industry) with proficiency in Python and major modern programming languages.
 Practical experience with modern agentic frameworks, software automation tools, and LLM architectures.
 Experience of driving research projects from initial ideation to a demonstrable prototype with a high degree of autonomy.
 Hands-on experience integrating third-party tools, program analysis frameworks, or open-source libraries into functional prototypes.
 Proven experience in data handling: constructing high-quality datasets, defining objective success metrics, and building robust benchmarks for new solutions.
 The ability to fast context-switch and maintain momentum across multiple concurrent, fast-moving research topics.
 Excellent communication skills in English, with a talent for translating complex research findings into clear, actionable artifacts for product engineering squads.
 Plus:
 Background in static analysis: abstract syntax trees (ASTs), code security, bug detection, etc..
 Familiarity with LLM techniques such as model fine-tuning, semantic search engines, etc.
 Experience with large-scale data processing frameworks and cloud infrastructure (e.g. AWS).
Additional comments
 This role is based in Geneva. We are unable to consider candidates unwilling to be in Geneva, but we are willing to relocate the right candidate.


In-office culture
We're intentional about this. We believe the best teams are built in the room together. Three anchor days — Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays — create the collaboration rhythm that makes a hub office worth having.

items.card: What you'll do: : LLM–data interfaces: Research and design how LLMs access and reason over TomTom's data. This covers retrieval strategies for structured and geospatial data, tool and API designs that LLMs can use reliably, text-to-query approaches, and grounding techniques. items.desc:
TomTom is a global leader in navigation, mapping, and traffic information. Join our dynamic team and vibrant culture to contribute to shaping the future of location technology.

We are looking for an Applied Scientist to shape how AI understands and uses TomTom's location data. You'll develop machine learning models and design the systems that let LLMs reason accurately over maps, traffic, points of interest and routing. You'll turn open-ended product questions into well-defined scientific problems, validate solutions with rigorous evaluation, and work with AI and software engineers to bring them to production.

What you'll do: :
LLM–data interfaces: Research and design how LLMs access and reason over TomTom's data. This covers retrieval strategies for structured and geospatial data, tool and API designs that LLMs can use reliably, text-to-query approaches, and grounding techniques. 
 Data representation: Develop representations that make location data usable by AI, such as embeddings for geospatial entities, knowledge graphs and structured context formats. 
 Evaluation science: Define how we measure whether LLM-powered systems are right. Build benchmarks, factuality and hallucination metrics, and evaluation datasets for location-grounded tasks, and work with engineers to automate them. 
 Model research and development: Design, train and fine-tune ML and deep learning models, including LLMs, computer vision, time-series and graph-based methods, using large-scale, multi-modal data. 
 Problem framing: Work with product managers and stakeholders to identify high-impact opportunities and turn them into well-defined scientific problems with clear success metrics. 
 Research to production: Write production-quality code and work with AI and software engineers to take solutions from prototype to production, balancing accuracy, latency, cost and scalability. 
 State of the art: Keep up with the latest research in LLMs, retrieval and agentic systems, and adapt promising techniques to TomTom's problems. 
 Knowledge sharing: Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, and help build a strong scientific culture. External publications and patents are encouraged.
What you'll need::
Bachelor’s, Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics or a related quantitative field, or equivalent professional experience. 
 Strong foundations in machine learning, deep learning, statistics and optimization. 
 Hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX, and with the Python scientific stack (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn). 
 Experience with one or more of: LLMs and generative AI, computer vision, time-series forecasting, graph neural networks, or reinforcement learning. 
 Experience in Search-related problems, such as information retrieval, ranking, relevance, or search algorithms, is a strong plus. 
 Proven ability to design experiments, define meaningful metrics and draw sound conclusions from data. 
 Experience working with large-scale datasets and distributed computing (e.g., Spark, Databricks, or cloud ML platforms on Azure, AWS or GCP). 
 Ability to write clean, maintainable code and to work with engineers toward production deployment. 
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical ideas to diverse audiences. 
 A track record of publications at top-tier venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, KDD) is a plus. 
 Experience with geospatial, mapping, mobility or sensor data is a plus, but not required.
What we offer 

A competitive compensation package, of course.  

Time and resources to grow and develop, including a personal development budget and paid leave for learning days, as well as paid access to e-learning resources such as O’Reilly and LinkedIn Learning. 

Time to support life outside of work, with enhanced parental leave plus paid leave to care for loved ones and volunteer in local communities.  

Work flexibility, where TomTom’ers, in agreement with their manager and team, use both the office and home to focus, collaborate, learn and socialize. It’s all about getting the best out of both worlds – we ask TomTom’ers to come to the office two days a week, and the remaining three are free to be worked in either location.

Improve your home office with a setup budget and get extra support with a monthly allowance. 

Enjoy options to work from your home country and abroad for a set number of days each year, to visit family and friends, or to simply explore the world we’re mapping.  

Take the holidays you want with a competitive holiday plan, plus an extra day off to celebrate your birthday. 

Join annual events like our  Hackathon and DevDays to bring your ideas to life with talented teammates from around the world. 

Become a part of our inclusive global culture and have the chance to collaborate with a diverse community – we have over 80 nationalities at TomTom!

items.desc: The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: "Taking the pulse of our Earth to safeguard a habitable planet." For the EU-funded project UPLIFT in section 4.3 Geoenergy (department 'Geosystems'), we are looking for a: Research scientist (f_m_x) – Geothermal Reservoir Stimulation Reference Number 11660 UPLIFT brings together key European Enhanced Geothermal System (EGS) industry and research institutions to demonstrate, at Czechia's leading energy research site RINGEN, how water-only multi-stage hydraulic shear stimulation treatments can be efficiently implemented in metamorphic basement rocks in Europe, while reducing technical, social, and environmental risks. A central focus is the development and application of adaptive stimulation designs that use real-time seismic and hydraulic data to improve treatment efficiency and safety. The project will also investigate micro-turbine drilling as an alternative to conventional perforation techniques to improve reservoir access. Laboratory experiments will assess the self-propping behaviour of European basement rocks and benchmark their stimulation response against acid- and proppant-based methods. Water-only and proppant-based stimulation treatments will also be compared at the Bedretto Underground Laboratory. In parallel, the project will develop high-fidelity, physics-based digital twins to guide stimulation design, alongside fast surrogate models to support real-time operational decision-making. The stimulation activities are supported by high-resolution, real-time seismic monitoring, conventional and adaptive traffic light systems, and social science research. As a postdoctoral researcher, you will play a central role in planning, supervising and analysing the adaptive multi-stage hydraulic stimulation treatments at the RINGEN EGS site in Litoměřice, Czechia. This position offers the opportunity to connect advanced research with field operations and contribute directly to developing efficient, safe geothermal stimulation technologies. Your responsibilities: Co-lead the hydraulic stimulation and well test activities at the Litoměřice EGS site Analyse stimulation and well test data to compare and understand the hydraulic and seismic response of metamorphic basement rock to different stimulation methods and injection protocols, including adaptive injection strategies Contribute to detailed operational planning and the preparation of tender documents Contribute to the techno-economic assessment of different stimulation methods and their implications for EGS development Publish your findings in peer-reviewed journals and NPUs, Hailo, Intel, AMD, Qualcomm) und hilfst uns damit, unsere Zielhardware für unsere Computer-Vision-Produkte auf Edge-Geräten zu finden. Inferenz-Optimierung: Du holst über Runtimes (z. B. ONNX, OpenVINO), Modelloptimierung (z. B. Quantisierung) und Hersteller-SDKs maximale Effizienz aus der Zielhardware. Inference-Services & Deployment: Du entwickelst schlanke Services inklusive Pre- und Post-Processing und bringst sie sauber containerisiert (Docker, Kubernetes) auf unseren Linux-Edge-Servern zum Laufen. Vom Prototyp in den Rollout: Du setzt die ausgewählte Zielarchitektur zunächst prototypisch um und treibst diese anschließend bis in den flächendeckenden Rollout in tausenden Filialen. Weiterentwicklung & Skalierung: Du wirst unser Treiber für effiziente und wirtschaftliche Inferenz auf Edge-Geräten, und sorgst dafür, dass wir diese fest in unseren aktuellen und zukünftigen Produkten verankern. Dein Profil Ausbildung: Du hast ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes technisches Studium und arbeitest seit mindestens 3 Jahren im professionellen Umfeld an Computer-Vision-Produkten. Fokus auf Inferenz & Edge-Hardware: Du hast praktische Erfahrung damit, Computer-Vision- oder vergleichbare AI-Modelle auf unterschiedlicher Hardware (idealerweise auch abseits klassischer GPUs) performant zum Laufen zu bringen, und kennst dich mit Inferenz-Runtimes wie z. B. ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO oder TensorRT aus. Computer-Vision-Verständnis: Du verstehst, wie typische Computer-Vision-Pipelines (z. B. Object Detection, Tracking oder Videostream-Verarbeitung) funktionieren und wie man diese effizient betreibt. Sauberer Code bis zur Produktion: Du weißt, worauf es bei produktionsreifem Code ankommt, und schreibst diesen in Python und idealerweise C++ oder Rust. Hardware-Neugier & Benchmarking-Expertise: Du hast Lust, neue Chip-Architekturen auszuprobieren, und bist gut darin, praxisnahe Benchmarks für unsere Computer-Vision-Modelle aufzubauen. Pragmatismus & Selbstständigkeit: Du magst es, wenn noch nicht alles in Stein gemeißelt ist, und nutzt die daraus resultierenden Freiräume proaktiv, um deine Themen voranzutreiben. Dabei weißt du genau, wann schnelle Prototypen gefragt sind und wann es auf produktionsreife Lösungen ankommt. Sprachkenntnisse: Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch. Dein Ansprechpartner Charoula Kostakopoulou Recruiterin E-Mail:recruiting@mail.schwarz

items.desc: Entra nel nostro mondo. Trasforma insieme a noi. Junior Data Scientist Quale sarà la tua sfida? Bip ha creato all’interno del proprio Competence Centre “xTech” il più nutrito gruppo di Data Scientist in Italia (fonte: statistiche LinkedIn), e dall’Italia coordina anche i propri gruppi di Data Scientist locali presso le proprie sedi estere. Il/La Data Scientist in Bip evolve non solo le proprie competenze di AI e Machine Learning, ma anche la comprensione dei fenomeni legati al Business dei nostri Clienti e le proprie capacità di tradurli in algoritmi e poi di comunicare e utilizzare i risultati degli stessi per migliorare ed efficientare i processi. I/Le nostri/e Data Scientist verranno introdotti in contesti progettuali dove comprenderanno le esigenze del Cliente, daranno indicazione ai Data Engineer sulla preparazione desiderata dei dati, sceglieranno o costruiranno i migliori mix di modelli più adatti al caso specifico, discuteranno gli output con il cliente e consegneranno il modello per l’ottimizzazione e passaggio in produzione finale ai Data Engineer. In contesti più semplificati in cui la componente di Data Engineering è meno elaborata, i nostri Data Scientist procederanno in autonomia anche nella data preparation e nel porting in produzione dei modelli ingegnerizzati. Oltre alle progettualità, ai/alle Data Scientist sarà richiesto un contributo attivo per alimentare la Community con attività di ricerca, scouting, concept di nuove soluzioni e business development. Sarai tu ad entrare nel nostro team? Requisiti Indispensabili: Da 0 a 3 anni di esperienza nel ruolo Laurea Specialistica in Ingegneria Informatica, Ingegneria Matematica, Informatica, Statistica o discipline affini (STEM); Forte approccio quantitativo e brillanti doti analitiche; Passione e competenza in ambito data exploration, analisi dati e creazione di modelli: il nostro team disegna e sviluppa sistemi a supporto di decisioni strategiche per il business; Competenze statistiche, di Data Mining, Machine Learning; Conoscenza di programmazione e scripting con Python Conoscenza di tematiche di Deep Learning, NLP e analisi dati non strutturati Conoscenza di strumenti di version control (es. Git); Comprensione di tecnologie legate ai Big Data come Hadoop, MapReduce, Spark Conoscenza approfondita di database relazionali e di costrutti SQL e SQL Programming; Conoscenza di database non relazionali Indispensabile la conoscenza fluente di italiano e inglese professionali Plus: Conoscenza dei linguaggi PySpark o Scala Esperienza di lavoro su piattaforma Databricks Esperienza nello sviluppo di applicazioni di Gen AI Conoscenza e l’utilizzo di API Cloud di Intelligenza Artificiale dei principali cloud provider (Google, Microsoft, AWS, IBM) e di altri strumenti di Advanced Analytics di Vendor specializzati Conoscenza di tecniche di semi-supervised e self-supervised learning. Esperienza con framework di lavoro AGILE (esempio: Scrum, Kanban) Soft Skills: Standing consulenziale Spiccate doti comunicative e interpersonali Orientamento al cliente e al raggiungimento degli obiettivi Adattabilità e flessibilità Precisione e stress tolerance nel rispetto delle scadenze Ottime capacità di gestione di progettualità complesse Disponibilità per trasferte in Italia e all’estero. Crescita e Formazione Più di 300 corsi su tecnologie e business emergenti, programmi di sviluppo personalizzati e iniziative di training e people care per supportare la tua crescita professionale e personale. Inclusione e Valori Promuoviamo l’unicità e garantiamo pari opportunità a tutte le persone. Lavoriamo per un ambiente etico, equo e accogliente, anche attraverso politiche attive per le categorie protette (L. 68/99). items.desc: Brief Info About Vinted Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission: Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life. Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces. Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members. Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. Information About The Position You’ll join the Detection subdomain within Trust & Safety, whose mission is to protect the Vinted community by identifying harmful content and activities. We build detection capabilities that enable timely prevention and moderation, reducing members’ exposure to harm, while minimising disruption to legitimate members. You’ll develop and improve machine learning models that identify harmful listings and suspicious behaviour across the marketplace, while minimising friction on legitimate members. Working with text, images and behavioural data, you’ll apply practical machine learning techniques to evolving detection challenges. You’ll work closely with Data Scientists, Decision Scientists, Product Managers and engineers to turn ideas into reliable production solutions. You’ll take ownership of well-defined projects across the ML lifecycle, from understanding the data and developing models to deployment, evaluation and ongoing maintenance. In this position, you’ll Develop, evaluate and improve machine learning models that detect harmful content and behaviour at scale. Engineer features, prepare training and evaluation datasets, understanding their limitations and addressing issues such as noisy labels, class imbalance and data leakage. Collaborate with engineers to integrate models into production and develop reliable training and inference pipelines using established tooling. Work with Decision Scientists and Product Managers to define success metrics and evaluate model improvements through offline analysis and online experimentation, balancing detection coverage with false positives and member experience. Monitor deployed models, investigate changes in their effectiveness and improve them as harmful behaviour and underlying data evolve. Write reliable, maintainable and reproducible code, document your work, share learnings and contribute ideas to the team’s roadmap. About You Practical experience developing machine learning solutions, with a solid foundation in machine learning, statistics and probability theory. Proficiency in Python and SQL, and experience with ML libraries such as scikit-learn or PyTorch. Hands-on experience preparing training datasets, engineering features, training models and evaluating them against baselines and metrics. Experience applying machine learning to at least one of the following: tabular or behavioural data, natural language processing, or computer vision. Familiarity with the production ML lifecycle, including deployment, monitoring and retraining. Ability to break down problems into manageable steps, work independently within an agreed scope and seek input when needed. Ability to communicate your approach, findings and trade-offs clearly, collaborate with technical and non-technical colleagues, and learn from feedback. Motivation to apply machine learning to member safety, with care for data privacy and the consequences of incorrect predictions. Nice to have Experience with fraud detection, content classification or other Trust & Safety applications. Experience with transformers, multimodal models or LLM-based workflows Work perks The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme 25 working days of holiday Access to all the tools & tech needed for work Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture Private health insurance Pension plan with flexible contribution options and a matching contribution from Vinted Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you …

items.desc: Description We're building the UK's next generation engineering powerhouse, providing critical technology that strengthens national security and resilience. We specialise in turning advances in sensing, AI, and communications into operational capability for the edge, where connectivity may be degraded or denied. Our work focuses on accelerating the deployment of technology, improving decision-making for frontline teams, and protecting people and critical assets in demanding environments. Headquartered in Bristol, Rowden employs over 200 people and operates over 20,000 square feet of engineering and manufacturing facilities. Recognised in the Financial Times FT1000 as one of Europe's fastest-growing engineering businesses, there has never been a better time to join. Engineering Graduates at Rowden This is not a traditional graduate scheme built around a narrow role or a long, segmented programme. The Applied Graduate Programme is designed for engineers who want broad systems and product exposure, with real responsibility early and close engagement with end users and operational constraints. Engineering graduates work on deployable systems supporting defence, emergency services, and national security organisations, alongside engineers from multiple disciplines. You will join a rotational engineering programme designed to build technical breadth fast, supported by experienced mentors, structured feedback, and clear milestones. From the outset, you will be trusted with meaningful work and increasing ownership as your capability develops. If you want to understand more about how we design and build systems at Rowden, it’s worth reading this blog from one of our Senior Principal Engineers. What You'll Work On As a Graduate Engineer at Rowden, the types of work you’ll be involved with include: Integrating sensor and data feeds into geospatial and situational awareness applications, working across software, systems, and interfaces. Designing and testing system behaviour under degraded communications, including store-and-forward, prioritisation, and security controls. Deploying and evaluating machine learning models for edge use cases such as computer vision or signal processing, with a focus on measurable performance and operational constraints. Building future variants of deployable sensing and communications products, influencing how those systems evolve through hands-on engineering, integration work, and performance data. Shipping software that enables edge devices to be deployed, configured, and sustained at scale. How The Graduate Programme Works You will complete several rotations before specialising within one of Rowden’s core engineering disciplines. The exact path isn’t rigid, we’ll shape it around your strengths, interests, and the needs of the business. Possible Rotations Include Software Engineering: mobile applications, geospatial tools, systems integration, and test evidence. Machine Learning Engineering: deployable models for edge CV and SIGINT, with measurable performance. Systems Engineering: user need through requirements, architecture, integration, verification, and fielding. Safety Engineering: hazard analysis, mitigations, and safety evidence to support delivery. Radio Frequency Engineering: spectrum monitoring and insight to improve operational awareness. Infrastructure Engineering / DevOps: cloud platforms, portable on-prem systems, automation, and reliability. Key Skills, Experience And Behaviours What we’re looking for A STEM degree or equivalent experience, with strong fundamentals in areas such as Engineering, Computer Science, Maths, Physics, Electronics, Data Science, or Cyber Security. Curiosity and learning agility, with the ability to pick up new concepts and apply them quickly. A collaborative mindset, with the confidence to take ownership where needed. Evidence of problem solving through projects, labs, hackathons, societies, or work experience. Eligibility Candidates must be eligible for SC Clearance. Recruitment process Our recruitment process is short, practical, and focused on how you think and work. Short tech test: A time-bound task designed to see how you approach a representative engineering challenge. Alignment call: A chat with someone from our Talent team or the hiring manager to explore cultural alignment, values, and what you’re looking for from your first role. Assessment day (to be held in February 2027): Spend time at Rowden, see our facilities, learn more about what we build and get hands-on with an engineering challenge. Designed to focus on reasoning, communication, and collaboration. Applications are open now for a September 2027 start. As part of your application, you will be asked to indicate two preferred focus (i.e. technical) areas so that we can shape your initial rotations. Working at Rowden We are committed to building a flexible, inclusive, and enabling company. Our aim is to create a diverse team of talented people with unique skills, experience, and …

items.desc: Location: London, UK (On-site) Company: Odysse Ltd Employment Type: Full-time Salary: £50,000 - £60,000 per annum, depending on relevant experience About Odysse Odysse is building the AI-powered fleet intelligence and orchestration layer for the future of electric and autonomous mobility. Operating a fully licensed zero-emission fleet in London, we combine real-world mobility operations with proprietary AI technology to make urban transportation more efficient, intelligent and sustainable. Our platform, OdySys, uses machine learning, operational data and external signals to optimise fleet utilisation, reduce inefficiencies and improve commercial performance. Our ambition extends beyond today's mobility operations. We are developing intelligent systems capable of supporting thousands of vehicles across cities, enabling the transition from human-driven electric fleets to large-scale autonomous mobility networks. As part of this vision, we are investing in advanced simulation and AI capabilities to model, test and optimise how fleets operate in complex urban environments. About the role We are looking for a hands-on and ambitious Data Scientist - AI & Simulation to help design and build our next-generation urban mobility simulation platform. You will work with real-world operational data to develop simulation environments, model fleet behaviour, evaluate operational strategies and generate synthetic data to improve our machine learning systems. The role combines simulation development, machine learning, optimisation and cloud computing , with opportunities to explore emerging approaches in reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems. This is not a traditional reporting-focused data science role. You will be building technology from the ground up, experimenting with intelligent decision-making systems and contributing directly to the future of electric and autonomous mobility. Key responsibilities Simulation Development: Design and validate Python-based simulations of fleet movements, demand, charging and urban mobility operations. Machine Learning & AI: Develop ML models, generate synthetic data and explore intelligent optimisation techniques. Scenario Modelling: Simulate different cities, fleet configurations and operational strategies to evaluate performance. Cloud & Data Infrastructure: Build scalable simulation workflows using cloud computing and data pipelines. Experimentation & Innovation: Validate simulations against real-world data, evaluate outcomes and improve AI-driven decision-making. Skills and experience Demonstrable hands-on experience building and validating simulation systems (essential) , using frameworks such as SimPy, SUMO, Mesa or equivalent. Strong Python skills, including NumPy, Pandas and scientific computing libraries. Solid understanding of machine learning, statistical modelling and optimisation. Proficiency in SQL, large-scale data processing and cloud-based workflows. Knowledge of reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems, synthetic data or geospatial analytics is an advantage. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively. Why join Odysse? At Odysse, you'll have the opportunity to build cutting-edge AI and simulation technology from the ground up, working with real-world operational data to solve complex mobility challenges. You'll gain exposure to intelligent optimisation, simulation and emerging AI technologies while contributing to our vision of transforming urban mobility across cities and autonomous transportation networks. As part of a growing technology team, you'll have the freedom to innovate, take ownership of meaningful technical challenges and see your work directly influence real-world operations and future technology development. Imagine a future where entire urban mobility networks can be simulated, tested and optimised before decisions are made in the real world. At Odysse, we're building towards that future - and we're looking for people who want to help create it.

We are building an AI-powered platform that turns match and training footage into individual performance insights, technical assessments, and actionable feedback for athletes and coaches. We are starting with rugby and expanding the technology to other sports. items.card: Imaginez, transformez et impactez le monde positivement : venez vivre au cœur du changement en tant que Responsible AI Engineer . Vos principales responsabilités seront les suivantes : Développer et implémenter des modèles et solutions AI en intégrant les principes de Responsible AI. items.desc: Imaginez, transformez et impactez le monde positivement : venez vivre au cœur du changement en tant que Responsible AI Engineer . Vos principales responsabilités seront les suivantes : Développer et implémenter des modèles et solutions AI en intégrant les principes de Responsible AI. Identifier et évaluer les risques liés aux modèles : bias, fairness, robustness, explainability, puis mettre en œuvre les mesures de mitigation adaptées. Optimiser et maintenir les systèmes AI existants afin d’améliorer leurs performances et leur conformité aux exigences Responsible AI. Intervenir sur l’ensemble du cycle de développement AI : préparation des données, conception, développement, tests, déploiement et support. Identifier et corriger les biais dans les datasets et les modèles. Contribuer aux guidelines, best practices et formations techniques internes en Responsible AI. Assurer la traçabilité/documentation des choix techniques, décisions et méthodologies utilisées. Participer aux échanges clients, avant-ventes et propositions commerciales. Maintenir une veille sur les nouvelles technologies AI et les problématiques éthiques associées. Des déplacements sont à prévoir en fonction des besoins projets/clients. Vous construisez une carrière agile, grâce à la formation, aux certifications et aux feedbacks reçus pour chacune de vos réalisations. Nos équipes apprennent chaque jour avec les meilleurs experts en France et à l’international. Vous évoluez dans un environnement de travail flexible qui vise à favoriser l’équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle : le télétravail donne la possibilité d’adapter son rythme professionnel en fonction des actualités de l’équipe et du projet. Nous vous proposons de vivre l’expérience du changement auprès de nos équipes, rejoignez Accenture. Le métier de Responsible AI Engineer est fait pour vous si : Bac+3/5 en informatique, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science ou domaine technique proche. Expérience en développement et déploiement de modèles Machine Learning / solutions AI. Maîtrise d’au moins 2 domaines ML/Data Science parmi : statistiques & probabilités, régression, clustering, Deep Learning / Neural Networks, NLP / Text Mining, Computer Vision / Image Recognition, Time Series Forecasting, Tree Ensembles, outils de visualisation ML. Programmation : forte maîtrise de Python, éventuellement R ou Java. Frameworks ML: TensorFlow, PyTorch. Expérience Big Data, notamment Spark ou Hadoop. Bases de données, data processing et data preprocessing. Connaissance des environnements Cloud Azure, AWS ou Google Cloud, en particulier leurs services AI/ML. Capacité à manipuler et analyser des datasets complexes. Vous tirerez votre épingle du jeu si : Formation complémentaire en Responsible AI / AI Ethics Certification AI, ML ou Data Science. Expérience sur des projets AI for Social Good / Ethical AI. Outils de visualisation spécialisés comme D3.js ou ggplot. Expérience en Project Management. Un bon niveau d’anglais. A propos de nous : Accenture, c'est une communauté de plus de 730 000 talents et une mission commune : réaliser la promesse technologique alliée à l’ingéniosité humaine. Dans un monde en perpétuel changement, nous accélérons la transformation des plus grandes entreprises, de la stratégie à la réalisation des projets, à l’aide des technologies de demain et dynamisons leur croissance grâce à l'expertise multi-sectorielle de nos experts. Nos recrutements sont fondés sur les compétences, sans distinction d’origine, d’âge, ou de genre et tous nos postes sont ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap.

items.title: IT-Mitarbeiter*in (m/w/d) für High Performance Computing und Künstliche Intelligenz im Verbundvorhaben „Lower Saxony Digital Science Support Space (DS3)"
items.card: Aufgaben: Projektmanagement und lokale Koordination des Verbundvorhabens DS³ am Standort LUIS sowie die Zusammenarbeit mit den beteiligten Partnerinstitutionen in Niedersachsen Aufbau, Konfiguration, Administration und Wartung des Tier-3-HPC-Clusters des LUIS sowie der dazugehörigen Storage-, GPU-beschleunigten Hardware- und Monitoring-Systeme Technische Unterstützung und Beratung von Nutzern und Forschenden bei der
items.desc: Die Leibniz Universität Hannover bietet exzellente Arbeitsbedingungen in einem lebendigen wissenschaftlichen Umfeld, eingebettet in die hervorragenden Lebensbedingungen einer modernen Großstadt im Grünen. In der zentralen Einrichtung Leibniz Universität IT Services (LUIS) sind mehrere Stellen zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt zu besetzen: IT-Mitarbeiter*in (m/w/d) für High Performance Computing und Künstliche Intelligenz im Verbundvorhaben „Lower Saxony Digital Science Support Space (DS3)“ (EntgGr.13 TV-L, 100 %) Die Stellen sind bis zum 30.06.2030 befristet. Die Abteilung Compute- und Speichersysteme der Leibniz Universität IT Services bietet im Rahmen des Dienstes Scientific Computing einen zentralen High-Performance Computing (HPC)-Rechencluster an. Ihre Stelle im Überblick Zur Unterstützung des neu aufzubauenden Verbundvorhabens „Lower Saxony Digital Science Support Space (DS³)“ im Rahmen der Hochschule.digital Niedersachsen suchen wir zwei engagierte Mitarbeiterinnen oder Mitarbeiter mit nachgewiesenem Interesse an den Bereichen High-Performance Computing (HPC), Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) und dem Betrieb der hierfür erforderlichen Infrastruktur und Services. Ziel des vom Land Niedersachsen geförderten Kooperationsprojekts DS³ ist der flächendeckende Ausbau von forschungsnahen IT-Infrastrukturen und Dienstleistungen an niedersächsischen Hochschulen. Als einer der tragenden Standorte wird das LUIS im Rahmen des Projekts eine Tier-3-HPC-Infrastruktur bereitstellen, betreiben und die Forschenden bei deren Nutzung unterstützen. Sie arbeiten in einem Team aus erfahrenen Beschäftigten sowohl eigenständig als auch gemeinsam schwerpunktmäßig an folgenden Aufgaben: Projektmanagement und lokale Koordination des Verbundvorhabens DS³ am Standort LUIS sowie die Zusammenarbeit mit den beteiligten Partnerinstitutionen in Niedersachsen Aufbau, Konfiguration, Administration und Wartung des Tier-3-HPC-Clusters des LUIS sowie der dazugehörigen Storage-, GPU-beschleunigten Hardware- und Monitoring-Systeme Technische Unterstützung und Beratung von Nutzern und Forschenden bei der effizienten Nutzung der HPC-Ressourcen, dem Deployment von KI-Werkzeugen und Large Language Models (LLMs), dem Performance Engineering sowie bei der Skalierung von HPC-Rechenprozessen und Machine Learning-Workloads Mitarbeit beim Aufbau und der Etablierung nachhaltiger Services im Bereich der forschungsnahen IT-Infrastruktur für datenintensive HPC- und KI-Anwendungen innerhalb des DS³-Netzwerks Erstellung von Dokumentationsmaterial für verschiedene Zielgruppen sowie die Vertretung des LUIS-Teilprojekts in projektinternen Arbeitsgruppen Wen suchen wir? Voraussetzung für die Einstellung ist ein abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium, vorzugsweise in einem MINT-Studiengang (oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation) mit einschlägiger Berufserfahrung im HPC- oder KI-Umfeld. Erfahrung im Linux-basierten Einsatz von Cluster-Technologien wie Workload-Managementsystemen (z. B. Slurm) sowie verteilten Dateisystemen (z. B. Gute Kenntnisse in den Skriptsprachen Python und Bash zur Automatisierung sowie Vertrautheit mit modernen Monitoring-Lösungen für Cluster-Systeme (z. B. Prometheus und Grafana) und die Bereitschaft zur Erstellung präziser technischer Dokumentationen werden vorausgesetzt. Kenntnisse in höheren Programmiersprachen, idealerweise C++, C oder Fortran, sind hierbei erwünscht. Sie haben Kenntnisse zu Containertechnologien (z. B. Apptainer/Singularity) zur Bereitstellung portabler KI- und HPC-Anwendungen. Idealerweise bringen Sie zudem Erfahrungen mit Virtualisierungsplattformen (z. B. KVM, oVirt, OpenStack) mit. Erfahrung im Umgang mit Konfigurations- und Management-Werkzeugen (z. B. Kickstart/PXE, EasyBuild, Pacemaker/Corosync, Puppet/Ansible) wird erwartet. Praktische Erfahrung mit KI-Systemen, dem Deployment von Large Language Models auf GPU-beschleunigter Hardware sowie Kenntnisse in der Versionsverwaltung Git sind hierbei von Vorteil. Regelmäßige Fortbildungen helfen Ihnen, Ihre persönlichen Kompetenzen gezielt weiterzuentwickeln. Sie sind eine aufgeschlossene Person mit guten kommunikativen Fähigkeiten, handeln lösungs- und zielorientiert und bringen eine hohe Selbstorganisation, Belastbarkeit sowie Teamfähigkeit mit. Sehr gute Englisch- und gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift werden vorausgesetzt, um unsere internationalen Nutzerinnen und Nutzer optimal zu betreuen. items.desc: Deine Aufgaben Hardware-Evaluation: Du testest alternative KI-Beschleuniger abseits von NVIDIA-GPUs (z. B. NPUs, Hailo, Intel, AMD, Qualcomm) und hilfst uns damit, unsere Zielhardware für unsere Computer-Vision-Produkte auf Edge-Geräten zu finden. Inferenz-Optimierung: Du holst über Runtimes (z. B. ONNX, OpenVINO), Modelloptimierung (z. B. Quantisierung) und Hersteller-SDKs maximale Effizienz aus der Zielhardware. Inference-Services & Deployment: Du entwickelst schlanke Services inklusive Pre- und Post-Processing und bringst sie sauber containerisiert (Docker, Kubernetes) auf unseren Linux-Edge-Servern zum Laufen. Vom Prototyp in den Rollout: Du setzt die ausgewählte Zielarchitektur zunächst prototypisch um und treibst diese anschließend bis in den flächendeckenden Rollout in tausenden Filialen. Weiterentwicklung & Skalierung: Du wirst unser Treiber für effiziente und wirtschaftliche Inferenz auf Edge-Geräten, und sorgst dafür, dass wir diese fest in unseren aktuellen und zukünftigen Produkten verankern. Dein Profil Ausbildung: Du hast ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes technisches Studium und arbeitest seit mindestens 3 Jahren im professionellen Umfeld an Computer-Vision-Produkten. Fokus auf Inferenz & Edge-Hardware: Du hast praktische Erfahrung damit, Computer-Vision- oder vergleichbare AI-Modelle auf unterschiedlicher Hardware (idealerweise auch abseits klassischer GPUs) performant zum Laufen zu bringen, und kennst dich mit Inferenz-Runtimes wie z. B. ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO oder TensorRT aus. Computer-Vision-Verständnis: Du verstehst, wie typische Computer-Vision-Pipelines (z. B. Object Detection, Tracking oder Videostream-Verarbeitung) funktionieren und wie man diese effizient betreibt. Sauberer Code bis zur Produktion: Du weißt, worauf es bei produktionsreifem Code ankommt, und schreibst diesen in Python und idealerweise C++ oder Rust. Hardware-Neugier & Benchmarking-Expertise: Du hast Lust, neue Chip-Architekturen auszuprobieren, und bist gut darin, praxisnahe Benchmarks für unsere Computer-Vision-Modelle aufzubauen. Pragmatismus & Selbstständigkeit: Du magst es, wenn noch nicht alles in Stein gemeißelt ist, und nutzt die daraus resultierenden Freiräume proaktiv, um deine Themen voranzutreiben. Dabei weißt du genau, wann schnelle Prototypen gefragt sind und wann es auf produktionsreife Lösungen ankommt. Sprachkenntnisse: Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch.

OUR STORY 
 At STMicroelectronics, we believe in the power of technology to drive innovation and make a positive impact on people, businesses, and society. As a global semiconductor company, our advanced technologies and chips form the hidden foundation of the world we live in today. 
 When you join ST, you will be part of a global business with more than 115 nationalities, present in 40 countries, and comprising over 50,000 diverse and dedicated creators and makers of technology around the world. 
 Developing technologies takes more than talent: it takes amazing people who understand collaboration and respect. People with passion and the desire to disrupt the status quo, drive innovation, and unlock their own potential. 
 Embark on a journey with us, where you can innovate for a future that we want to make smarter and greener, in a responsible and sustainable way. Our technology starts with you. 
 ST is excited to welcome an Embedded Software Development Intern (Audio DSP Platform) for our ST Carmel, IN office. 
 Please note: 
 This is an in-person internship starting in Summer 2027. 
 The current team at our Kokomo, IN office will be moving to our new office located in Carmel, IN - the internship will take place in Carmel, IN . 
 YOUR ROLE 
 Join our Software R&D team to help build an embedded audio algorithm development platform based on an STM32 Nucleo board and a production audio amplifier. The platform will support algorithm development, speaker characterization, and customer demonstrations.
 You will work with software and hardware engineers to bring up the platform, connect it to audio amplifiers and a PC, and develop the software framework and tools needed to test and demonstrate audio features.
 YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Create an embedded SW platform for the development of advanced audio algorithms.
 Develop and test interfaces between the Nucleo (microprocessor) board, audio amplifiers, and PC, including TDM audio input/output, I²C control, and USB and/or Ethernet connectivity.
 Enable audio streaming between the embedded platform and a PC.
 Build a reusable software framework for algorithm development, speaker testing, and customer demonstrations.
 Implement and validate speaker-characterization algorithms using existing examples, including processing current-feedback and voltage-output measurements.
 Support integration and testing with external amplifiers and test equipment.
 Contribute to a clean, self-contained demonstrator, potentially including an interface board to replace temporary wiring.
 YOUR SKILLS & EXPERIENCES 
 Majoring in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Acoustics, or a related field.
 Knowledge of embedded software development and programming in C.
 Familiarity with digital signal processing and audio signals.
 Interest or experience in STM32 microcontrollers and embedded interfaces such as I²C, USB, Ethernet, or digital audio interfaces.
 Familiarity with audio amplifiers or speaker testing is an advantage.
 Strong problem-solving and communication skills.
 At STMicroelectronics, base salary is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range depending on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The base hourly rate range for this role is between $30 and $41 USD.

The selected candidates will become future leaders in research and education in this field, and their research plans are expected to strengthen our research centres Corelab and/or Terra. Examples of AI applications include design, construction management, building services, and real estate decision-making. Research Centre Terra is Finland’s leading expert in infrastructure. Its main areas of focus are geotechnics, earth structures, railway track structures, and the digitalisation of infrastructure, together with the laboratory and measurement services that support them. Examples of AI applications include characterization of ground conditions and estimation of ground properties from multivariant ground investigation data, use of monitoring and surveillance data in condition assessment and predictive maintenance of infrastructures. The duties of the professor will be further specified, and their quantitative ratios confirmed, in the annual workload plan. Do you have the expertise in AI and predictive modelling to help improve how wind turbines operate in icy conditions? If so this role could be ideal. We’re looking for a Research Associate to join OptimICE, an international Horizon Europe project bringing together 14 organisations to reduce the impact of icing on wind energy in cold climates. This 42-month fixed-term role offers the opportunity to contribute to research that improves how wind turbines are monitored, operated and maintained in icy conditions. Working closely with Dr Jonathan Nixon and the Kent research team, you’ll develop and validate physics-informed AI models for icing detection and wind-power prediction, helping wind farm operators anticipate icing, predict power production and make better decisions about ice protection and maintenance. items.desc: Job number ENG04109 Faculties Faculty of Engineering Departments Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - Hybrid Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 3 Jan 2027 About the role End-to-end learning-based constructions are becoming increasingly popular for communication systems, but what do neural networks actually learn when they are trained to communicate: do they rediscover Shannon-theoretic constructions, or something new? The forward process of a diffusion model is a Gaussian channel, so should a diffusion model be viewed as a joint source–channel decoder? When every block of a communication system is learned, is the bit still the right interface? We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to work on these and related questions at the interface between information theory and modern machine learning, as part of a joint NSF–EPSRC project between Imperial College London and Texas A&M University. The aim is to use information theory both as a lens to explain what learned communication systems do and as a guide to designing new ones, from analytically tractable Gaussian models to real data. Potential research directions include, but are not limited to: Generative models meet information theory: diffusion models viewed through Gaussian channels and estimation, generative priors for communication and compression at extremely low rates, and rate–distortion–perception trade-offs. Opening the black box of learned codes: what neural encoders learn on tractable (e.g., vector Gaussian) sources, whether they recover known constructions such as Shannon–Kotel’nikov mappings or superposition codes, and what a “neural interface” between source and channel coding should look like. Multi-user and networked settings: correlated sources over multiple-access and relay channels, and communication-efficient inference and learning with large models at the network edge. These questions are timely: generative AI is reshaping how data are compressed and transmitted, and AI-native, semantic and task-oriented communication are being considered for 6G, yet principled answers about what learned systems can and cannot achieve remain scarce. You will be encouraged to develop your own research agenda within this space, from fundamental limits to over-the-air demonstrations on our software-defined radio testbed. This full-time, in-person postdoctoral position is based at Imperial College’s South Kensington Campus in London, UK, and is funded for up to 24 months, starting in January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The Research Associate will be supervised by Prof. Deniz Gunduz within the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department at Imperial College London. Co-supervision will be provided by Prof. Krishna Narayanan and Prof. Chao Tian at Texas A&M University (USA), through regular joint meetings and research visits. What you would be doing Key responsibilities include: To shape and lead your own research agenda within the themes above To undertake original research of international excellence To develop fundamental theory and turn it into practical learned coding and communication schemes, validated in simulation and, where appropriate, on our software-defined radio testbed To write reports for submission to research sponsors To present findings at international conferences and at joint project meetings with Texas A&M University To publish in leading venues in information theory, machine learning and communications (e.g., IEEE Trans. items.title: Research Associate in Private and Trustworthy AI: Information-Theoretic Foundations
items.card: About the role How can we design a watermark that survives editing or paraphrasing? What does it mean, information-theoretically, for a model to have `forgotten’ a training example? What is the price in utility of preventing a model from leaking its training data? We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to tackle questions like these within INFORMED-AI, the UKRI AI Hub on Information Theory for Distributed AI
items.desc: Job number ENG04107 Faculties Faculty of Engineering Departments Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - Hybrid Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 2 Dec 2026 About the role How can we design a watermark that survives editing or paraphrasing? What does it mean, information-theoretically, for a model to have `forgotten’ a training example? What is the price in utility of preventing a model from leaking its training data? We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to tackle questions like these within INFORMED-AI, the UKRI AI Hub on Information Theory for Distributed AI (Imperial, Bristol, Cambridge, Durham). The aim is to bring the tools of information and coding theory (e.g., hypothesis testing, channel coding with adversaries, rate-distortion theory, and operational measures of information leakage) to enable trustworthiness of modern generative models, and to turn the resulting insights into practical algorithms. Potential research directions include, but are not limited to: watermarking and provenance for LLMs and diffusion models (fundamental detectability-quality-robustness trade-offs, watermarks that provably resist adversarial editing, and connections to information hiding and arbitrarily varying channels); machine unlearning (information-theoretic definitions and certificates of forgetting, and efficient algorithms that achieve them); and privacy-preserving training and inference (privacy-utility trade-offs, membership inference and memorisation viewed as hypothesis testing, and privacy in federated and distributed learning). These questions are extremely timely and important: regulation such as the EU AI Act is beginning to require that AI-generated content be watermarked, while principled answers are still missing. You will be encouraged to develop your own research agenda within this space. This full-time, in-person postdoctoral position is based at Imperial College’s South Kensington Campus in London, UK, and is funded for up to 24 months, starting in January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The Research Associate will be supervised by Prof. Deniz Gunduz within the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department at Imperial College London. items.desc: Facing the challenges of our time - Help us grow and be more impactful! CSEM is advancing the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate the design of complex physical systems. Several ongoing projects apply ML-driven optimization and physics-informed modeling to engineering domains including photonic integrated circuits, electromagnetic antenna design, and photonic simulation. The “ Integrated and Wireless Systems” Business Unit, based in Neuchâtel, Switzerland is looking for a motivated intern to contribute to the AI and machine learning aspects of these efforts. Your mission You will support a multidisciplinary team in applying machine learning to inverse design and simulation problems. The internship sits at the intersection of AI and physics-based engineering: you will help develop, train, and benchmark ML models that optimize device geometries or accelerate physical simulations. Depending on your profile and interests, your work may focus on one or more of the following application areas: Inverse design of nonlinear photonic waveguides for supercontinuum generation, using surrogate-based and Bayesian optimization to explore large design spaces. AI-assisted antenna design, combining electromagnetic simulations with data-driven modeling to address multi-objective constraints and explore complex design spaces. items.desc: Summary Apple's DRM stack protects media content and applications. Across the industry, external attackers increasingly use LLMs — interactively or via automated/agentic pipelines — to accelerate reverse-engineering of software protections; this is a general and growing trend, not specific to any one target. This internship addresses that trend directly: developing, from first principles, inputs that measurably perturb an LLM's internal state (activations, attention distributions, representation geometry) in ways that degrade its ability to usefully assist an attacker analyzing protected code/binaries. Description This internship addresses that trend directly: developing, from first principles, inputs that measurably perturb an LLM's internal state (activations, attention distributions, representation geometry) in ways that degrade its ability to usefully assist an attacker analyzing protected code/binaries. Responsibilities Formulate the problem mathematically: define what "confusion" or degraded internal state means in terms of measurable quantities (activation/representation drift, attention entropy, logit distribution shift, loss landscape behavior) rather than qualitative output judgments. Develop gradient-based and optimization-based methods for crafting adversarial inputs (e.g. embedding-space perturbation, discrete token optimization à la GCG/greedy coordinate search, universal adversarial triggers) targeting the internal-state objectives defined above. Analyze transformer internals (attention matrices, residual stream, activation subspaces) to identify structural properties — e.g. spectral characteristics, representation collapse, direction vectors linked to specific behaviors — that can be exploited or reinforced. Study whether techniques derived on open-weight models (full white-box access) transfer to closed-weight models via black-box/transfer-based optimization, and quantify the transfer gap mathematically. Build a rigorous evaluation methodology: statistically sound metrics, ablations isolating which mathematical property of the input drives the effect, and robustness checks across model families and versions. Assess durability: whether effects derived from current architectures are expected to hold under fine-tuning, distillation, or future model versions, based on the underlying mathematical mechanism rather than empirical trial-and-error. Document the mathematical framework, methods, and results internally for Apple's use only; no external publication. Minimum Qualifications Currently completing a Master's degree or enrolled in a PhD, in Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, with strong theoretical grounding. Strong foundations in linear algebra, optimization (convex and non-convex), and probability/information theory, and ability to apply them to deep learning internals rather than just use libraries. Solid understanding of transformer architecture internals (attention mechanics, residual stream, embeddings) at a mathematical level. Hands-on experience with gradient-based adversarial attack techniques (FGSM/PGD-style methods, discrete optimization for token sequences, universal adversarial perturbations). Proficiency in Python and PyTorch, including writing custom gradient computations/hooks into model internals (not just using high-level APIs). Preferred Qualifications Research experience in adversarial machine learning or mechanistic interpretability (activation patching, representation engineering, steering vectors). Familiarity with reverse engineering / binary analysis, to reason about what a real attacker workflow needs from the LLM. Coursework or research in spectral methods, information theory, or statistical learning theory applied to neural network analysis. items.desc: Position description Category Mathematics, information, scientific, software Contract Internship Job title Intership Learning ultrasonic acquisition patterns for 3D interface characterisation-Saclay-H/F Subject Volumetric ultrasonic inspection with a 2D matrix array generates large amounts of data. In the configuration considered here, the matrix probe is coupled to the component through a conformable water-filled membrane that adapts to its unknown surface. The water–component interface must first be located and characterised to compute refraction points and travel times inside the component, and subsequently form the TFM 3D (Total Focusing Method) image correctly. This internship aims to accelerate this characterisation stage by selecting, under a fixed acquisition budget, a sparse pattern of informative elements or emissions. Contract duration (months) 6 months Job description As an intern at the CEA, you will have the opportunity to work within a world-renowned research environment. Our teams consist of passionate and dedicated experts, providing an ideal setting for learning and collaboration. You will have access to state-of-the-art equipment and top-tier research resources to carry out your assignments. The work conducted may potentially lead to a scientific publication. Objectives and proposed work For parametric surfaces, the internship will leverage existing semi-analytical estimation of planar and cylindrical surface parameters [1], and use reinforcement learning to identify sparse acquisition patterns that minimise errors in the estimated parameters, surface geometry and refracted travel times. For general surfaces, the internship will investigate how geometric envelope methods [2] can be extended to sparse acquisition settings, where spatial derivatives of the travel-time field must be estimated on a graph of sparse array elements, notably through weighted local regression. Regular, random, deterministic and optimised patterns from the 2D sparse-array literature [3] will serve as initialisations, baselines and relative penalties during training. All strategies will be compared at equal acquisition cost on simulated and then experimental data, using errors in surface parameters, surface points and normals, together with the induced travel-time error in an internal region. Methodology and outlook The work will combine geometrical modelling, signal processing, optimisation and reinforcement learning. A first policy will learn a fixed acquisition pattern tailored to a given family of surfaces; extending it to sequential and adaptive selection will be a natural next step. Reconstructed TFM image quality may subsequently provide an additional criterion for refining the interface. In the longer term, surface estimation and refraction-point estimation could be integrated into a learnt amortised solver. References [1] E. Iakovleva, D. Roué, and M. Marmonier, “Time efficient autofocus TFM imaging for ultrasonic inspection of planar and cylindrical components,” Ultrasonics, vol. 166, art. 108118, 2026, doi: 10.1016/j.ultras.2026.108118. [2] J. Camacho, J. F. Cruza, J. Brizuela, and C. Fritsch, “Automatic dynamic depth focusing for NDT,” IEEE Trans. Ultrason., Ferroelectr., Freq. Control, vol. 61, no. 4, pp. 673–684, 2014. [3] A. Ramalli, E. Boni, E. Roux, H. Liebgott, and P. Tortoli, “Design, implementation, and medical applications of 2-D ultrasound sparse arrays,” IEEE Trans. Ultrason., Ferroelectr., Freq. Control, vol. 69, no. 10, pp. 2739–2755, 2022, doi: 10.1109/TUFFC.2022.3162419. # CEA-List Methods / Means Python Applicant Profile Final-year engineering student or master’s student in machine learning, signal processing or applied mathematics; proficiency in Python/Pytorch; interest in ultrasonics, scientific computing. items.desc: A technology consultancy delivering applied research and engineering for clients tackling complex, high-stakes technical problems. The organisation is growing its technical team and offers structured mentorship from senior scientists and engineers. What the job involves The role centres on applying machine learning to unusual, real-world problems, often without an existing playbook to follow. You'll combine off-the-shelf tools with custom-built components, moving between understanding the theory behind a model and getting a working version built and tested. Work is organised around projects running from early conceptual exploration through to functioning prototypes, lasting anywhere from a few months to a couple of years. Responsibilities generally include: Reviewing relevant technical literature and staying current with the field Forming and testing new ideas or hypotheses Building and training models for non-standard applications Rapid, hands-on prototyping and debugging Running structured experiments Interpreting and reporting on results Recommending next steps or further research directions There's also a client-facing element — understanding client needs and translating them into workable technical solutions. items.desc: Wil je de computer vision technieken van morgen mee helpen vormgeven? Als Researcher in het Vision Team werk je volledig intern aan onderzoek en ontwikkeling. Je verkent nieuwe technieken, zet experimenten op en zorgt dat wat vandaag in de wetenschappelijke literatuur verschijnt, morgen bruikbare kennis is voor ons team. Over Vintecc’s Vision Team Vintecc versnelt de industrie met AI en software op maat. We tellen meer dan 70 collega's in Roeselare (hoofdkantoor) en Gent. Het Vision Team geeft machines en processen visuele intelligentie: objectherkenning en optisch sorteren, real-time tracking, volumescanning en productiemetingen. Waar onze Vision Engineers die oplossingen bij klanten bouwen, kijk jij verder vooruit. De functie Als onderzoeker van het Vision Team doe je fundamenteel onderzoek binnen onze R&D-trajecten, bijvoorbeeld met VLAIO-steun of samen met universiteiten en kennisinstellingen. Je resultaten worden door je collega-engineers ingezet in klantprojecten, waardoor je onderzoek rechtstreeks resultaat oplevert in de praktijk. Zo kun jij je volledig focussen op het onderzoek zelf, terwijl je collega’s de klantprojecten trekken. Wat doe je? Je volgt de state of the art in computer vision en deep learning op en beoordeelt wat de moeite waard is voor de industrie. Je voert onderzoek uit binnen lopende R&D-projecten, rond thema's als synthetische data, 3D deep learning, objectdetectie en -tracking, en modellen op edge-hardware. Je ontwerpt experimenten, test nieuwe methodes grondig en evalueert de resultaten objectief. Je documenteert je bevindingen helder in technische rapporten en projectdeliverables. Je helpt mee aan het uitschrijven van nieuwe R&D-projectvoorstellen. Je deelt je kennis met het team via demo's, validatie met projectdata, interne sessies of publicaties. Wie zoeken we? Een doctoraat in computer vision, AI of een verwant domein geniet de voorkeur. Een master in de ingenieurswetenschappen, informatica of AI met aantoonbare onderzoekservaring kan ook. Een diepgaande kennis van computer vision en deep learning (bv. CNN's, transformers, detectie en segmentatie). Je gebruikt Python, NumPy, PyTorch en OpenCV om experimenten uit te voeren. Een onderzoekende, kritische houding: je zet zelf experimenten op en durft resultaten in vraag te stellen. Je werkt graag geconcentreerd en zelfstandig aan een duidelijk afgebakende onderzoeksvraag. Je bent communicatief: je legt je resultaten helder uit aan collega's, mondeling en schriftelijk, zowel in het Nederlands als in het Engels. Pluspunten (geen must): Ervaring met synthetische data, simulatie of rendering (bv. Blender, Unity, Omniverse). Ervaring met 3D-vision, dieptecamera's of multispectrale beeldvorming. Publicaties of ervaring met Vlaamse of Europese onderzoeksprojecten. Wat bieden we? Loon Een competitief loon, afgestemd op je opleiding en ervaring, met vakantiegeld en een eindejaarspremie die je fiscaal voordelig kunt inzetten via ons cafetariaplan. Extralegale voordelen Een mobiliteitsbudget of bedrijfswagen met tankkaart of laadpas, of een woon-werkvergoeding. Maaltijdcheques en ecocheques. Een gsm en mobiel internetabonnement. Een groepsverzekering en een hospitalisatieverzekering. Een maandelijkse onkostenvergoeding. Een collectieve groepsbonus (cao 90) vanaf een bepaalde anciënniteit. Groeien en ontwikkelen Opleidingen, conferenties en samenwerking met universiteiten en kennisinstellingen. Duidelijke groeipaden en een job die je mee vormgeeft (job crafting). Autonomie en ruimte voor initiatief: je tekent je eigen onderzoekslijnen mee uit. Work-life balance Een open, hechte bedrijfscultuur met korte lijnen en een partyteam. Glijdende werkuren en thuiswerk. 32 verlofdagen die je vrij kiest. Je werkt vanuit ons hoofdkantoor in Roeselare en kunt af en toe ook terecht in ons kantoor in Gent.

items.card: You will build the speech and voice AI that runs across Talkpush: our own AI interviewer, real-time conversation analysis, candidate scoring, and support for new languages. You will be the speech specialist on the team, deciding with product what to build next and shipping it. You will get context, data and support, and little technical hand-holding, by design. The problem and the data Our candidates speak on real
items.desc: Location: Remote. Compensation: USD 45,000 to 65,000 base, plus equity. About Talkpush Talkpush is the AI-powered applicant tracking system and recruitment CRM built for high-volume hiring. Founded in Hong Kong about ten years ago, we help employers in retail, customer experience, healthcare, transportation and finance attract, screen, interview and hire thousands of candidates at once, over WhatsApp, SMS, social channels, chat and voice. Millions of people have been hired through the platform, mostly across Asia-Pacific, Latin America and other emerging markets. Mission Give every candidate a fair hearing by voice, in their own accent and language, at the scale of high-volume hiring. You will build the speech and voice AI that runs across Talkpush: our own AI interviewer, real-time conversation analysis, candidate scoring, and support for new languages. You will be the speech specialist on the team, deciding with product what to build next and shipping it. You will get context, data and support, and little technical hand-holding, by design. The problem and the data Our candidates speak on real phone lines and in browsers, often on 8 kHz audio, in noisy rooms, answering unscripted questions. Many are Filipino, Indian, Latin American and South African English speakers, and many switch between languages mid-sentence (Tagalog and English, for example). Off-the-shelf speech models were mostly trained on clean, scripted audio and a narrow set of reference accents, and they struggle here. We run our own voice stack and keep our own recordings. That gives us a large, rare dataset: tens of thousands of labelled audio clips from real interviews, many linked to recruiter ratings and hiring outcomes. First 90 days Listen to a lot of real calls. Map the recordings, ratings and hiring outcomes, and check how reliable the human labels are. Build a gold evaluation set, held out and stratified by market, accent and score band, joined to hiring outcomes. This becomes the bar every model must clear. Fine-tune an open speech encoder (Whisper, WavLM or wav2vec2) into a first speech scorer for fluency, pronunciation and intelligibility. Run it silently alongside live traffic and publish honest results, including where it fails. Write a dated plan for the year and share it. First year Add a transcript and content branch and fuse it with the acoustic model. Calibrate scores to real hiring outcomes, with light adapters for different clients and roles. Distil the model into a fast version for real-time analysis during and right after each call, so the AI interviewer can adapt mid-conversation. Extend to new languages (candidates include Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, French, Turkish and Urdu) and to code-switched speech. Publish an accent-robustness benchmark showing that matched-proficiency speakers get matched scores across accent groups. Responsibilities Own speech and voice models end to end: data, training, evaluation, deployment and monitoring. Shape the voice AI roadmap with product, engineering and client-facing colleagues. Write the specs, then ship them. Keep measurement honest: held-out test sets, per-accent error analysis, test-retest checks, no vanity metrics. Make fairness across accents a design requirement from day one. Work in production with our engineers on latency, cost and reliability. Own outcomes end to end, commit to dates, and write short, clear updates. Must-haves You have shipped speech ML models to production that real users depend on. You have fine-tuned Whisper, WavLM, wav2vec2 or similar encoders on your own data and can explain what worked and what did not. You have worked with messy real-world audio: telephony, 8 kHz, noise, spontaneous speech. You have built pronunciation, fluency, speaker or paralinguistic models, or ASR for accented or low-resource speech. You have designed evaluation sets and reported results you did not like, and changed course because of them. You have owned a product area or a technical roadmap, including telling people what you would not build. Nice-to-haves Experience with code-switched or multilingual speech. Work on fairness, bias audits or calibration of scores against human raters or downstream outcomes. Streaming or real-time inference, and model distillation. Forced alignment tools (Montreal Forced Aligner, WhisperX) and public L2 corpora (speechocean762, L2-ARCTIC). Using audio-LLMs as weak labellers, or TTS to create synthetic training data. Papers at Interspeech or ICASSP, or well-used open-source speech work. Experience in HR tech, contact centres or language testing. Interview process Our process: a 10-minute voice pre-screen with our AI interviewer, a take-home on real audio (about a day of work across a week), a case study with our CEO, a technical deep dive with a peer engineer, then references. Every hire needs a unanimous yes. Compensation and location Location: Remote. Compensation: USD 45,000 to 65,000 base, plus equity.
