items.desc:
About the team

The AI Deployment Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior.

This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems.

About the role

We are seeking a technically proficient, product-minded engineer to help push the frontier of advanced AI with our strategic startup customers. You'll work with some of the most exciting AI startups in the world, helping them optimize their own systems and turning those learnings into durable improvements across OpenAI’s research and products. You will partner deeply on complex workflows, identify the gaps that matter, and help transform those gaps into reproducible evaluations, technical insights - helping shape OpenAI's research and product direction.

This role is well suited to engineers who are equally comfortable debugging a workflow, iterating on prompts or agents, designing evaluations, and collaborating across research and product. You should be excited by ambiguous, high-impact problems and motivated by the opportunity to shape how advanced AI systems improve in practice.



In this role, you will:

 - Work directly with strategic startup customers to understand critical workflows, uncover failure modes, and identify high-impact opportunities for improvement.

 - Prototype and iterate on prompts, agents, and workflow designs to better understand system behavior and unlock customer value.

 - Synthesize and deliver valuable feedback to the Product and Research teams, turning real usage patterns into clear, reproducible evals, benchmarks, and technical artifacts that improve model and product quality and ensure customer-grounded learnings influence roadmap and model development.

 - Build repeatable tools, patterns, and evaluation approaches that raise the quality bar across multiple use cases.

 - Operate with strong judgment in ambiguous environments, balancing immediate technical problem-solving with longer-term system improvement.

 - Build relationships within the startup ecosystem, serving as a technical partner to both individual customers and the broader community.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong software engineering & AI fundamentals. For example, experience as a startup CTO, software engineer, ML engineer, Data Scientist or equivalent. Experience shipping production systems end-to-end is a strong plus.

 - Have experience as a technical founder, or engineer at an early stage startup

 - Have familiarity with, or interest in, model training pipelines and reinforcement learning.

 - Have experience building AI applications, agents, or evaluation systems, and can reason clearly about model behavior in complex workflows.

 - Are comfortable working directly with highly technical users and translating their challenges into concrete technical signals.

 - Can move fluidly between prototyping, debugging, evaluation design, and cross-functional collaboration.

 - Communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Bring high agency, strong product sense, and a bias toward building durable improvements rather than one-off fixes





About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. 

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. Apple's DRM stack protects media content and applications. Across the industry, external attackers increasingly use LLMs — interactively or via automated/agentic pipelines — to accelerate reverse-engineering of software protections; this is a general and growing trend, not specific to any one target. This internship addresses that trend directly: developing, from first principles, inputs that measurably perturb an LLM's internal state (activations, attention distributions, representation geometry) in ways that degrade its ability to usefully assist an attacker analyzing protected code/binaries.

items.desc: Company Description Ubisoft is a global leader in gaming with teams across the world creating original and memorable gaming experiences, from Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six to Just Dance and more. We believe diverse perspectives help both players and teams thrive. If you’re passionate about innovation and pushing entertainment boundaries, join our journey and help create the unknown! Ubisoft Bordeaux Founded in 2017 by a handful of Ubisoft experts, our studio now counts over 400 talents from 20 different nationalities. Our teams contribute to some of Ubisoft’s biggest franchises: leading the production of Assassin’s Creed Mirage in 2023, working on Assassin’s Creed Shadows and the Claws of Awaji expansion, as well as unannounced projects. Beyond our AAA productions, we also drive technological innovation within the group through our expertise in the Anvil game engine and Ubisoft’s Online Services. We have also established a dedicated R&D division, La Forge, which brings together Ubisoft engineers and academic researchers to collaborate on prototypes that support game development, particularly in the field of AI. Job Description Rendering complex visual effects, such as refractive glass, translucent materials, smoke, and other view-dependent or volumetric phenomena, often require specialized rendering techniques, including dedicated rendering passes or ray tracing. While these methods can produce high-quality results, they can also be computationally expensive, making them challenging to integrate into real-time applications under tight performance constraints. Recent advances in neural rendering, frame generation, and generative models open new possibilities for rethinking how such effects are produced. Rather than explicitly simulating complex light transport, neural models could learn to reconstruct or approximate the final appearance of an object from its rendered representation and surrounding image context. This suggests a new rendering paradigm in which computationally expensive visual effects could be partially replaced by learned image-space transformations. This internship will explore neural compositing, an approach in which selected objects are rendered using simplified geometric or shading proxies and subsequently enhanced by screen-space neural models that predict their final visual appearance. The objective is to investigate whether this approach can reproduce the visual complexity of effects such as refraction, translucency, and volumetric phenomena while reducing the cost of conventional rendering techniques. The work will involve exploring recent developments in neural rendering, neural shading, and frame generation, and investigating their potential application to real-time visual effects. Different neural compositing strategies will be considered through experimental prototypes, with an emphasis on understanding how scene information and rendered inputs can be leveraged to reconstruct complex visual phenomena. The internship is exploratory in nature, with the aim of identifying the strengths and limitations of neural compositing and determining which classes of visual effects are best suited to this approach. The findings will help assess its potential as a complement to conventional rendering techniques and inform future research on the topic. References [1] DLSS 5: Generative Neural Rendering (https://research.nvidia.com/labs/adlr/DLSS5/) [2] Generative AI model for Global Illumination effects (https://gpuopen.com/learn/genai-model-for-global-illumination/) [3] Temporally stable generative illumination with a one-step diffusion model (https://gpuopen.com/learn/temporally-stable-generative-illumination/) [4] An Introduction to Neural Shading (https://research.nvidia.com/labs/rtr/publication/duca2025neural/) Qualifications You are in the final year of an engineering degree or pursuing a research master in computer science or a related field Ability to read and understand research papers Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python Good Knowledge of machine learning and neural networks Good Understanding of image processing or computer vision concepts Basic Understanding of computer graphics and real-time rendering Familiarity with diffusion models or generative models is a plus Good communication skills in English, written and spoken. Additional Information Contract : 6 months internship from March 2027 to September 2027. An internship agreement provided by your school is mandatory. Location : Bordeaux Supervision Antoine Houdard (R&D Scientist) Georges Nader (R&D Scientist)

items.desc: 97170 PETIT-BOURG Retour à la liste des résultats Présentation INRAE L’Institut national de recherche pour l’agriculture, l’alimentation et l’environnement (INRAE) est un établissement public de recherche rassemblant une communauté de travail de 12 000 personnes, avec 272 unités de recherche, de service et expérimentales, implantées dans 18 centres sur toute la France. INRAE se positionne parmi les tout premiers leaders mondiaux en sciences agricoles et alimentaires, en sciences du végétal et de l’animal. Ses recherches visent à construire des solutions pour des agricultures multi-performantes, une alimentation de qualité et une gestion durable des ressources et des écosystèmes. Votre mission s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet TAESA (Guadeloupe Une Santé) financé par le FEDER Région Guadeloupe, qui a pour objectif de co-concevoir avec les agriculteur.ices, et avec l'appui des politiques publiques, des systèmes agricoles fournissant des produits sains aux consommateurs. Impliquant une cinquantaine de chercheur.es d'INRAE et du CIRAD, il se place délibérément dans une démarche agroécologique pour accompagner les agriculteur.rices vers des pratiques vertueuses et productives. L'agroécologie implique de la part des chercheur.es de déployer une démarche participative, seule capable d'hybrider les connaissances paysannes, politiques et scientifiques et d'aboutir à des innovations utiles et durables. Dans le cadre de ce projet, nous développons un outil de phénotypage à haut débit des cultures végétales fondé sur l'imagerie aérienne. Le dispositif repose sur un drone DJI Mavic 3 Multispectral équipé d'une caméra RGB (20 MP) et de quatre bandes multispectrales (vert, rouge, red edge, proche infrarouge), avec positionnement RTK centimétrique. Le traitement des images est réalisé sur une station de calcul MSI Edgexpert (puce NVIDIA GB-10), qui sera dédiée au développement des algorithmes d'intelligence artificielle. Les données sont acquises sur des parcelles expérimentales, sur plusieurs dates de vol au cours du cycle cultural, avec collecte simultanée de mesures de vérité terrain Environnement de travail, missions et activités L'objectif du stage est de concevoir, entraîner et évaluer des modèles d'apprentissage profond pour l'analyse des orthomosaïques issues des vols drone. Les tâches visées comprennent : 1. la segmentation sémantique ou d'instance (par exemple : distinction culture / adventices / sol, couverture du sol,segmentation de la canopée) ; 2. la détection et le comptage d'objets (par exemple : comptage de plants, détection d'anomalies) ; 3. l’extraction et la comparaison d'indices de végétation (NDVI, NDRE, GNDVI) à partir des données multispectrales calibrées en réflectance. Le ou la stagiaire participera à l'ensemble de la chaîne de traitement : préparation et structuration du jeu de données, annotation d'un lot initial d'images, choix des architectures (par exemple U-Net, YOLO, ou modèles de fondation pré- entraînés avec transfert learning), entraînement sur MSI Edgexpert, évaluation méthodologique (validation croisée par parcelle) et industrialisation du pipeline sous forme de code reproductible. Missions confiées au ou à la stagiaire : 1. État de l'art sur l'application de l'apprentissage profond à l'imagerie agricole par drone ; 2.Participation aux campagnes d'acquisition terrain et aux mesures de vérité terrain ; 3. Construction du jeu de données : prétraitement des images, calibration radiométrique, génération desorthomosaïques, annotation d'un lot initial de tuiles ; 4. Développement et entraînement des modèles sur la station de calcul (Python, PyTorch, CUDA) ; 5. Évaluation comparative des approches (métriques de segmentation et de détection, validation par parcelle, tests degénéralisation inter-dates et inter-sites) ; 6. Rédaction d'un pipeline de traitement reproductible (code versionné, documentation) et contribution à la restitution des résultats (rapport de stage). Prise de fonction possible entre Janvier et Juin 2027. Formations et compétences recherchées Licence/Master (Bac+3/5) Formation recommandée : Master 2 ou dernière année d'école d'ingénieurs en intelligence artificielle, vision par ordinateur, science des données, géomatique / télédétection, ou agronomie avec spécialisation numérique. Compétences techniques attendues :1. Solide maîtrise de Python (NumPy, Pandas) ; 2. Expérience pratique de l'apprentissage profond avec PyTorch ou TensorFlow (projet personnel, académique ouantérieur attesté) ; 3. Notions de traitement d'images et de télédétection souhaitées ; une expérience avec des données raster (GDAL,rasterio, QGIS) est un plus ; 4. Connaissance des outils de gestion de code (Git) et, idéalement, des environnements conteneurisés (Docker) et du calcul GPU ; 5. Un intérêt marqué pour les applications agronomiques est souhaité ; une formation ou une expérience en agronomie constitue un atout apprécié. Prepare training and evaluation datasets. Analyse model errors, identify gaps in the data, define annotation tasks and review the resulting examples. Select models and develop prompts. Compare internally hosted models with external APIs in terms of quality, latency and cost. Maintain evaluation datasets and benchmarks. Check new versions for regressions and investigate poor responses and user feedback. Build services and APIs around models. Package and deploy them, add logging and monitoring, and investigate issues in production. Improve inference speed, GPU memory usage and serving cost while maintaining the required response quality. Understanding of transformer models, tokenisation, training and text generation. Experience adapting language models through supervised fine tuning and approaches such as LoRA. Ability to prepare and validate datasets, prevent data leakage and investigate model errors. Experience evaluating generated text using benchmarks, human review and automated methods. Understanding of the limitations of each approach. Experience working with model APIs, prompts and structured outputs. Ability to build and maintain APIs using FastAPI or a comparable framework. Practical experience with Docker, Linux, Git and deploying models on GPUs. Familiarity with an inference framework such as vLLM or an equivalent tool. Ability to add logging, monitoring and appropriate tests, investigate production failures and roll back a faulty release. SQL skills sufficient to retrieve and analyse product data. English sufficient to read technical documentation and research papers. Practical experience with recommendation systems, even if limited. Bonuses up to $5000 for recommending successful applicants for positions in the company; 50% payment for professional training, international conferences, and meetings; Corporate discount for English lessons; Health benefits. According to the paychecks, if you are not eligible for corporate medical insurance, the company will compensate you with up to $ 1,000 gross per year per employee. items.card: About the role Wild populations are facing increasing environmental pressures that can outpace their ability to adapt. We are seeking a quantitative researcher to investigate whether interventions could help populations adapt, and to understand their potential benefits and risks. You will join Dr Katie Willis’s research group in the Department of Life Sciences at Imperial’s Silwood Park Campus to work as part of the
items.desc: Job number NAT02329 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Life Sciences (Silwood Park) Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus Silwood Park Campus - Hybrid Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 16 Dec 2026 About the role Wild populations are facing increasing environmental pressures that can outpace their ability to adapt. We are seeking a quantitative researcher to investigate whether interventions could help populations adapt, and to understand their potential benefits and risks. You will join Dr Katie Willis’s research group in the Department of Life Sciences at Imperial’s Silwood Park Campus to work as part of the MERGE (Modelling Evolutionary Resilience: from Genes to Ecosystems) project. MERGE is funded by the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) through its Accelerated Adaptation programme, which explores whether adaptation in wild species can be accelerated responsibly to help address biodiversity loss. Within MERGE, you will collaborate with researchers at Imperial, the University of Reading, the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and Topos Institute UK. You will also work with experimental teams across the wider ARIA programme, bringing modelling expertise to questions across different biological systems. What you would be doing You will develop and analyse models to investigate the potential benefits and risks of novel interventions intended to accelerate adaptation in wild populations. This will include investigating how genetic, demographic and ecological processes influence intervention outcomes and population persistence. Your work will draw on relevant literature and empirical evidence, alongside simulation studies, sensitivity analyses and uncertainty quantification. You will work with ARIA’s experimental teams (Technical Area 1) to identify modelling questions and data needs. Your models will help inform experimental design, interpret findings and compare intervention options, connecting experimental evidence with predictions for natural populations. There will also be scope to explore new intervention approaches within the group’s wider research programme. You will help develop existing proposals and contribute ideas of your own, with research priorities agreed with Dr Willis. You will maintain well-documented code and analyses, contribute to publications, presentations and regular reports, and support relevant student research projects. What we are looking for You will hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in a relevant biological, mathematical or computational discipline. We welcome applicants from backgrounds including ecology, evolutionary biology, mathematical biology, applied mathematics and computer science. You will bring: Experience of developing and analysing mathematical or computational models to address biological questions. Knowledge of at least one area relevant to population modelling, such as population genetics, population ecology, evolutionary biology or mathematical biology. Scientific programming experience in Python, C++, Mathematica, R, Julia or a comparable language. Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including the ability to evaluate model assumptions and results critically. Clear communication skills, initiative and a willingness to contribute actively to the group’s research and collaborate across disciplines. What we can offer you The opportunity to join an ambitious, fast-paced ARIA-funded programme exploring new approaches to help wild populations adapt to environmental change. Collaboration with researchers across disciplines and partner institutions, with scope to help shape research questions and develop your ideas within agreed project priorities. Access to Imperial’s dedicated career support for researchers and professional development opportunities. Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Further information The post is available as soon as possible. This is a full-time appointment based at Silwood Park Campus, fixed-term until October 2028, with the possibility of a further two-year extension, subject to grant approval. Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant. If you require any further details on the role please contact: Katie Willis, katie.willis@imperial.ac.uk. Informal enquiries are welcome. Available documents Attached documents are available under links. Clicking a document link will initialize its download. Please note that job descriptions are not exhaustive, and you may be asked to take on additional duties that align with the key responsibilities mentioned above. We reserve the right to close the advert before the stated closing date, should we receive a high volume of applications. Please submit your application as early as possible to avoid disappointment. The position focuses on developing reinforcement learning methods that produce understandable control strategies and provide insight into the underlying system dynamics and causal relationships. The research will address safe and effective control of cyber-physical systems, with particular emphasis on UPPAAL Stratego and collaboration with domain experts and external partners. Expected starting date: 01.12.2026. Your work tasks You will develop and evaluate methods for explainable and causality informed reinforcement learning. The aim is to make learned strategies transparent to human domain experts, support well-founded trust in their decisions, and improve understanding of hidden dynamics and causal relationships in the systems being controlled. Your tasks will include: Developing compact, interpretable representations of learned control strategies, including strategy minimisation with guaranteed preservation of safety properties. Investigating how causal information can inform reinforcement learning and help explain the behaviour and decisions of learned strategies. Working with reinforcement learning and recurrent neural networks in UPPAAL Stratego, including implementation and experimental evaluation. Applying and evaluating the methods on safety-critical cyber-physical systems, with relevant case studies in water and wastewater infrastructure. Collaborating with DEIS researchers, the UPPAAL development team and external partners, and contributing to scientific publications and dissemination. The work builds on DEIS research in safe reinforcement learning and practical experience with UPPAAL Stratego for modelling and optimal control of wastewater infrastructure, including collaboration with HOFOR continuing the DIREC Bridge project Verifiable and Safe AI. Your competencies You should have a strong background in reinforcement learning and machine learning, solid programming skills, and experience implementing and evaluating research methods. Knowledge of explainable AI, causal reasoning, recurrent neural networks, or interpretable policy representations is particularly relevant. Experience with UPPAAL or UPPAAL Stratego, formal verification, and modelling and control of cyber-physical systems is an advantage. You should be able to work independently, collaborate with researchers and domain experts, and communicate research clearly in English. Qualification requirements Appointment as a research assistant requires academic qualifications at master’s degree level. A relevant degree in computer science or a closely related discipline is expected. Who we are You will join Section DEIS at the Department of Computer Science, Aalborg University. The position brings together research in formal methods, machine learning and cyber-physical systems, with opportunities to contribute to the UPPAAL tool suite and its applications. How to apply Your application must include the following: An application stating your reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position. Curriculum Vitae (CV). Diplomas. A list of publications. You may attach a maximum of five publications (optional). Documentation of teaching qualifications, following the relevant faculty guidelines for teaching portfolios. Dissemination qualifications, including participation in committees, boards or organisations. Additional qualifications relevant to the position. References or recommendations. Please consult Aalborg University’s application requirements for further guidance. The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University’s website. Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. Do you have any questions For questions about the position, please contact Professor Kim Guldstrand Larsen, kgl@cs.aau.dk, telephone +45 22 17 11 59. Further information Read more about our recruitment process here The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here. The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. items.desc: Cambrex Profarmaco Milano is looking for a curious and dynamic intern interesed in Artificial Intelligence. For our Site in Paullo (Milan) we are looking for a trainee interested in with an expertise in ML methods and AI to insert in our Analytical Development team for an industrial project focused on building an AI-powered HPLC recommendation engine. This project leverages proprietary pharmaceutical data to develop machine learning models that predict optimal chromatographic conditions for new compounds. Responsibilities: Design and curate a structured experimental knowledge database linking molecular representations (SMILES, InChI, fingerprints), physicochemical descriptors, chromatographic method parameters, and experimental outcomes, with a focus on data quality, reproducibility, and design suitable for ML; Develop a feature selection pipeline for classical descriptors (RDKit, Mordred) and learned representations (molecular fingerprints, graph-based embeddings); Research, train, and benchmark predictive models for chromatographic outcomes (retention behaviour, mobile phase strength, column selectivity class), exploring both interpretable models and state-of-the-art approaches; Design a molecular similarity module grounded in chemical space geometry, evaluating distance metrics and embedding spaces for nearest-neighbour method retrieval from historical data; Build a recommendation engine that unifies predictive modelling and the similarity module, with uncertainty quantification, confidence scoring, and explainability to support trust and adoption by domain scientists; Extend the engine into an agentic LLM interface that allows natural language interaction with the underlying models and database; Validate the system on held-out experimental data, document methodology to publication standard, and present research outputs to both technical and domain-expert audiences. Qualifications and Skills: Degree in Computer Science/Engineering or a closely related field; Deep understanding of ML and AI. Strong research instincts: ability to identify the right problem formulation, design-controlled experiments and critically evaluate model behaviour rather than just benchmark metrics; Proficiency in Python and relevant libraries (scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, PyTorch, TensorFlow), comfort reading and adapting research code. Soft Skills: Good interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a team and flexibility; Proactivity, a strong focus on results, and problem-solving skills; Ability to work independently and communicate technical results to a non-specialist audience. It would be considered a plus: Familiarity with molecular representations and cheminformatics tools (SMILES, fingerprints, graph neural networks for molecules) or willingness to learn; Active interest in explainable and interpretable ML (XAI), particularly in applied scientific contexts where trust and transparency are critical; Hands-on experience with LLM tool-use, function calling, or agentic frameworks or conceptual grounding in how LLMs interact with external systems; Exposure to scientific, industrial, or experimental datasets with inherent noise, class imbalance, or sparse labelling, common in real-world R&D settings. What You Will Gain: Access to a proprietary industrial HPLC dataset not available in academic settings; AI research challenge with real-world constraints; Immersion in cheminformatics and pharmaceutical analytical R&D, with direct collaboration with domain scientists who will challenge and sharpen your modelling decisions; Research outputs aligned with your doctoral trajectory: publishable methodology, a working system demonstrating scientific AI in industrial settings; Mentoring from both chemoinformatics and domain experts, with genuine intellectual exchange. Location: Cambrex Profarmaco Milano Srl, Paullo (MI) On-site or Hybrid Model (to be discussed) Contract: We offer 1 year intership, details will be clarified during the interview process.

You will collaborate with researchers at Imperial, the University of Reading, the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and Topos Institute UK. items.desc: We wish to appoint a Research Associate to work on a national project with the TIMELY Team, in the Department of Psychiatry, University of Cambridge. The TIMELY Team is working to build clinically useful digital tools to predict mental health problems in children and young people and to support prevention pathways. This role will support a collaborative project to establish and develop the National Mental Health (MH) Translational Research Collaborative's Secure Data Environment (MH-TRC SDE), leading data standardisation. The appointee will work with the University of Cambridge team (Dr Anna Moore, Rudolph Cardinal), and collaborators at NHS Merseyside (Dr Jim Hughes, Informatics), University of Liverpool, Swansea University, Arden and Greater East Midlands CSU, King's College London, the SDE Network and HDR UK. The role is funded by the NIHR. The project is focused on developing data resources to support MH research. The Research Associate will contribute to the creation of a population-wide, multi-agency database called CADRE (Child and Adolescent Data REsource), which combines data drawn from healthcare, social care, education, and other services. CADRE is one of many MH SDEs that support MH research nationally; these SDEs require their raw data to be standardised to the OMOP Common Data Model. The Research Associate will support a high-level landscape review of OMOP use for MH data. They will adapt the CADRE standardisation approach to SDEs in Birmingham, Liverpool, and Manchester, as part of the effort to build a streamlined toolkit/guidelines to support OMOP standardisation for MH SDEs nationally. We are especially interested in integrating digital tools, including artificial intelligence, to the standardisation process. The role will also communicate to the MH research community about the importance of data standardisation and promote the MH SDE toolkit. The Research Associate will liaise with MH SDEs and data providers from across the UK. They will lead meetings and guide the data team to support project goals. Contribution to publications is needed. items.desc: Company Description Ubisoft is a global leader in gaming with teams across the world creating original and memorable gaming experiences, from Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six to Just Dance and more. We believe diverse perspectives help both players and teams thrive. If you’re passionate about innovation and pushing entertainment boundaries, join our journey and help create the unknown! Ubisoft Bordeaux Founded in 2017 by a handful of Ubisoft experts, our studio now counts over 400 talents from 20 different nationalities. Our teams contribute to some of Ubisoft’s biggest franchises: leading the production of Assassin’s Creed Mirage in 2023, working on Assassin’s Creed Shadows and the Claws of Awaji expansion, as well as unannounced projects. Beyond our AAA productions, we also drive technological innovation within the group through our expertise in the Anvil game engine and Ubisoft’s Online Services. We have also established a dedicated R&D division, La Forge, which brings together Ubisoft engineers and academic researchers to collaborate on prototypes that support game development, particularly in the field of AI. Job Description Rendering complex visual effects, such as refractive glass, translucent materials, smoke, and other view-dependent or volumetric phenomena, often require specialized rendering techniques, including dedicated rendering passes or ray tracing. While these methods can produce high-quality results, they can also be computationally expensive, making them challenging to integrate into real-time applications under tight performance constraints. Recent advances in neural rendering, frame generation, and generative models open new possibilities for rethinking how such effects are produced. Rather than explicitly simulating complex light transport, neural models could learn to reconstruct or approximate the final appearance of an object from its rendered representation and surrounding image context. This suggests a new rendering paradigm in which computationally expensive visual effects could be partially replaced by learned image-space transformations. This internship will explore neural compositing, an approach in which selected objects are rendered using simplified geometric or shading proxies and subsequently enhanced by screen-space neural models that predict their final visual appearance. The objective is to investigate whether this approach can reproduce the visual complexity of effects such as refraction, translucency, and volumetric phenomena while reducing the cost of conventional rendering techniques. The work will involve exploring recent developments in neural rendering, neural shading, and frame generation, and investigating their potential application to real-time visual effects. Different neural compositing strategies will be considered through experimental prototypes, with an emphasis on understanding how scene information and rendered inputs can be leveraged to reconstruct complex visual phenomena. The internship is exploratory in nature, with the aim of identifying the strengths and limitations of neural compositing and determining which classes of visual effects are best suited to this approach. The findings will help assess its potential as a complement to conventional rendering techniques and inform future research on the topic. References [1] DLSS 5: Generative Neural Rendering (https://research.nvidia.com/labs/adlr/DLSS5/) [2] Generative AI model for Global Illumination effects (https://gpuopen.com/learn/genai-model-for-global-illumination/) [3] Temporally stable generative illumination with a one-step diffusion model (https://gpuopen.com/learn/temporally-stable-generative-illumination/) [4] An Introduction to Neural Shading (https://research.nvidia.com/labs/rtr/publication/duca2025neural/) Qualifications You are in the final year of an engineering degree or pursuing a research master in computer science or a related field Ability to read and understand research papers Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python Good Knowledge of machine learning and neural networks Good Understanding of image processing or computer vision concepts Basic Understanding of computer graphics and real-time rendering Familiarity with diffusion models or generative models is a plus Good communication skills in English, written and spoken. Additional Information Contract : 6 months internship from March 2027 to September 2027. An internship agreement provided by your school is mandatory. Location : Bordeaux Supervision Antoine Houdard (R&D Scientist) Georges Nader (R&D Scientist)

ABOUT US

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator’s Summer 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading AI photo and video solution for e-commerce, helping businesses sell at first sight.

We’re an international team of 130+, with offices in Paris and New York. We take ownership of what we build, move quickly to learn what works, and speak candidly, united by our ambition to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.




ROLE SUMMARY

We're looking for a Product ML Engineer to join one of our product experience teams — SMB, Scaler or Enterprise — and own the ML side of short, high-impact projects.

You'll work on focused ML problems with a clear product outcome, sometimes fine-tuning one of our models, sometimes integrating the best externally available model, but always choosing the fastest and most effective path to customer value.

You'll bring the technical depth of an Applied Scientist while operating with the pace and pragmatism of a product engineer. You'll own the journey from framing the problem through to shipping, measuring and iterating on the feature in production.

Your time horizon is weeks rather than quarters, and success is measured by what reaches users and the impact it creates.

 - Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production.

 - Move from idea to production quickly. Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact.

 - Stay close to users. Get rapid feedback from customers, monitor how people use what you've shipped and use those insights to drive the next iteration.

 - Balance technical depth with pragmatism. Know when deeper modelling work is necessary and when an existing solution is already good enough to ship.

 - Write production code. Work directly in the product team's codebase rather than operating primarily through research notebooks and experiments.

 - Own quality in production. Build sound evaluations, monitor performance and investigate failures once the feature is live.
   


ABOUT YOU

 - You've shipped ML into production. You have 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping ML-powered products, with strong experience in PyTorch or equivalent frameworks such as TensorFlow or JAX.

 - You have applied-science depth. You can fine-tune vision or diffusion models, design meaningful evaluations and debug training runs when necessary.

 - You're a pragmatic builder. You care about solving the customer's problem rather than proving that your own model is the best approach. You'll happily use an external model, API or existing library when that's the fastest route to value.

 - You're product-minded. You measure success through shipped features, user behaviour and business outcomes rather than papers or benchmarks alone.

 - You're comfortable in production codebases. You can move between experimentation and production engineering, writing maintainable code that lives inside a real product.

 - You have strong ownership. You're comfortable taking an ambiguous ML problem, deciding what matters, choosing an approach and driving it through to production.

 - You iterate quickly. You enjoy short feedback loops and would rather ship something useful, learn from users and improve it than spend months optimising something that hasn't reached production.

 - You're curious and collaborative. You can both explain your expertise and learn from the deep technical expertise around you. You value knowledge sharing and humility.

 - You're fluent in English. French isn't required.

Nice to have: experience shipping generative image models or diffusion models into production; experience evaluating third-party AI APIs against internal alternatives; experience working in a fast-growing startup or directly within a product team.



BENEFITS

items.card: The Role German (C1+) and English required You make sure 10+ software companies get real value out of AI. You work embedded in one of our portfolio platforms. You own the AI Hub for its companies. The AI Hub is our Open WebUI-based AI platform: each company has its own instance in its own tenant, and the data stays in the EU. You keep it running, roll it out, fix what breaks, and help each company's people use it
items.desc: About CHAPTERS Group CHAPTERS Group is a listed German serial acquirer of vertical market software companies. We have grown 10x in the past five years and now own 55+ companies. Each one runs its own business, close to its customers. We help them get stronger without taking over. AI is one of the biggest opportunities we see for them, and it only works if the people in these companies actually use it. Tasks The Role German (C1+) and English required You make sure 10+ software companies get real value out of AI. You work embedded in one of our portfolio platforms. You own the AI Hub for its companies. The AI Hub is our Open WebUI-based AI platform: each company has its own instance in its own tenant, and the data stays in the EU. You keep it running, roll it out, fix what breaks, and help each company's people use it well. You are part of the AI Core Team in the CTO office. You work closely with us: you bring back what you see in the field, test new capabilities, and help shape the platform for all 55+ companies. You are hands-on. You deploy, configure, fix and integrate. Each company also has AI Champions who drive adoption locally. You are their technical backbone: when something needs engineering, you do it, and you make sure the next similar request is faster. What You Will Do Run the AI Hub for 10+ companies: deployments, updates, configuration, SSO with Entra ID, monitoring, backups and incident handling Onboard companies and teams: set up skills, knowledge bases and tools and get each company productive on the Hub Be the technical point of contact: when something breaks or a Champion is stuck, you diagnose and fix it. You document recurring issues so they get solved once. Connect the Hub where a use case needs it: Microsoft 365 / Graph, CRM, ticketing and ERP systems, through tools, MCP servers and REST APIs Turn repeated questions into reusable assets: documentation, templates and short hands-on sessions Work with the AI Core Team: share patterns across companies, test new features, and feed back into the platform roadmap Support our M&A team occasionally (around 10 to 20% of your time) on technical questions, for example assessing the tech and AI stack of acquisition targets What We Are Looking For Required German (C1 or higher) and fluent English. You work with managing directors and non-technical teams in German every day. We cannot make exceptions here. Production operations experience. You have deployed and operated containerised applications in production (Docker, CI/CD, Linux, a major cloud, Azure preferred), and you were responsible when they broke. This usually means 2+ years in a DevOps, platform, SRE or backend role. Python you are comfortable reading, debugging and extending Hands-on with LLMs. You use them seriously in your own work and have built something with them, at work or on the side. You know where they fail. You explain technical things so non-technical people understand them and can act on them. You are comfortable being the go-to technical person for teams that are not technical. Strong signals Enterprise identity: Entra ID, OAuth, SSO Self-hosted LLM platforms such as Open WebUI or LibreChat MCP, tool calling, agent frameworks Infrastructure as Code (Bicep, Terraform) A support, solutions or customer-facing technical role in your background Experience working across several companies, tenants or a group structure This role is not for you if you want to spend most of your time building new AI products from scratch you are looking for ML research or model training you want to work only with engineers and avoid direct contact with business teams Benefits What You Get Real ownership: 10+ companies, one platform, and you are the person who makes AI work there A small team in the CTO office with a direct line to leadership. Decisions get made fast. Impact beyond your platform: what works for your companies becomes the standard for 55+ Permanent full-time position , remote-first, with occasional on-site time Development: talent reviews, events and conferences. We hire people who want to grow with us. How to Apply Send your CV and answer this one question in German , max. 200 words. No cover letter needed. Tell us about a system you ran in production that broke. What happened, what did you do, and what changed afterwards? We are looking forward to your application!

items.desc: Machine Learning Engineer | AI Start-Up | London | £100–120k + Equity The Company Our client is a well-funded AI start-up developing advanced machine learning technology to solve complex, real-world problems across the energy and natural resources sector. Combining probabilistic machine learning, graph-based models and large-scale real-world datasets, their technology helps organisations make better decisions around major infrastructure projects, improving efficiency, reducing costs and supporting the energy transition. With established commercial customers and backing from leading investors, the business is now scaling its core technology and engineering team. They're looking for an experienced Machine Learning Engineer with strong Python, PyTorch and mathematical modelling skills to take ownership of improving and optimising the sophisticated ML models underpinning their technology. Why This Role Stands Out Work with advanced probabilistic ML, graph-based models and PyTorch, tackling complex problems involving real-world data. Focus on model optimisation, accuracy and robustness, with genuine ownership of improving existing machine learning models. Work directly with the CTO and experienced ML researchers, influencing how models are developed and improved. Solve challenging engineering problems involving computational efficiency, statistical performance and production reliability. Join a well-funded AI start-up with established customers, meaningful equity and genuine commercial applications. The Role As a Machine Learning Engineer, you'll take ownership of improving the performance, accuracy and reliability of the machine learning models at the heart of the company's product. The emphasis is on hands-on model development, optimisation and engineering, with dedicated ML researchers developing new modelling techniques and an MLOps Engineer managing infrastructure and deployment. You'll work with sophisticated probabilistic and graph-based models, getting into the underlying mathematics and Python/PyTorch code to identify weaknesses, resolve performance bottlenecks and improve how models behave on complex real-world datasets. This will involve everything from numerical optimisation and inference performance to model calibration, testing and production hardening. Working closely with the CTO and research team, you'll help bridge the gap between advanced ML research and reliable commercial software, with your improvements directly influencing live customer projects. What You'll Be Working On Machine Learning Model Optimisation: Improve the accuracy, statistical performance, robustness and computational efficiency of existing models. Python & PyTorch Engineering: Refactor, debug, test and optimise complex ML code, improving maintainability and production reliability. Probabilistic & Graph-Based ML: Work with sophisticated mathematical models, improving inference, uncertainty calibration and performance. Model Evaluation & Testing: Develop rigorous validation approaches, identify model weaknesses and measure the impact of improvements. Computational Performance: Optimise numerical operations, investigate bottlenecks and improve model efficiency across large, complex datasets. Research to Production: Collaborate with ML researchers to turn advanced modelling techniques into robust, scalable implementations. Your Experience We're looking for a technically strong, hands-on Machine Learning Engineer who enjoys understanding the mathematics behind ML models and improving how they perform. You'll ideally have experience owning production machine learning models, with the ability to work beyond established frameworks and standard hyperparameter tuning to make meaningful improvements to the underlying models. Essential Experience Commercial experience developing, improving and maintaining production machine learning models. Strong Python and PyTorch programming skills, with experience working directly with model implementations. Solid mathematical and statistical foundations, including model evaluation, optimisation and performance analysis. Demonstrable experience improving model accuracy, inference performance, computational efficiency or robustness . Experience debugging, refactoring and testing complex ML code in production environments. Ability to work independently on challenging modelling problems and collaborate effectively with research and engineering teams. Nice to Have Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), graph-based learning or PyTorch Geometric. Probabilistic machine learning, Bayesian modelling or uncertainty quantification. Numerical optimisation, sparse linear algebra or computational performance profiling. Experience with physical-world data , including geospatial, environmental, scientific, sensor or engineering datasets. Experience translating research models into production-quality software. Familiarity with AWS, MLflow, Weights & Biases or similar ML tooling. Master's degree or PhD in Machine Learning, …

items.desc:
Valencia, California
 Digital Signal Processing Engineer 
 Join Advanced Bionics as a Digital Signal Processing Engineer I and help develop the next generation of cochlear implant technology. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will contribute to the design, development, and testing of digital signal processing algorithms and embedded software that help improve how cochlear implant recipients experience sound.
 This is an exciting opportunity for an early-career engineer with a strong foundation in digital signal processing, MATLAB, and embedded programming who wants to apply technical skills to innovative hearing technology.
 Responsibilities:
 Design, develop, and implement digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms supporting advanced sound processing strategies for cochlear implants.
 Develop, test, and optimize embedded software for real-time cochlear implant applications using C and MATLAB.
 Support the integration of software with custom integrated circuits, analog and digital converters, sensors, and other hardware components.
 Analyze DSP algorithm performance, troubleshoot software issues, and contribute to root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
 Develop and maintain software requirements, design specifications, test plans, and verification documentation throughout the product development lifecycle.
 Collaborate with hardware, systems, and test engineering teams to support software integration, debugging, verification, and validation.
 Participate in technical design reviews and contribute to software improvements while following applicable quality and regulatory requirements.
 More about you:
 Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related engineering field required.
 0–2 years of relevant experience in digital signal processing or embedded software development; academic projects, internships, and co-op experience are welcome.
 Strong understanding of digital signal processing theory, signal analysis, and mathematical concepts used in algorithm development.
 Programming experience with MATLAB and foundational knowledge of C for embedded systems.
 Understanding of fixed-point arithmetic, real-time embedded systems, and digital/analog hardware interfaces.
 Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, and documentation skills with the ability to collaborate across engineering disciplines.
 Experience with audio signal processing, low-level programming, C#/.NET, machine learning fundamentals, or medical device development is a plus.
 A minimum of 200Mb/sec download and 10Mb/sec upload speed internet connectivity is required to support any remote/hybrid employee functionality at Sonova.
 Don't meet all the criteria? If you're willing to go all in and learn, we'd love to hear from you!
 We are looking forward to receiving your application via our online job application platform. For this position, only direct applications will be considered. Sonova does not recruit via app, Telegram, carrier pigeon, or any other format that does not include speaking with an actual human. If you are offered a job without speaking with someone, please contact Sonova Human Resources.
 What we offer:
 Medical, dental, and vision coverage*
 Health Savings, Health Reimbursement, Flexible Spending/Dependent Care Accounts
 TeleHealth options
 401(k) plan with company match*
 Company-paid life/AD&D insurance
 Additional supplemental life/AD&D coverage available
 Company-paid Short/Long-Term Disability coverage (STD/LTD)
 STD/LTD buy-ups available
 Accident/Hospital Indemnity coverage
 Legal/ID Theft Assistance
 PTO (or sick and vacation time), floating Diversity Day, and paid holidays*
 Paid parental bonding leave
 Employee Assistance Program (24/7 mental health support hotline, five company-paid counseling sessions, and more)
 Robust internal career growth opportunities
 Tuition reimbursement
 Hearing aid discount for employees and family
 Internal social recognition platform
 D&I-focused: D&I council and employee resource groups
 Plan rules/offerings dependent upon group company/location. 
 This role's annual pay range is between $79,000 and $100,000. Actual compensation will depend on qualifications, experience, skills, and other job-related factors.
 How we work:

items.desc:
About Us
 At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference.
 The Job
 Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.
 In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:
 Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.
 OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.
 Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.
 Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.
 Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.
 Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.
 Qualifications:
 Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.
 Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python
 Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.
 Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.
 Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.
 Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers
 Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.
 Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team.
 Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus.
 Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus.
 Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus.
 What We Offer
 Participation in our warrant program (stock options).
 Work with state-of-the-art technology in a pioneering field.
 A vibrant, learning-focused work environment.
 A role where you can make a significant impact on healthcare delivery.
 Join Our Team
 We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

items.desc: Bouw mee aan het AI-platform achter de oplossingen van morgen AI krijgt een steeds grotere rol binnen Bank Van Breda. Daarom bouwen we aan een centraal en modulair AI-platform dat modellen, agents, kennis, data, integraties en governance samenbrengt in één betrouwbaar fundament. Als AI Engineer werk je mee aan dit platform en ons AI Engineering Framework. Je experimenteert met nieuwe technologie, zet ideeën snel om in werkende pilots en maakt succesvolle oplossingen robuust, veilig en herbruikbaar. Zo help je andere teams om sneller en betrouwbaarder AI-oplossingen te ontwikkelen. Wat wordt jouw uitdaging? Je ontwikkelt herbruikbare AI-capabilities en platformdiensten rond modellen, agents, kennis, evaluatie en monitoring. Je bouwt ons AI Engineering Framework verder uit met onder meer agents, skills, templates, testing en CI/CD. Je zet nieuwe AI-concepten om in werkende pilots en maakt succesvolle oplossingen veilig, schaalbaar en herbruikbaar. Je integreert het AI-platform met Microsoft Azure, API’s, databronnen en bedrijfsapplicaties, met aandacht voor security, privacy en governance. Je experimenteert met nieuwe AI-technologieën, ondersteunt andere engineers en helpt zo onze developer experience continu verbeteren. Wat mag je van ons verwachten? Je krijgt een hands-on sleutelrol in de uitbouw van ons centrale AI-platform. Je krijgt ruimte om nieuwe technologieën te verkennen, ermee te experimenteren én ze daadwerkelijk in te zetten. Je werkt daarbij niet aan één specifieke AI-use case, maar bouwt mee aan een platform waarmee verschillende teams betrouwbare AI-oplossingen kunnen ontwikkelen en inzetten. Niet zomaar een bank. Wel jouw ideale werkplek. Bij Bank Van Breda ervaar je geen doorsnee bedrijfscultuur. Warm, bruisend en met een grote mate van collegialiteit en initiatief. In onze moderne en creatieve werkomgeving neem je als medewerker veel verantwoordelijkheid op. Autonoom werken wordt gestimuleerd, met coaching om jouw groei te ondersteunen. Flexibel werken, leuke après-werk activiteiten, en het vieren van successen maken deel uit van onze bedrijfscultuur. We waarderen jou Dankzij jouw inzet kunnen wij onze missie waarmaken. Daarom bieden we een gepaste verloning aan: Een aantrekkelijk salaris aangevuld met maaltijdcheques, fietsvergoeding en een ruim aantal vakantiedagen. Een bedrijfswagen met tankkaart of wettelijk mobiliteitsbudget. Een flexibel Flexplan waarmee je je 13de maand onder meer kan inzetten voor bikelease, pensioensparen, internet en IT-materiaal. De nieuwste iPhone met abonnement en uitgebreide hospitalisatie-, invaliditeits- en groepsverzekering vanaf je eerste werkdag. Tot 50% thuiswerk, ruime glijtijden en veel autonomie. Deel mee in ons succes via ons winstdeelnameplan en de collectieve bonus gekoppeld aan de NPS-doelstellingen. Volop ruimte om te groeien via coaching en interne en externe opleidingen. Wist je trouwens dat Bank Van Breda in 2026 opnieuw tot de beste werkgevers van het land behoort volgens Great Place To Work , met een mooie 2de plaats? Van kop tot teen. Of het scheelt niet veel. Je hebt een masterdiploma Burgerlijk Ingenieur, Informatica, Industriële Wetenschappen, Handelsingenieur of een vergelijkbare technische richting, of behaalt dit binnenkort. Je hebt een sterke basis in software engineering en affiniteit met generatieve AI, LLM's, agents en AI-platformtechnologie. Je bouwt graag zelf en hebt ervaring met .NET en/of Python, API's, cloudplatformen, containers en CI/CD. Kennis van Microsoft Azure is een sterke troef. Je begrijpt hoe identity, data-integratie, observability en schaalbaarheid samenkomen in een betrouwbaar platform. Je kan snel een prototype realiseren én weet wanneer het tijd is voor standaardisatie, hergebruik en productiebeheer. Je werkt graag samen, deelt kennis en hebt aandacht voor security, privacy, compliance en risicobeheer. Een dosis humor maakt jou compleet. Vink je niet het volledige lijstje af, maar voel je toch een onweerstaanbare kriebel om ons te contacteren? Doen! Want jij verdient meer in je job. Voor functies die vallen onder de regelgeving rond de bankierseed (wet van 22 april 2019), zal in het kader van het selectieproces gevraagd worden om een attest van de FSMA voor te leggen waaruit blijkt dat er geen beroepsverbod van toepassing is. Bank Van Breda en haar medewerkers gaan zorgvuldig om met vertrouwelijke informatie, op een correcte en ethische manier. We koesteren diversiteit en verwelkomen mensen met verschillende achtergronden, ongeacht gender, functiebeperking, afkomst, levensbeschouwing, seksuele oriëntatie of leeftijd.

items.desc: Pourquoi a-t-on besoin de vous ? Would you like to contribute to innovative digital projects supporting the development of sustainable data center solutions? Join the Data Center Team at Saint-Gobain and help transform technical product information into digital construction solutions for international clients and partners. BIM solution development: create, adapt and improve BIM objects and assemblies in Revit for selected construction applications. Data modeling and quantification: structure parameters, manage variants and generate schedules and quantity take-offs. Technical case studies: contribute to solution comparisons between reference construction systems and alternatives, supporting cost, environmental and performance analyses. Atlas knowledge base management: collect, structure and validate technical product and system data, ensuring consistency, traceability and reliability of information. AI-assisted data verification: use approved AI tools to extract information, verify outputs against source documents and identify missing, inconsistent or outdated data. BIM and data integration: connect BIM objects to technical documentation, performance requirements. Ce poste est-il fait pour vous ? You are completing a Master's degree (Bac+5) in civil engineering, construction engineering, digital construction, architecture or a related field and are looking for a final-year internship. Experience with BIM tools and methodologies You understand construction systems and are comfortable reading technical documentation, construction details and product data sheets. You have strong analytical skills and are comfortable working with structured data. You have a professional level of English (minimum B2) You are curious, rigorous, well organized and comfortable working autonomously while collaborating with multiple stakeholders. You are interested in digital innovation, AI applications and sustainable construction solutions for data centers. items.desc: Notre client dans le secteur Banque et finance recherche un/une Administrateur(trice) de plateformes IA & adoption H/F Description de la mission : Contexte Une banque indépendante organisée en cinq lignes métier déploie une stratégie IA en plusieurs phases. D?avril à juillet 2026, 237 collaborateurs ont été formés, Microsoft Copilot a été déployé sur les postes et 103 utilisateurs ont été équipés de Claude (claude.ai, Claude Code et Cowork). Les IA publiques sont filtrées par liste blanche. Le taux d?utilisateurs actifs de Claude atteignait environ 90 % au T2 2026 et une communauté IA interne d?environ 120 personnes se réunit chaque mois. La deuxième phase, lancée en septembre 2026, s?articule autour de l?apprentissage collectif et de la veille, de la constitution de corpus de connaissance, d?agents et de skills par domaine, puis du passage du prompt au processus et au produit. Trois cas candidats sont en test pour une décision Go / No-Go au T1 2027. La gouvernance est partagée avec le RSSI et la Conformité ; la charte d?usage et les procédures restent à formaliser. La migration de Claude Team vers Claude Enterprise est en cours, avec SSO / SCIM via Entra ID, journaux d?audit et environ 200 licences cibles. Microsoft Copilot est également déployé, dont 30 licences Copilot Pro. Le déploiement ciblera d?abord l?équipe Data, puis la banque digitale et la direction des risques. L?équipe Data compte neuf personnes et utilise Microsoft Fabric (Lakehouse, Spark et Power BI), en production depuis un an. Le pilier consacré aux corpus, agents et skills s?appuie sur une base de connaissance centralisée par domaine, issue des sources de vérité (code, dossiers de production et processus métier). Les agents consultent ces corpus et utilisent des skills réutilisables au standard Agent Skills, dans Claude Projects, Cowork ou Claude Code, avec des connexions aux données et outils via des serveurs MCP. Pour l?équipe Data, le corpus sera construit par rétro-documentation de la plateforme, qui comprend environ 30 pipelines et 80 notebooks, ainsi que par la génération de diagrammes et les dossiers de production. Le code est la référence prioritaire et les coûts en tokens doivent être maîtrisés. Les actifs existants comprennent Fabric MCP, un data plugin NL2DAX avec RLS et un agent Corporate Banking en cours de mise en production. Une passerelle MCP interne avec APIM et flux OBO est envisagée. Mission Administrer et animer Claude Enterprise et Microsoft Copilot, piloter les usages et les coûts, favoriser l?adoption et la formation des collaborateurs, et co-construire les premiers agents et skills métiers. La mission est rattachée au Head of Data et s?effectue en lien avec le chef de projet du pilier 2, le RSSI et la Conformité. Principales responsabilités Finaliser la migration de Claude Team vers Claude Enterprise : SSO, provisioning SCIM avec Entra ID, workspaces, rôles, politiques, restriction de la publication publique d?artifacts, sièges, connecteurs, serveurs MCP autorisés et journaux d?audit. Administrer Microsoft 365 / Copilot, notamment les licences Copilot Pro, les paramètres et la console d?administration. Maintenir avec le RSSI la liste blanche des IA autorisées et les paramètres de sécurité, et assurer l?onboarding des utilisateurs. Automatiser le reporting mensuel de l?adoption par plateforme et domaine (utilisateurs actifs, peu actifs et dormants), via l?Admin / Analytics API Anthropic et les exports Copilot ; réattribuer les sièges inactifs. Suivre le pool de tokens, les coûts par usage et les alertes de dépassement. Fournir au COMEX un tableau de bord adoption / coûts, sous Power BI ou sous forme d?application HTML. Déployer le pilier 2 domaine par domaine : onboarding, ateliers, accompagnement des champions et key users, et mesure de l?activation. Structurer les parcours de formation par niveau (découverte, maîtrise, agents et skills), les supports et le kit d?onboarding ; animer la communauté IA mensuelle et la veille. Maintenir le catalogue des cas d?usage et une bibliothèque de projets, prompts et skills ; co-construire les premiers agents et skills métiers. Rédiger et maintenir la charte d?usage IA et les procédures avec le RSSI et la Conformité ; instruire les demandes d?accès aux connecteurs et aux données. Assurer le support utilisateurs de niveaux 1 et 2 et la relation avec Anthropic et Microsoft. Environnement technique Plateformes IA : Claude Enterprise, claude.ai, Claude Projects, Cowork, Claude Code, Microsoft Copilot et Microsoft 365 Identité et administration : Entra ID, SSO, SCIM IA et intégration : prompt engineering, agents, skills, Agent Skills, MCP, APIM, flux OBO Données et reporting : Python, API REST, Excel, Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, Lakehouse, Spark Sécurité et conformité : RGPD, secret bancaire, cloisonnement des données, journalisation, RLS Livrables attendus Plateformes administrées et migration de Claude Enterprise finalisée (SSO / SCIM, politiques et audit). Reporting mensuel …

Vous êtes autonome, rigoureux(se), curieux (e) dynamique et proactif , organisé(e), force de proposition et capable d’animer les priorités d’une petite équipe dans un environnement PME. Vous êtes reconnu pour votre esprit d’équipe et votre sens du service, prenez à cœur les nouveaux challenges avec enthousiasme et détermination, vous avez démontré vos talents en développant des partenariats et faites preuve d’opportunisme pour atteindre vos objectifs. Il percorso formativo sarà incentrato in particolare sui seguenti temi: Personalizzare la didattica con l’Intelligenza Artificiale Progettare attività didattiche con l’Intelligenza Artificiale Scrivere prompt efficaci per l’Intelligenza Artificiale Principali ambiti di intervento Il/la formatore/trice si occuperà di: introdurre i principali strumenti e modelli di Intelligenza Artificiale generativa applicati alla didattica; accompagnare i docenti nella progettazione di attività didattiche supportate dall’IA; mostrare come utilizzare l’Intelligenza Artificiale per personalizzare e differenziare i percorsi di apprendimento in base ai bisogni, ai livelli e alle caratteristiche degli studenti; guidare i partecipanti nella costruzione di prompt chiari, efficaci e strutturati, finalizzati alla produzione di materiali, attività, esercizi, rubriche, verifiche e contenuti didattici; proporre strategie per utilizzare l’IA nella progettazione di unità di apprendimento, lezioni, attività interdisciplinari e percorsi laboratoriali; sviluppare attività pratiche, casi d’uso ed esempi immediatamente trasferibili nella pratica scolastica; supportare i docenti nell’utilizzo dell’IA per la produzione e rielaborazione di testi, immagini, schemi, mappe, materiali semplificati e contenuti personalizzati; approfondire il tema della verifica critica degli output generati dall’IA, con particolare attenzione all’affidabilità delle informazioni e alla qualità dei contenuti prodotti; sensibilizzare i partecipanti sui temi della privacy, della tutela dei dati, dell’etica e dell’utilizzo responsabile dell’Intelligenza Artificiale in ambito scolastico; accompagnare i docenti nella realizzazione di attività e project work da sperimentare concretamente in classe. items.desc: Location Milan, Lombardy, Italy Job ID R-264429 Date posted 17/11/2026 Are you ready to turn breakthrough CAR-T science into real outcomes for patients across Italy? As a Clinical Research Associate focused on CAR-T studies, you will be the driving force that transforms cutting-edge cell therapy into high-quality, inspection-ready execution at site level. You will join a dedicated team working across a fast-moving, innovative pipeline. In close collaboration with local study leaders, medical colleagues and fellow CRAs, you will ensure that every assigned site is set up, monitored and closed with precision—so patients can access novel therapies sooner. Imagine seeing the impact of your site leadership reflected in safer, faster, more reliable study delivery. Accountabilities Site Start-up and Activation: Prepare, initiate and activate assigned sites, ensuring compliance with AstraZeneca procedures, ICH-GCP and local regulations, and delivering to agreed commitments and timelines. Investigator Identification and Engagement: Contribute to investigator selection; perform Site Qualification Visits and manage document collection, preparation, review and tracking for submissions throughout the study lifecycle. Training and Site Readiness: Train, support and advise investigators and site staff on study requirements, including Risk Based Quality Management principles, to embed quality at source and strengthen patient safety. Monitoring Excellence: Conduct remote and onsite monitoring visits per the study-specific Monitoring Plan; perform Source Data Review, Case Report Form review and Source Data Verification; complete monitoring reports and follow-up letters within required timelines. Performance and Issue Management : Track recruitment, site quality and performance; proactively identify issues, drive timely resolution and escalate as appropriate; adapt monitoring intensity via regular risk assessments. Data Integrity and Safety Reporting: Ensure timely data entry and query resolution; manage accurate and prompt reporting and follow-up of Serious Adverse Events; maintain data systems up to date according to required timelines. Supply and Accountability Stewardship: Oversee study and drug supplies, drug accountability and, where applicable, preparation for drug destruction in alignment with protocol and procedural requirements. Inspection Readiness and Compliance: Support sites to maintain inspection-ready Investigator Site Files; coordinate audit and inspection activities with study leadership; ensure essential documents are collected, uploaded and archived on time. Cross-functional Collaboration : Actively participate in Local Study Team meetings and contribute to national investigator meetings; partner with Medical Science Liaisons as directed; share site insights to elevate study delivery. Governance and Responsibility: Manage all activities in line with company values, code of conduct, internal procedures and relevant legislation related to people, finance, technology, security and Safety, Health and Environment. Essential Skills/Experience Excellent knowledge of international guidelines ICH-GCP, basic knowledge of GMP/GDP. Excellent attention to details Good written and verbal communication skills Good collaboration and interpersonal skills Good negotiation and problem solving skills Ability to travel nationally/internationally as required Valid driving license Desirable Skills/Experience Scientific Degree equivalent degree Experience on management of CAR-T Cell Therapy studies Demonstrated project management skills including scope, budget, timeline, resource management and use of associated tools. Knowledge of R&D ways of working Ability to effectively work with External Service Providers Ability to look for and champion more efficient and effective methods/processes We carefully consider all applications, including those from candidates eligible under Italian Protected Categories legislation (Art. 1 and Art. 18, L. 68/99).
