items.desc: Join Instil's agentic product development team in 2027 and learn to build software the way it will be built in the agentic age: engineers owning the problem, the architecture and the key decisions, with AI agents accelerating everything in between. About the role At Instil, agentic product engineering is how we deliver. Our teams work alongside an agentic workforce that generates requirements, builds across parallel workstreams, runs continuous quality and security checks or monitoring systems in production. The result is software that ships faster, with lower risk. The agents do a lot, but people stay firmly in charge - orchestrating. We own the problem, the architecture and the key decisions. That is the skill set we will help you build from day one. As a graduate you will join a delivery team working on real client products for organisations ranging from ambitious start-ups to global brands. You will learn the fundamentals of great software engineering and, alongside them, how to direct, review and get the best out of AI agents. What you'll do You will work across our full delivery lifecycle, supported by experienced engineers and mentors. Plan: take part in discovery with clients, help shape requirements and use agents to turn ideas into rapid prototypes and a backlog ready to build. Build: write, review and test production code, directing agents across parallel workstreams and learning to judge when their output is right and when it is not. Ship: help release software to production, design for observability and use agents to monitor systems, analyse issues and drive improvements. Along the way you will: Learn to make sound technical decisions and explain them clearly Build good habits in security, testing and code quality, so speed never comes at the cost of trust Work directly with clients and colleagues as part of a collaborative, multi-disciplinary team Share what you learn, as our ways of working with agents are evolving all the time What we're looking for We care more about how you think than what you already know. Essential: A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related discipline Solid programming fundamentals in at least one modern language, such as TypeScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, or C# Hands-on experience with AI coding tools, Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor or similar, through projects, hackathons or coursework Strong problem-solving skills and the judgement to question an answer rather than simply accept it Clear communication skills and an enjoyment of working in a team Nice to have: Side projects, open source contributions or a portfolio that shows what you have built An interest in cloud platforms, security or web and mobile development What you'll get A structured graduate programme combining engineering fundamentals with hands-on training in agentic development A mentor and regular feedback, with a clear path to progress Real client work from your first months, not just internal projects Access to the latest AI tools and the time to learn them properly A collaborative culture where people share knowledge openly Graduate details Start date: September 2027 Location: Belfast Working pattern: Hybrid – at least 3 days per week in our Belfast office Right to work: Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK Why Join Instil? At Instil, we believe great work starts with happy, motivated people. That’s why we’ve built a benefits package that supports your wellbeing, growth, and life outside of work, because when you thrive, so do we. Recognition That Matters: A discretionary annual performance bonus that rewards your impact and contribution to our success. Flexibility Built In: Flexible working arrangements and summer hours, because life isn’t 9 to 5, and balance matters. Financial Security: A highly competitive pension scheme with generous employer contributions, private healthcare, and life assurance for peace of mind. Health & Wellbeing: Employee Assistance Programme, mental health support, cycle-to-work scheme, and regular social events to keep our culture vibrant. Time to Recharge: 35 days holiday, enhanced maternity pay, and family-first policies so you can focus on what matters most. Learning Never Stops: From courses to certifications, we’ll invest in your development so you can keep growing and shaping what’s next. Community & Culture: Opportunities to volunteer, give back, and be part of initiatives that make Instil a truly inclusive and connected workplace. And that’s just the start, drop us a note to find out more. Please note: We offer flexible hybrid working, but candidates should be based in Northern Ireland and able to attend our Belfast office when required. items.title: AI Native Creative Strategist - EdTech (French fluent )
items.card: YOUR MISSION You lead the Content Factory not by management, but with creativity. Your goal is to produce content that is so good, unique, and aligned with our values that people would cry if they had to unsubscribe. In a classic content team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the volume, you design the machine, set the bar and make the calls. Humans do what no machine can:
items.desc: What if your next playground was to build a global, iconic Brand, with a creative machine that never sleeps, and compounds? Then you’ll love this. We’re not looking for a "Social Media Manager" to follow a calendar. We’re looking for an AI-native Creative Strategist (Brand & Content). Someone who understands that to win today, you don’t just need "content", you need a Movement. This isn’t another content job. Most content teams use AI to write captions faster. That’s the 99%. We want to be in the 0.1%: a media where AI runs the creative loop, from the signal to the hook, the cut, the post and the lesson. Every day, on every platform, in French and in English. You bring the taste. The machine you build brings the scale. Here’s the bet: a company that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. We aim for $10M in revenue with 10 people, each of them running a dozen agents. WHAT AI-NATIVE CONTENT MEANS AT PARADOX Paradoxically, the more AI runs our content, the more human it has to feel. AI doesn’t make more of what everyone makes. It makes more of what only we can make. Our creative machine has to be able to: 1. Read the signals. Comments, DMs, retention graphs, saves, shares, search trends, objections from sales calls, and what the best creators and advertisers in the world are publishing right now. 2. Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, years of interviews, lives and courses, member stories, and every past post with what it taught us, in one shared company brain. 3. Generate in our voice. Hooks, scripts, shorts, carousels, cuts, thumbnails and captions, in French and in English. 4. Ship. Format, schedule, publish and answer, on every platform. 5. Measure with real KPIs. Retention, shares, saves, follower growth, and the followers who become leads and members. Not likes. 6. Learn and loop on its own. Double down on what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and start the next cycle without waiting for a meeting. This is already real. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content and wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations. And our product is AI-native too: Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day. OUR MISSION At Paradox, we are convinced that greatness is trainable, and we believe self-help is broken. Most learning platforms are used the same way: consuming generic theories, getting quick highs, ending with no real change. People deserve more: a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them. That’s why we want to empower people at scale, by leveraging cutting edge technologies like AI, and crafting user experiences with outstanding aesthetics. We do that by merging: Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors) Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals) Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys) To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS. Short history Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world. YOUR MISSION You lead the Content Factory not by management, but with creativity. Your goal is to produce content that is so good, unique, and aligned with our values that people would cry if they had to unsubscribe. In a classic content team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the volume, you design the machine, set the bar and make the calls. Humans do what no machine can: taste. YOUR 5 MAIN MISSIONS 1. Architect the "Dual-Brand" Strategy Build a symbiotic strategy where David Laroche’s personal brand and Paradox’s company brand reinforce each other without cannibalization. Implement radical new formats (documentaries, conceptual shorts) that shatter the boring codes of the "Self-Help" industry. Define distinct, sharp editorial lines for each platform: Depth & Search for YouTube, Aesthetic & Vibe for Instagram, and Authority & Authenticity for LinkedIn. The old way: a strategy deck written once a year, and a calendar filled by habit. At Paradox: agents watch every platform, every competitor and every comment continuously. They tell you which angle is rising, which format is tiring and which story our audience asks for. The strategy updates every week, on evidence. 2. Radical Concepting & End-to-End Delivery Take responsibility for the entire production chain from hooks to storyboarding the narrative, and ensuring the final cut matches the vision. Own the packaging: titles, thumbnails and the first 3 seconds. You test variants every week and know your click-through and retention numbers by heart. Deliver what you pitch. The old way: one shoot becomes one video and a handful of posts. At Paradox: one shoot, one live or one interview becomes dozens of hooks, shorts, carousels …

items.desc: ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE : École du ministère en charge de l'industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines- Télécom, 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l'avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses 4 missions - former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l'innovation - en un cercle vertueux et porteur d'innovation. Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche la place IMT Mines Albi comme école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT, à savoir l’industrie du futur responsable, l’énergie, économie circulaire et société ainsi que l’ingénierie, santé et bien-être. IMT Mines Albi s‘est dotée en 2023 et pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en 7 grandes actions, répondant ainsi aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT à laquelle elle appartient. Ce poste, ouvert au sein d’IMT Mines Albi, est rattaché au Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) qui compte à ce jour environ 70 personnes. Le centre s’intéresse à la cinétique des organisations et au développement de solutions d’aide à la décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs et incertains. Ceci est mis en pratique par la représentation, la modélisation et l’analyse des données de ces organisations afin de formaliser de la connaissance conduisant à la prise de décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs, incertains et/ou perturbés. Le CGI est structuré selon quatre axes de recherche appliquée : Axe FLOWS : Systèmes logistiques flexibles pour un monde durable ; Axe DISCS : Systèmes numériques pour la gestion des crises et la sécurité ; Axe WHOPS : Systèmes organisationnels pour la santé et le bien-être ; Axe TRACE : Résilience territoriale, agilité et économie circulaire. Huit expertises scientifiques et techniques sont au cœur de ces axes de recherche : Ingénierie systèmes, Ingénierie des modèles, Théorie de la décision, Recherche opérationnelle, Technologies immersives, IA générative, IA symbolique, et IA connexionniste. Les chercheurs et ingénieurs du CGI exploitent et contribuent particulièrement aux paradigmes scientifiques suivants pour réaliser les projets de recherche ou formation : l’Internet Physique, la Physique des Décisions, les Jumeaux Numériques Organisationnels. Le poste à pourvoir concerne l'un des projets de recherche de l'axe WHOPS. Le but de ce projet est de répondre à un besoin exprimé par l'Agence Régionale de Santé (ARS) et un hôpital de la région parisienne. La personne recrutée sera intégrée à une équipe de chercheurs en ingénierie organisationnelle pour la santé, ce qui garantira un accompagnement visant une montée en régime rapide et un suivi régulier des activités de l'ingénieur(e) recruté(e). DESCRIPTION DU POSTE : Le contexte général du projet concerne le pilotage des capacités hospitalières et l'anticipation des tensions sur l'offre de soins. Il s'agit d'un enjeu majeur pour les établissements de santé, les institutions en charge de la planification de l'offre de soins, et plus largement, pour l'ensemble des professionnels impliqués dans l'orientation des patients. L'objectif général du projet est de développer et expérimenter, en s'appuyant sur des données réelles provenant du système d'information d'un hôpital, des outils innovants d'analyse et de prévision-prédiction de l'activité hospitalière, essentiels pour améliorer l'anticipation et le pilotage des capacités (ressources humaines et lits). Parmi les outils et solutions envisagés, un intérêt particulier porte sur les principes du jumeau numérique asynchrone permettant l'analyse rétrospective des parcours patients et la simulation "in silico" de scénarios prospectifs. D'autres outils et techniques, concurrents ou complémentaires, notamment à base de projections statistiques et d'intelligence artificielle, devront aussi être explorés. De manière générale, l'ingénieur(e) de recherche recruté(e) interviendra sur les développements et les travaux de recherche visant l'objectif général du projet. Plus précisément, la mission consiste à : Analyser les données associées aux flux de patients et les déterminants organisationnels et médicaux influençant les durées de séjour et l'occupation des lits ; Développer des modèles permettant d'estimer et d'anticiper l'évolution des taux d'occupation des capacités hospitalières ; Développer des outils d'aide à la décision destinés aux professionnels hospitaliers et aux acteurs de la régulation ; Produire une méthodologie reproductible et transférable à d'autres établissements ou territoires de soins ; Documenter tous les travaux de développement dans des dossiers techniques à destination d'autres développeurs. Rédiger des notices d'utilisation pour les utilisateurs …

items.desc: Grant Writer (f/m/x) in Bioengineering 103053 Full time 39 hrs./week Neuherberg near Munich At Helmholtz Munich, we develop groundbreaking solutions for a healthier society in a rapidly changing world. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation. Through strong partnerships, we accelerate the transfer of new ideas from the lab to real-life applications, improving lives. Your work provides the foundation for scientific discoveries with real impact, shaping the future of health. The at Helmholtz Munich and the Chair of Biological Imaging (CBI) at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) form one of Europe's leading centers for biomedical imaging and sensing innovation. Our mission is to create transformative technologies that reveal previously inaccessible biological information and accelerate breakthroughs in medicine, biology, and environmental health. Our interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers from more than 25 countries develops technologies that bridge fundamental research, clinical translation, and real-world healthcare impact. With state-of-the-art infrastructure, strong industrial partnerships, and a proven track record of innovation, IBMI offers an exceptional environment for motivated professionals seeking to support research at the forefront of bioengineering. We are seeking a highly qualified and motivated Grant Writer (f/m/x) to streamline our grant-writing process and support scientists of all career stages in preparing proposals for third-party funding. Working closely with our researchers, you will help develop, write, and compile compelling applications to national and international funding agencies. As part of the IBMI science management team , you will work at the interface between researchers, the central administrations of Helmholtz Munich and TUM, external partners, and funding agencies. Your contribution will give our scientists room to focus their creative potential on developing the imaging and sensing technologies of tomorrow. Your tasks Lead funding applications to national and international funding agencies, from first idea to submission. Write and refine proposals together with our scientists, so that complex research convinces reviewers. Coordinate submissions and post-award preparations with researchers, the administrations of Helmholtz Munich and the Technical University of Munich, partners, and funders. Spot new funding opportunities and keep track of funding programs and their requirements. Edit and polish scientific texts for different audiences, e.g. award nominations, journal manuscripts, ethics applications for clinical studies, reports, and communication content. Your profile A Master Degree or PhD in natural sciences, electrical engineering, physics, optics, medical technology, or biomedical computing. You have co-written or led funding proposals for competitive funding, peer-reviewed publications and reviews, and articles for the general public in English. Excellent ability to analyze complex research projects and present them clearly to different audiences. Strong organizational and management skills, combined with the ability to motivate and inspire colleagues, as well as proficiency in business English. Desirable qualifications Fluency in written and spoken German. You have worked in a business, industry, or partnership setting (e.g. technology transfer, industry collaborations). This position offers the opportunity to advance your career at the intersection of science and administration, working with experienced science managers and researchers in a highly international, multidisciplinary environment. If you fulfill all the requirements, you may be eligible for a salary grade of up to E 13. Social benefits are based on the Collective Wage Agreement for Public-Sector Employees (TVöD). The position has an (initial) fixed term of 2 years but may be extended under certain circumstances. Managing Director Mike Frieser: „We believe that diversity is the key to groundbreaking research and innovative solutions. Our flexible working models and remote options create a supportive environment for balancing work and family life. For us, contributing to a healthier society in such an inspiring workplace is truly meaningful.“ Benefits Work-Life-Balance: Flexible working hours and flexi-time models Personal Development: Continuous education and training Recreation: 30 days annual leave, flexi days, plus public holidays Family Support: child care, holiday care, care for the elderly Health Promotion: Sports, company doctor, mental health initiatives Retirement Provision: Company pension plan Interested in applying? If you have any questions, feel free to contact Dr. Andreas Hillmair, andreas.hillmair@helmholtz-munich.de, who will be happy to help. Our recruiting is decentralized - your application will be reviewed directly by the specialist department in which you could work in the future. Please send your application only via our online application tool and …

items.title: AI Native Creative Strategist - EdTech (French fluent )
items.card: YOUR MISSION You lead the Content Factory not by management, but with creativity. Your goal is to produce content that is so good, unique, and aligned with our values that people would cry if they had to unsubscribe. In a classic content team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the volume, you design the machine, set the bar and make the calls. Humans do what no machine can:
items.desc: What if your next playground was to build a global, iconic Brand, with a creative machine that never sleeps, and compounds? Then you’ll love this. We’re not looking for a "Social Media Manager" to follow a calendar. We’re looking for an AI-native Creative Strategist (Brand & Content). Someone who understands that to win today, you don’t just need "content", you need a Movement. This isn’t another content job. Most content teams use AI to write captions faster. That’s the 99%. We want to be in the 0.1%: a media where AI runs the creative loop, from the signal to the hook, the cut, the post and the lesson. Every day, on every platform, in French and in English. You bring the taste. The machine you build brings the scale. Here’s the bet: a company that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. We aim for $10M in revenue with 10 people, each of them running a dozen agents. WHAT AI-NATIVE CONTENT MEANS AT PARADOX Paradoxically, the more AI runs our content, the more human it has to feel. AI doesn’t make more of what everyone makes. It makes more of what only we can make. Our creative machine has to be able to: 1. Read the signals. Comments, DMs, retention graphs, saves, shares, search trends, objections from sales calls, and what the best creators and advertisers in the world are publishing right now. 2. Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, years of interviews, lives and courses, member stories, and every past post with what it taught us, in one shared company brain. 3. Generate in our voice. Hooks, scripts, shorts, carousels, cuts, thumbnails and captions, in French and in English. 4. Ship. Format, schedule, publish and answer, on every platform. 5. Measure with real KPIs. Retention, shares, saves, follower growth, and the followers who become leads and members. Not likes. 6. Learn and loop on its own. Double down on what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and start the next cycle without waiting for a meeting. This is already real. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content and wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations. And our product is AI-native too: Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day. OUR MISSION At Paradox, we are convinced that greatness is trainable, and we believe self-help is broken. Most learning platforms are used the same way: consuming generic theories, getting quick highs, ending with no real change. People deserve more: a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them. That’s why we want to empower people at scale, by leveraging cutting edge technologies like AI, and crafting user experiences with outstanding aesthetics. We do that by merging: Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors) Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals) Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys) To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS. Short history Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world. YOUR MISSION You lead the Content Factory not by management, but with creativity. Your goal is to produce content that is so good, unique, and aligned with our values that people would cry if they had to unsubscribe. In a classic content team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the volume, you design the machine, set the bar and make the calls. Humans do what no machine can: taste. YOUR 5 MAIN MISSIONS 1. Architect the "Dual-Brand" Strategy Build a symbiotic strategy where David Laroche’s personal brand and Paradox’s company brand reinforce each other without cannibalization. Implement radical new formats (documentaries, conceptual shorts) that shatter the boring codes of the "Self-Help" industry. Define distinct, sharp editorial lines for each platform: Depth & Search for YouTube, Aesthetic & Vibe for Instagram, and Authority & Authenticity for LinkedIn. The old way: a strategy deck written once a year, and a calendar filled by habit. At Paradox: agents watch every platform, every competitor and every comment continuously. They tell you which angle is rising, which format is tiring and which story our audience asks for. The strategy updates every week, on evidence. 2. Radical Concepting & End-to-End Delivery Take responsibility for the entire production chain from hooks to storyboarding the narrative, and ensuring the final cut matches the vision. Own the packaging: titles, thumbnails and the first 3 seconds. You test variants every week and know your click-through and retention numbers by heart. Deliver what you pitch. The old way: one shoot becomes one video and a handful of posts. At Paradox: one shoot, one live or one interview becomes dozens of hooks, shorts, carousels …

items.desc: Aquaculture Technician (Fish Platform) Localização: Champalimaud Centre for The Unknown Entidade Empregadora: Champalimaud Foundation Regime: Tempo Inteiro Posição: Plataformas Científicas e Tecnológicas Início da Candidatura: 16 Nov. 2026 Champalimaud Foundation (Fundação D. Anna de Sommer Champalimaud e Dr. Carlos Montez Champalimaud), a private, non-profit research institution in Lisbon, Portugal, is looking for an Aquaculture Technician to join our team at the Champalimaud Research Program - Fish Platform. This is a full-time position requiring teamwork, multitasking, effective task prioritisation, attention to details and accurate record keeping. The postholder will participate in an on-call rota and adjust daily duties to meet the needs of the Platform. The Fish Platform (FP), established in 2011, provides a state-of-the-art facility for the housing and breeding of fish models, ensuring high standards of health and welfare. It continuously develops and refines husbandry, housing, and welfare practices, as well as related technologies. The Platform offers a comprehensive range of services, including complex line maintenance, the generation of transgenic and gene-edited fish, and assisted reproduction. Through close collaboration with researchers, the Platform adapts its services to the needs of the scientific community. Its focus on scientific and technological innovation has contributed to numerous collaborative research projects, a patent, and more than ten peer-reviewed publications. The FP also provides consultancy on zebrafish facility design and management, as well as tailored training and technology transfer. The selected candidate will: We are seeking a highly motivated technician to support the operations and services of the Champalimaud Fish Platform. The selected candidate will join a dynamic, collaborative team responsible for maintaining high scientific and animal welfare standards. In addition to routine technical duties, the role may involve research and development activities to improve existing fish models, refine husbandry and reproductive techniques, and develop new models and technologies. Responsibilities will include: Maintenance of recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) for multiple freshwater fish species and associated equipment. Water quality monitoring and troubleshooting. Maintenance of live feed cultures. Fish feeding, breeding, housing, and embryo care. Larval rearing. Fish health monitoring. Accurate record keeping. Technical assistance to researchers. Participation in a weekend rota and adaptation of daily duties to the operational needs of the Platform. Other tasks relevant to the maintenance and development of the Platform ́s scientific and animal welfare standards. The ideal candidate will be organised, responsible, committed, and a team player, with strong logical thinking skills, attention to detail, and the ability to prioritise tasks and multitask effectively. Employer: Champalimaud Foundation Number and type of fellowships or contracts to be awarded: one (1) fellowship Application closing date: until position is filled Expected position starting date: 01 December 2026 Required Education Level: BSc or MSc Requirements Research Field: Biological sciences Education Level: Bachelor Degree or equivalent Skills/Qualifications Minimum qualifications: Degree in Aquaculture, Marine Biology or other relevant Life and/or Health Sciences. Specific Requirements: Essential skills: Strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and accurate record keeping. Ability to prioritise tasks, multitask, and adapt to changing operational needs. Strong sense of responsibility and commitment. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team. Strong logical thinking and problem-solving skills. Desirable skills that will also be considered: Experience with recirculating aquaculture systems Personal license for animal care, experimentation and euthanasia Prior experience in a research environment Languages: English, Excellent Benefits Remuneration package commensurate with skills, qualifications and experience. Full immersion into a research excellence ecosystem with highly motivated researchers, supported by state-of-the-art technology and continuous development opportunities. Initial duration: 6 months, with possibility of renewal for additional periods, without limit of renewals. Eligibility criteria National, Foreign or Stateless candidate(s) who hold a BSc or MSc degree in Aquaculture, Marine Biology or other related scientific areas and a scientific and professional curriculum that reveals a profile appropriate to the activity to be developed. Selection process Candidates will be screened to determine eligibility based on minimum qualifications listed in call. Candidates meeting minimum requirements will be scored according to the required application materials: CV: 70% weighting, Motivation letter 30%. Answers to the optional challenge questions, if provided, may be considered …

items.desc: Applications are invited for a Clinical Scientist to join the dynamic Radiotherapy Physics group at The Christie. The successful applicant will ideally be HCPC registered, but applications from final-year STP trainees will also be considered. The successful applicant will join a team of Clinical Scientists providing a full range of scientific and technical support to the radiotherapy service in at least two of the following areas as part of the routine service: dosimetry, brachytherapy, treatment planning, scientific computing. The post holder will be expected to work towards MPE RPA2000 certification. The successful applicant will work with a wide range of radiotherapy IT systems including treatment planning systems (RayStation, Monaco, Oncentra etc.), oncology management systems (Mosaiq), and auto-contouring packages including those based on deep-learning models (Limbus, RayStation, ProKnow). Clinical scientists in the team are encouraged to present new ideas to improve the service and will be supported to develop them by the whole team. Clinical work in RT physics The successful candidate will contribute to at least 2 of the following areas: the treatment planning service including treatment planning and checking, and advising the multi-disciplinary team on issues relating to clinical treatment plans. the dosimetry service including quality control, commissioning of new equipment, and responding to issues and/or faults. the brachytherapy service including treatment planning, checking, and delivery. Quality control and machine commissioning. the scientific computing service including supporting automation projects, compliance with regulation and guidance and development of artificial intelligence tools. Management The successful candidate may be required to contribute to both clinical audit and internal quality system audits. Research & Development The successful candidate will be expected to take an active role in research and development work, in line with the department objectives. Major departmental priorities include the transfer of all treatment planning activities to the RayStation TPS, the on-going replacement of linear accelerators and the commissioning of daily on-line adaptive radiotherapy. Teaching & training The role may involve specialist teaching on MSc courses in collaboration with the University of Manchester. The Christie is one of Europe’s leading cancer centres, looking after more than 64,000 patients a year. We are based in Manchester and serve a population of 3.2 million across Greater Manchester & Cheshire, but as a national specialist around 25% patients are referred to us from other parts of the country. items.desc: We are pleased to offer a 12-month Post-CCT Fellowship in Robotic Colorectal Surgery at West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, fully funded by the Intuitive Foundation. The post is ideal for newly accredited colorectal surgeons (CCT or equivalent) who want to build expertise in robotic colorectal surgery in a high-volume NHS teaching unit. Our multi-platform robotic service has three da Vinci systems: the dV5 for complex elective resections, the Xi for day-case and short-stay surgery at St Albans City Hospital, and the X for emergency robotic surgery. You will receive structured mentorship from accredited robotic consultants, supervised console training, simulation and high-volume operating. Core hours are Monday to Friday, plus supervised consultant-level emergency robotic on-call equivalent to four weekends per year. Full details will be discussed at interview. You will operate on consultant-supervised robotic colorectal lists across the dV5, Xi and X platforms, including right and left-sided resections, TME and emergency robotic surgery, and undertake day-case robotic surgery at St Albans City Hospital. You will also attend cancer clinic and the colorectal MDT, and contribute to teaching, audit, governance and research. Lower GI endoscopy lists are available. We are looking for a surgeon on, or within 6 months of joining, the GMC Specialist Register in General Surgery, with comprehensive knowledge of colorectal and general surgical disorders, strong general surgical management skills and a commitment to teaching. Robotic training or experience, JAG accreditation in lower GI endoscopy, research publications and current ATLS are desirable. With a new hospital planned for Watford, work underway to update theatres at St Albans City Hospital and plans for a neighbourhood healthcare centre in Hemel Hempstead, this is an exciting time to join us. We are building on the success of our award-winning virtual hospital and re-imagining models of care, working closely with partners and making the most of advances in digital healthcare. Staff wellbeing and development are a priority, as is the role of innovation in improving clinical care, outcomes and patient experience. Our vision is Excellent patient care, together and our values are to be empowered, compassionate, professional and inclusive. They capture an important balance across what we must all do as individuals and to support others. We offer a variety of flexible working options as we recognise the importance of a good work life balance. www.westhertshospitals.nhs.uk/flexibleworking If you have a disability or long-term health condition and require support or guidance please contact westherts.recruitment@nhs.net If you are a Service Leaver, Veteran, Military Reserve, Cadet Force Adult Volunteer, or partner/spouse of those serving please tick "Member of the Armed Forces Community" on the application form. We reserve the right to close this advert early due to the volume of applicants. Please apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. If you do not hear back within 3 weeks of your application, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion. Provisional weekly job plan: Monday: cancer clinic (AM), colorectal MDT (PM) Tuesday to Thursday: robotic colorectal operating lists Friday: GI X-ray meeting (AM), academic day Lower GI endoscopy lists are also available. The fellow will not join the general surgical 1:12 on-call rota, but will undertake consultant-level on-call for emergency robotic colorectal surgery (four weekends per year) under direct supervision of the on-call consultant. Elective activity is cancelled during on-call, post-on-call and Colorectal Surgeon of the Week duties. The fellow will teach and supervise registrars, foundation doctors and medical students, and work closely with consultant colleagues, theatres, nursing and CNS teams, the MDT, gastroenterology and endoscopy. Cross-site working across Watford, St Albans and Hemel Hempstead is reflected in the job plan.

A PhD in psychology, public health or a related applied health discipline, with relevant professional accreditation or equivalent experience A sustained track record of excellence in applied public health and behavioural science research Demonstrable academic leadership and management experience, including line management and strategic decision-making Experience of teaching, assessing and examining undergraduate students in clinical, healthcare or academic settings What we can offer in return: As a member of our team, you can expect a friendly, open and collaborative working environment and support in your development and wellbeing. items.desc: Introduction The Reuse & Repair Analytics team in Veldhoven helps ASML make informed decisions about returned machine parts by analyzing repair potential, reuse opportunities, and operational performance. As the team continues to grow, we are exploring how agentic AI can support in business analytics, improve decision-making, and increase automation. In this internship, you will help identify analytical AI use cases and turn them into solutions that create measurable value for users. Your work will support the adoption of new technologies and contribute to more efficient ways of working across the organization. Your assignment As an AI Analytics intern, you will help the team explore, validate, and demonstrate how agentic AI can support business analyses within the Reuse & Repair domain. You will work closely with business analysts and business stakeholders to understand user needs and develop solutions that improve business insights and business performance. You will also help make these solutions accessible by creating supporting materials and best practices. Your main responsibilities will be: Identify opportunities where AI agents can analyse and support decision-making. Translate user needs into clear and structured requirements for AI solutions. Develop and test AI agent prototypes using Genie in MS Azure. Evaluate results and collect user feedback to improve solutions. Create documentation, onboarding materials, demonstrations, and user guidance. Monitor solution performance through data analysis and reporting. Collaborate with analytics professionals and business stakeholders to support adoption. This is a bachelor’s or master’s non-thesis internship for minimum 5 months, minimum 4 days per week (3 days on-site). The start date of this internship is as of February 2027. Your profile To be suitable for the internship, you: Are enrolled in a bachelor’s degree or master’s degree in data science, artificial intelligence, computer science, business analytics, or a related field. Have a strong interest in analytics, artificial intelligence, automation, and digital innovation. Have basic programming experience with Python or low-code development platforms. Are analytical and able to use data to evaluate outcomes and identify improvements. Are a clear communicator who can explain technical concepts in simple language. Are proactive and enjoy collaborating with different stakeholders. Important application tip: For this internship, clear communication is just as important as technical skills. We encourage you to describe your experience in straightforward language and provide practical examples of your work. Your ability to explain complex topics clearly will be part of the selection process. Other requirements you need to meet: You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship; If you are a non-EU citizen, studying in the Netherlands, your university is willing to sign the documents relevant for doing an internship (i.e., Nuffic agreement); You attach your cover letter with a clear motivation on why you are interested in this internship assignment in particular; You need to be located in the Netherlands to be perform your internship. In case you are currently living/studying outside of the Netherlands, your application shows the willingness to relocate. items.card: About the role We are looking for a Threat Hunter to join our Cyber Defense Operation Center. You will proactively search across our IT, cloud, manufacturing and connected-vehicle environments for threats that may not be identified by existing detection rules. This role combines traditional threat hunting with security data analytics, machine learning, graph analytics and AI-assisted investigation . You will work
items.desc: Reports to: Tech Lead, Cyber Defense Operation Center About the role We are looking for a Threat Hunter to join our Cyber Defense Operation Center. You will proactively search across our IT, cloud, manufacturing and connected-vehicle environments for threats that may not be identified by existing detection rules. This role combines traditional threat hunting with security data analytics, machine learning, graph analytics and AI-assisted investigation . You will work with large volumes of security telemetry, develop and test hunting hypotheses, investigate suspicious behaviour and turn successful hunts into stronger detections and repeatable hunting methods. We are looking for someone who already has some hands-on experience in cybersecurity, threat detection, SOC operations, security analytics or a related field , and who wants to develop deeper expertise in advanced threat hunting. What you will do Threat hunting and investigation Develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunts across IT, cloud, manufacturing/OT and connected-vehicle environments. Use MITRE ATT&CK to understand attacker behaviour and structure hunting activities. Investigate suspicious or unusual activity, gather evidence and escalate confirmed threats to the incident response team. Document hunts clearly so that queries, methods and findings can be reviewed and reused. Turn successful hunting techniques into new detection rules, scheduled queries or automated hunting jobs. Machine learning and advanced analytics Apply machine learning techniques such as anomaly detection, clustering, rare-event analysis and user/entity behaviour analytics to security data. Help prepare datasets and develop meaningful features from security telemetry. Monitor models and investigate data drift, unexpected results or changes in performance. Interpret analytical results and explain how they contribute to an investigation. Security data and detection Query our security data lake to analyse large volumes of historical and near-real-time security telemetry. Correlate information across endpoints, networks, identities, cloud platforms and other security data sources. Identify gaps in telemetry, data quality or detection coverage. Develop reusable queries and contribute to production detection content. Graph analytics and attack paths Use graph analytics to understand relationships between identities, assets, privileges and network activity. Explore potential lateral movement and privilege escalation paths. Apply techniques such as shortest-path analysis, centrality and community detection. Use graph relationships to connect activity that may appear unrelated when individual events are viewed in isolation. AI and investigation automation Use and test AI agents that support activities such as evidence collection, enrichment, correlation and investigation summarisation. Help improve prompts, tools and automated investigation workflows. Evaluate AI-generated results against analyst-led investigations. Apply appropriate security guardrails and ensure human validation and traceability remain part of automated investigations. Develop an understanding of attacks targeting AI and agentic systems. Threat intelligence and collaboration Translate threat intelligence, particularly intelligence relevant to the automotive sector, into practical hunting hypotheses. Support incident response and forensic investigations through analysis of historical telemetry. Work closely with detection engineering, incident response, red teams and regional security teams. Contribute to our threat-hunting library and MITRE ATT&CK coverage. What we are looking for You do not need to be an expert in every technology listed below. We are particularly interested in people with a strong investigative mindset who already have a foundation in cybersecurity and want to develop further in advanced threat hunting. Ideally, you have: A degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Data Science or a related subject, or equivalent practical experience. Around 2–4 years of relevant experience in cybersecurity, for example in threat hunting, SOC/security operations, detection engineering, incident response or security analytics. A good understanding of attacker techniques and MITRE ATT&CK . Experience working with endpoint, network, identity or cloud security telemetry. Working knowledge of Python and SQL , or comparable experience analysing large security datasets. Some practical exposure to machine learning, data analytics or graph technologies . An interest in LLMs and agentic AI , particularly their application to cybersecurity. Strong analytical skills and the ability to investigate incomplete or ambiguous signals. Good written and spoken English and the ability to explain technical findings clearly Certifications such as Security+, BTL1, GSEC or equivalent are welcome but not essential. At Stellantis, we assess candidates based on qualifications, merit and business needs. We welcome applications from …

items.desc: At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business. Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere. Role Summary An established performer who consistently applies analytics capabilities, principles and playbooks to solve business issues, with a moderate level of guidance and direction. Regularly interacts with stakeholders up to Senior Manager level. Experience 1-2+ years for Bachelors/Masters grad (preference for Mathematics or Scientific degree) OR 2+ years experience in a comparable data analytics role with relevant experience Education Demonstrated experience of delivering data-driven insights and recommendations that drove change or performance improvement for stakeholders. Demonstrable intermediate level experience of using R, Python or SQL for data analysis, structuring, transforming and visualising big data* N/A Functional/ Technical Skills Critical thinking and showing an inquisitive mind Problem solving Communication and influencing Information Gathering Listening Statistics SQL, Python, R or similar Basic data visualisation for communicating results to stakeholders of different technical levels Business acumen Role Expectations Basic level ability to extract data from multiple data sources and combine into the required datasets for model building or analytics Has a basic understanding of probability, frequentist , and how to apply to business problems (eg. AB testing, log regression output). Understands difference between statistically signifiant test readout vs exploratory analysis. Demonstrates begineer level understanding and correct applicaton of descriptive statistics. Like Analysis of variance, regression analysis & knowledge of basic probability theorm Is able to select appropriate measurement techniques and design and recommend both simple and complex experiments to answer business questions eg. Pre/post, AB, causal impact etc Understands caveats and more complex approaches to common experiment types (pre/post, AB, causal impact etc). Rudimentary understanding of and ability to build common models such as linear and non-linear regression, clustering etc and a basic understanding the format of the data required for the modelling process. Possesses basic level understanding of common data models, their underlying assumptions, the types of business questions they can best answer, and what data sources would best support the model (i.e. linear and logistic regression). Shows iniative to learn new modelling approaches and techniques and apply those learnings to current projects. Has a basic knowledge of the business domain and uses this knowledge to refine the question at the heart of the modelling project, drive model design decisions (i.e. model selection, feature engineering), and provide recommendations (model improvements, business changes, AB tests, further analysis etc). Manager plays a strong support role Favors iterative delivery and works with stakeholders to refine requirements, agree on what is in scope for each step of the project, and evolve requirements based on learnings and guidance from manager Demonstrates an understanding of technical information to understand and synthesize different data sources and create basic data pipelines and workflows to support the model. Values reproducability and creates shareable code and documentation to share with wider team on tools like github, IEX, confluence. Creates clear visualizations that support the data story and deepen the audience's understanding. Makes established visualisation selection with limited supervision and favors clarity over complexity. Awareness of inclusive design principles and a willingness to learn more and apply learning to visualisations (i.e. color selection). Builds trust and works collaboratively and transparently with stakeholders. Seeks out analytics teammates for peer reviews, brainstorming and other upskilling and improves their own skills by doing the same for both junior and senior teammates. With manager's support, is able to clearly articulate project goals, methodology, caveats and conclusions to technical and non technical audiences and demonstrates good understanding of how to adjust project outputs such as presentations or executive summaries based on the audience's goals and level of technical understanding. items.desc: Do you want to question, change, and steer our company into the future? Are you passionate about technology and ready to make a difference? Then you will thrive at SEB. At SEB, we believe in fresh thinking, new working methods, and innovation to create a fairer and more sustainable world. Since SEB was founded in 1856, our focus on customers and long-term relationships has been at the heart of our success, while we place a strong emphasis on sustainability and digitalization as we shape the future of SEB. With the Tech Trainee programme and as an employee, we'll help you develop new skills and take on more responsibility to create a positive impact. You will become a crucial key player in shaping the future of the bank. Your tech trainee position and your team Join SEB’s IT Asset Management team as a Developer and start your career in an environment where software engineering, data and AI are becoming increasingly connected. You will join our Agile delivery team to design, develop, and maintain reliable integrations that support IT Asset Management across the full IT asset lifecycle. Working with complex data models, you will build APIs and automated data flows that connect our applications with surrounding systems, ensuring data is accurate, consistent, and available where it adds the most value. Your work will support IT asset inventory, process automation, AI registry governance, and compliance, while data visualization, BI, and reporting will help turn this data into actionable insights. We are in the middle of an exciting shift towards agentic system development across our entire delivery. We record decisions in Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and give both humans and AI agents context through progressive disclosure, using skills and AGENTS.md files so the right knowledge shows up at the right time. You will have the opportunity to explore how AI can support everything from coding and testing to documentation, problem solving and solution design. You will use modern development tools and practices, including CI/CD, pair programming, and GitHub Copilot. Our team values open collaboration, continuous learning, and knowledge sharing through initiatives such as “Demo Fridays.” The team consists of both junior and senior developers, creating an environment where you can learn from experienced colleagues while contributing with your own perspectives and ideas. Technologies : Back-end development using .NET and C# Front-end development using Angular REST APIs and system integrations SQL Server, data modelling and complex data flows CI/CD, GitHub and Kubernetes Automation and AI-enabled development using GitHub Copilot LLMs, AI agents and agentic development practices Simultaneously by working in the role you are being recruited to, you will participate in SEB's Tech Trainee Programme for six months. It will give you the opportunity to develop an extensive network within the bank, gain a deep understanding of the financial industry and our global tech organization, and be professionally and personally challenged. As part of the programme, you can expect to: contribute to meaningful projects, work on tech tracks, gain communication and leadership skills, and participate in a hackathon and a business challenge. Key traits to thrive in this role and programme We’re looking for young talents who are curious, motivated, and ready to question the status quo. To thrive in this role and in the Tech Trainee programme, you need to have : Graduated within the past two years, or will graduate before the programme starts on 1st September 2027 – from a relevant academic degree or a two-year vocational education in IT or tech Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to take ownership Great communication skills and to be able to work in English We also believe you have: Have a solid foundation in solution development and programming principles. items.desc: W Allegro tworzymy przyszłość e-commerce, łącząc zaawansowane technologie z realnym wpływem na biznes oraz środowiskiem, które sprzyja rozwojowi – zarówno kompetencji technicznych, jak i miękkich. Jesteśmy jedną z największych i najbardziej nowoczesnych firm technologicznych w Polsce, a Allegro Advertising to jeden z najszybciej rosnących obszarów naszej działalności – z przychodami rosnącymi około 2× szybciej niż platforma Allegro i 3× szybciej niż cały rynek reklamy w Polsce. Zespół Advertising Data & AI działa na styku technologii i biznesu, dostarczając analizy, produkty analityczne i insighty wspierające kluczowe inicjatywy departamentu Advertising. Nasza praca realnie wpływa na rozwój reklamowy największych marek oraz ponad tysięcy sprzedawców działających na Allegro. Poszukujemy analityka danych, który chce pracować z dużą skalą, mieć realny wpływ na decyzje biznesowe i tworzyć rozwiązania oparte na danych, które faktycznie napędzają wzrost. Identyfikowanie szans wzrostu i optymalizacja : Ścisła współpraca z kluczowymi interesariuszami w celu przekształcania złożonych zbiorów danych w jasne rekomendacje, które wzmacniają propozycję wartości (value proposition) naszych produktów reklamowych. items.desc: About ELCA We are ELCA, one of the largest Swiss IT tribe with over 2,200 experts. We are multicultural with offices in Switzerland, Spain, France, Vietnam and Mauritius. Since 1968, our team of engineers, business analysts, software architects, designers and consultants provide tailor-made and standardized solutions to support the digital transformation of major public administrations and private companies in Switzerland. Our activity spans across multiples fields of leading-edge technologies such as AI, Machine & Deep learning, BI/BD, RPA, Blockchain, IoT and CyberSecurity. In this 6-month internship starting in Spring 2027, you'll use agentic AI to uncover hidden business rules in legacy .NET/VB6 code. Your tasks Research and compare agentic AI approaches that combine LLM-driven agents with static and program analysis to mine business rules from legacy code. Select the most promising approach and AI engines, including options beyond LLMs. Design and build a prototype agent that navigates a representative legacy .NET/VB6 codebase on its own and cross-references related modules. Extract and document business rules, turning knowledge that only lives in the code into a clear specification that experts can review. Add mechanisms that flag uncertain findings for expert review. Validate your results with domain experts and use their feedback to improve the agent. Propose a repeatable methodology and best practices for using agentic knowledge mining before modernization, replacement or retirement decisions. Lay the groundwork for a scalable Legacy Modernization Assessment offering for clients across the market. What we offer A dynamic, collaborative workplace with a highly motivated, multicultural team working across international sites Monthly AI meetups with our expert AI team, where you can ask questions and move your topic forward The chance to make a difference in people's lives by building innovative solutions Internal coding events such as Hackathons and Brownbag sessions, plus our technical blog Monthly After-Works organized at each location About your profile Bachelor or Master degree (EPFL, ETH, university) in Computer Science or related discipline You have programming experience in .NET , and ideally some knowledge of VB6/VB.NET (or you're happy to learn). You are familiar with static code analysis. You have worked with different AI engines, LLMs and beyond. You are curious about agentic AI and keen to build your own agent. You like to work in a structured way and to share your findings clearly with experts. You are fluent in written and spoken English, as well as German or French. Application: Please attach your academic transcripts to your application. Applications without transcripts will not be reviewed. items.desc: Position Overview: As we continue to expand and evolve our Supply-Chain-focused Data Integration Platform, we're looking for Python Software Engineer with a strong affinity for AI/ML to join our Product & Engineering team. We launched Pathfinder, which brings AI into the world of EDI and Data Integration – it’s already live in production and proven stable. What we need now is a skilled software engineer to expand its scope with clean, production-grade code. In this role, you’ll build additional AI agents within this established framework, taking them from blueprint to production. These agents leverage both LLMs and hybrid AI/ML systems. Our mission is to connect people, data and intelligence (human & artificial) to optimise processes across the supply chain, always choosing the right tool for the right challenge. Ready to make an impact? You’ll get to take ownership of: Developing Pathfinder, a multi-agent AI system built on protocol-driven, microservice-oriented architecture – where specialised agents are dynamically orchestrated to assist users in navigating the complexities of data integration, automating routine tasks and proactively solving problems to make them significantly more productive. Defining and implementing scalable microservices that drive data mapping, transformation, and intelligent integration. Developing and maintaining RESTful APIs to ensure seamless communication between services and systems. Creating and optimising event-driven data pipelines to enable real-time processing, automation, and decision-making across our products. Evaluating, selecting, and implementing the best-fit tools and technologies to solve complex engineering and data challenges effectively. Collaborating directly with key customers and internal stakeholders to validate solution performance and ensure product impact and usability. What You’ll Bring: 3+ years of professional software engineering with Python as your primary language, and a track record of building and running production-grade software – including being the person who fixed it when it broke. Python craft: strictly typed, well-structured code that goes well beyond scripting or notebooks. You model your data at every boundary – Pydantic, attrs or similar – and you're comfortable working within an established framework. A production mindset: you think about maintainability, testing, telemetry, and debugging, and you’re comfortable handling production issues and contributing to root cause analysis (RCA). Deep, practical async Python: you have built services on asyncio and you know what it buys you and what it doesn't – async generators, cancellation, and why a single blocking call inside a coroutine stalls everything around it. Micro-services and event-driven architectures on top of that. A feel for what goes wrong across a network boundary: timeouts, bounded retries with backoff, idempotency. You read an outbound call with no deadline on it as a defect rather than a detail. Proficiency in designing and consuming RESTful APIs. An affinity for AI/ML: curiosity about or hands-on experience with LLMs and agentic systems is a strong plus, though neither is required – we care more that you engineer well than that you already know this stack. Deep ML specialism is not needed. Strong communication skills in English. Nice to have: Supply chain or logistics domain knowledge – the cherry on top, not a requirement. Willingness to dig into the Java codebase of our core product to understand what functionality is already available, even before it’s exposed via an API. Experience with CI/CD (GitHub Enterprise) and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, Pulumi). Familiarity with cloud AI services (e.g., SageMaker, Bedrock, Azure ML). ML platform DevEx The core components are in place, and now we want to make them great to use. You'll work closely with the data scientists and ML engineers who build recommender systems, personalisation products, and predictive models. Improve our Flyte-based orchestration platform. Speed up local-to-cluster iteration, make runs easier to observe and debug, and turn recurring pain points into platform features, templates and documentation. Standardise how we track and ship models. Define MLflow conventions for experiment tracking, artifacts and the model registry, and build golden paths (well-supported default routes from experiment to production) for model rollout. Develop our Triton-based model serving. Measure and improve latency and cost through caching, scaling strategies, shared or sliced GPUs, and backends for new model types. Listen to users. Talk to the teams using the platform, find out where they lose time, and prioritise accordingly. Multimodal retrieval foundation Today we serve article text embeddings via our vector store (Vespa). A new initiative aims to extend this to podcasts and video too, so that teams across the organization can build search, recommendations and discovery on one shared retrieval layer. Productionalise podcast embeddings. We have a working approach for embedding segmented transcripts. You'll turn it into a reliable, observable and cost-efficient pipeline (orchestrated with Flyte) and feed the results into Vespa, including schema design, indexing and evaluation of retrieval quality. Extend to video. Apply the same transcript-based approach to video content, reusing as much of the podcast pipeline as possible. Explore native video embeddings. Later in the engagement, evaluate current open-weights video and multimodal embedding models against our transcript-based baseline, and give the team a clear, evidence-based recommendation on what is worth adopting. Across both tracks Leave things better documented than you found them. Because this is a time-limited engagement, we expect clear handover: runbooks, architecture notes and knowledge-sharing sessions, so the team can own and evolve everything you build. Share what you learn with the wider organisation and help raise AI literacy among data scientists and other engineers. What we’re looking for: You are an experienced engineer (typically 4+ years) who can work independently, make sound technical decisions, and leave a team stronger. More specifically, you have: Solid experience as an ML engineer, ML platform engineer, or similar, with a track record of taking ML systems from experiment to production. Strong Python skills, with a habit of writing clean, tested code. Hands-on experience with ML orchestration and experiment tracking (Flyte, Kubeflow, MLflow or similar). Flyte and MLflow are a strong plus. Experience with model serving and inference optimisation (Triton inference server, TorchServe, KServe, vLLM or similar), and working knowledge of GPU workloads. Good working knowledge of Docker, Kubernetes and the command line, and comfortable using logs, metrics and traces to find out why something broke. Practical experience with embeddings and retrieval: generating embeddings at scale, vector or hybrid search, and judging retrieval quality. Familiarity with Git, CI/CD (GitHub Actions) and modern cloud-native environments, and with coding assistants (with the judgment to check their output critically). A product mindset for internal platforms: you care whether teams actually adopt what you build, and you think about developer experience, documentation and migration paths. Bonus qualifications: Hands-on experience with Vespa or similar search and vector engines (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Weaviate, Qdrant). items.desc:
ABOUT BLACK FOREST LABS

We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world.

Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use.

Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next.

 


WHY THIS ROLE

We develop AI models and run the infrastructure on which those models are trained, deployed, and served to customers. We're looking for an experienced, hands-on security engineer to protect how our staff work: the accounts they sign in with, the devices they use, the third-party tools they rely on, and the agents they delegate work to. You'll work closely with IT, which operates our employee services and devices.

This is an engineering role: you'll spend your time building tools and automations, designing practical controls, investigating escalations, and shipping changes.

 


WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

These are the areas this role draws from; you're not expected to cover
them all at once:

 - Identity and access. Strengthen how staff authenticate and what they can reach: single sign-on coverage, phishing-resistant authentication, and access provisioning and revocation that stay reliable and complete as people and tools change. Design scoped, short-lived credentials for the tools and agents that act on staff's behalf, and improve our ability to detect credential misuse.

 - Endpoint security. Work with IT on device trust, hardening, and visibility across our fleet. Find practical ways for engineers and researchers to install what they need without introducing unnecessary risk.

 - AI agents and staff tooling. Help staff use agents and AI-powered tools productively and safely. Review the threat models, permissions, and data flows of tools staff build or adopt, including coding agents, desktop assistants, browser extensions, and MCP servers. This includes how staff supervise and stay accountable for delegated actions, and the audit trails that make agent activity reviewable. Build sandboxes, credential patterns, and guardrails that make the secure path the convenient one.

 - Third-party tool security. Define a scalable security review for the tools staff use day to day, and work with IT, which owns procurement and provisioning, to build security checks into how tools are onboarded and offboarded. Maintain a current picture of which tools can reach company code, credentials, and customer data as tools are added and retired.

 - Visibility and response. Make sure identity, endpoint, and SaaS telemetry is collected and usable. Investigate escalations and incidents in these areas, verify that we can contain a compromised account or device quickly, and turn findings into lasting fixes.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong experience in identity and access security and endpoint security. Hands-on experience administering an identity provider and a device-management platform.

 - Practical understanding of OAuth, OIDC, SAML, secrets handling, and authorization design. You can trace how an application obtains and uses credentials and find where access controls can be bypassed.

 - Hands-on engineering ability. You can read unfamiliar code, inspect how an app talks to APIs, and write the automation and tooling that replace manual processes.

 - Experience using LLMs and agents in your own work, along with a clear-eyed view of where they help, where they don't, and how they can be attacked or misused.

 - Good security judgment. You can distinguish meaningful risks from theoretical ones and apply controls in proportion to the risk.

 - Experience supporting researchers, engineers, or other highly technical staff, and a track record of finding secure ways to meet their needs.

 - Comfort working with real autonomy and turning loosely defined problems into concrete improvements.

Experience with macOS security, developer tooling, SaaS security, software distribution, agent integrations, or threat hunting would be particularly relevant, but none is a prerequisite. We're more interested in people who have solved difficult security problems for real users than in candidates who can check every box on a technology list.

 


HOW WE WORK TOGETHER

We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You’ll be based in Europe and work from your home location, with one week each month spent with us in Freiburg to stay connected with the team.

items.desc:
At IQM, we build world-leading quantum computers for the well-being of humankind. We design systems to tackle computational challenges beyond the practical limits of classical machines. Our work sits at the edge of science and engineering. It's complex, demanding, and deeply collaborative. We turn deep research into reliable, full-stack systems that drive discoveries in fields like medicine, energy, and technology, reshaping how the world computes.
 Join the team that gives quantum a heartbeat.
 The work 
 As an Advanced Full Stack Software Engineer , you'll join our Vertical Deployment team within Algorithms and Applications, developing a platform that brings quantum computing closer to real-world applications.
 You'll contribute to building user-facing features for configuring, executing, and monitoring computational workflows, with a focus on frontend development and additional contributions to backend services, APIs, and integrations. You'll take ownership of features from development to deployment, working independently and collaborating with the team to deliver practical solutions.
 What you’ll actually do 
 Design, develop, test, and maintain frontend features using Vue.js and TypeScript , with a focus on creating intuitive, responsive, and user-friendly interfaces.
 Take an active role in shaping the platform's user experience, bringing creativity and design thinking into how complex workflows and technical information are presented.
 Translate user needs and technical requirements into practical frontend solutions, considering usability, functionality, and maintainability.
 Take ownership of feature areas or related task groups, from understanding requirements and proposing solutions to implementation, testing, and deployment.
 Contribute to backend development using Node.js and TypeScript, including building and integrating REST APIs and supporting services.
 Work with PostgreSQL, Redis, and asynchronous workflow systems, addressing challenges such as long-running jobs, task dependencies, retries, and failure handling.
 Debug and resolve issues across different layers of the platform, including frontend, backend, and workflow execution.
 Collaborate with researchers, software engineers, and other stakeholders to understand user needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.
 Participate in code reviews and contribute to coding standards, development practices, and CI/CD processes.
 Identify technical risks, proactively suggest improvements, and make sound implementation decisions while knowing when to seek input.
 What we’re looking for 
 3+ years of professional full-stack experience, focused on the frontend
 Computer Science degree (or related quantitative field) or equivalent industry experience
 Strong frontend skills ( Vue.js , JavaScript), with attention to UX and user flow; some experience working with UI/UX designers
 Solid backend experience: Node.js (TypeScript), REST APIs, relational databases, and job-queue-backed data stores — ideally PostgreSQL and Redis
 Understanding of async processing and workflow systems: long-running jobs, state management, task dependencies, retries, idempotency
 Familiarity with CI/CD, Docker, and logging/monitoring tools such as OpenTelemetry
 Ability to work independently — breaks down ambiguous requirements and owns deliverables with minimal supervision
 Strong communication: explains technical decisions, flags blockers, gives constructive review feedback
 Nice to have 
 Experience with workflow orchestration frameworks, particularly Argo Workflows
 Background in computational, scientific, or other technically complex software platforms
 Familiarity with quantum computing — or interest in learning
 Why IQM? 
 Full-stack quantum computing: From quantum hardware to software layers and beyond, we build across the full-stack.
 High-performance playground: We aim high, and we know sustainable performance only works when life outside work does too—hybrid setups, flexible hours.
 Never the smartest: You won’t always be the smartest person in the room. Neither will we. Expect to learn constantly - from each other and beyond with IQM’s Learning Hub, LinkedIn Learning, and a team-based L&D budget.
 Approachable leadership: Flat hierarchy, direct access. Feel free to approach any leaders. They're friendlier than they look!
 The sweet spot: Big enough to matter. Small enough to move fast. Growing between a startup and a corporation. We’re in the phase where top performers get noticed.
 Bigger than IQM: Our people build know-how for the entire quantum ecosystem. We publish papers, run hackathons, and help shape a market that's still being defined.
 The future of computing won’t build itself. You might be one of the few who do. 
 Meet our people and learn more about IQM on our stories page.
 Explore our scientific publications.
 We'll start interviews and move forward with hiring as soon as we meet strong candidates. Please submit your application soon.
