items.desc: Who are we? We're a smart hydration company rebuilding an industry that still runs on sugar water and single-use packaging. Filtered water, functional flavors, zero bottles. Still, sparkling, cold, and hot. All poured from one tap. We create hydration people want to reach for, starting with the workplace where we help teams thrive. As an AI-native company, we build at speed. In 2025, Aquablu ranked 2nd in the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 (Netherlands) and 30th in the Sifted 250 (Europe), both rankings of the fastest-growing companies by revenue growth. In 2026 we were named a winner of Maya's Culture 100 Europe Awards as one of the best workplaces to thrive in. Growing that fast and thriving comes down to our people. Our team is our biggest asset and one that we're proud of. We're committed to maintaining our vibrant culture as we continue to grow. The Role You'll own the quality of the firmware and embedded systems across our physical product portfolio. That means making sure every firmware release is tested, reliable, and ready for the field, and that defects are caught before they reach a client. This is a senior, hands-on role. You understand electronics and embedded systems well enough to reproduce and diagnose issues yourself, read a schematic, and build your own test kits and jigs. You don't wait for an engineer to set things up for you. You run your area independently. Over the past year, we've built a validation framework that changed how we release firmware. We now ship on evidence instead of gut feel: structured test cycles across our product generations, tracked defects across release candidates, formal release reviews, and controlled rollouts to the fleet. Your first job is to own that framework and keep it strong. Your bigger job is to take it further. Today, testing mostly happens once a release is nearly done. We want to catch risk earlier, inside the firmware stage-gate process, through integration testing, corner cases, and tests at the edges of the operating envelope. You'll move firmware QA from reacting to preventing. What You'll Do Embedded & Firmware Testing Own test strategy and execution for firmware and embedded systems across our physical products. Reproduce field and development issues independently, using your electrical and embedded understanding. Develop diagnostic and validation methods for firmware features, aligned with our stage-gate process. Define and run regression testing ahead of every firmware release. Test at the system-integration and interface level, including the edges of the operating envelope where real risk sits. Reliability & Field Quality Support containment and root-cause analysis for firmware and embedded field issues. Feed field learnings back into the test suite. Every field issue is a missing test. Contribute embedded input to DFMEA and PFMEA and to our stage-gate quality gates. What You Bring Experience building embedded test capability from an early stage, a background that bridges electronics and firmware, or exposure to a stage-gate release process for embedded products sets you apart. 6+ years in embedded or Firmware QA A strong electrical and embedded background: you read schematics, understand PCB and hardware behavior, and reproduce embedded issues on your own. Firmware testing experience across diagnostics, validation, and regression. A hands-on, self-sufficient approach: you build your own test kits, jigs, and test environments. Experience with system-level integration testing for a hardware and firmware product. A pragmatic, risk-weighted mindset: you test in proportion to the risk, not for coverage's sake. Comfort in a lean, fast-moving team where you own your area, and the habit of using AI tools every day. Why Aquablu? You'll build the foundation that lets quality scale at Aquablu, with real ownership from day one and a direct line to our firmware and digital engineering teams. A yearly base salary between €70k and €98k (incl. 8% holiday allowance) 26 paid holiday days Equity through our Aquablu for All plan: everyone shares in what we're building Healthy (heavily discounted) lunches Urban Sports Club membership Access to the Corporate Benefits platform for endless savings Travel compensation >10km A pension plan by Zwitserleven Endless amounts of our very own flavored water Check out our YouTube to get a feeling for the culture at Aquablu

You build cloud-agnostic services, application programming interfaces and workflows, from data ingestion to deployment and monitoring. You work in a multidisciplinary team with end-to-end ownership. Together we achieve more than alone We believe in the power of differences. By combining people’s differences, we become an even better bank. You can also contribute to banking services for our personal and business clients and to social issues such as the food and energy transitions. Why everyone is welcome at Rabobank At Rabobank, we are working toward a culture where everyone feels welcome. We value our differences and use them to collaborate more effectively and make better decisions. We do this step by step, paying attention to what is going well and to the areas where we can continue to improve. By being open to different perspectives, we are creating an environment where colleagues feel heard.  We are looking for a highly technical Solution Architect, operating at the intersection of strategy, solution design, and technology delivery.
 The candidate will be expected to remain hands-on with technology and code, steer critical architectural and engineering decisions, and support the design and implementation of complex banking platforms. The role requires the ability to translate business priorities, regulatory requirements, and operational needs into clear, robust, and well-reasoned technical solutions, while aligning with (and contributing to) enterprise architecture standards and target-state roadmaps.
 The successful candidate will work effectively with both business and technology stakeholders, driving architectural alignment and consensus across multiple teams, and taking ownership of solution delivery from concept through production adoption.
 The role increasingly involves the adoption of Artificial Intelligence solutions. The candidate is expected to demonstrate a solid understanding of how modern AI capabilities can be responsibly integrated into financial-services platforms, as well as proven experience in leveraging AI tooling and orchestrating AI agents at scale to accelerate delivery, improve engineering productivity, and enable new execution models.
 What you'll be doing
 • Design end-to-end solutions — own the architectural design of scalable, resilient, and high-performing systems across complex banking domains.
 • Stay hands-on — remain actively involved in implementation, code reviews, and technical problem-solving alongside engineering teams.
 • Define the standards — develop guidelines, non-functional requirements (NFRs), archetypes, walking skeletons, and reusable components that set the bar across squads.
 • Build for scale and resilience — design distributed systems using microservices architecture, RESTful APIs, and event-driven approaches capable of handling enterprise-grade, high-throughput workloads.
 • Harness AI as a force multiplier — identify opportunities to integrate AI capabilities (including LLMs, agentic frameworks, and AI-assisted tooling) into platform design, and actively orchestrate multi-agent workflows to accelerate project delivery — balancing innovation with the compliance and risk demands of a regulated environment.
 • Champion cloud-native delivery — ensure all solutions align with our GCP adoption strategy, DevSecOps principles, and the firm's SDLC standards.
 • Bridge business and technology — work closely with business stakeholders and engineering teams to translate complex banking requirements into elegant, pragmatic technical solutions.
 • Drive engineering excellence — champion Agile methodologies and best practices, leveraging tools like Jira and Confluence to keep delivery sharp and transparent.
 What you'll need to succeed
 • 7–12 years of experience in software architecture and engineering, with a strong emphasis on hands-on delivery of enterprise-scale distributed systems.
 • Proven track record in a banking or financial services environment, with a solid grasp of transactional systems, data consistency, and regulatory context.
 • Deep expertise in Java and hands-on experience designing and implementing REST APIs, microservices, and event-driven architectures.
 • A working understanding of the AI landscape — including LLMs, prompt engineering, agentic patterns, RAG architectures, and AI orchestration frameworks — and how to apply them responsibly within a regulated enterprise context.
 • Practical ability to leverage AI tooling as a force multiplier — you know how to harness AI coding assistants, orchestrate multi-agent workflows at scale, and use agentic frameworks to dramatically accelerate delivery cycles, reduce time-to-solution, and free engineering teams to focus on higher-order problems.
 • Solid experience across the data domain — both relational and non-relational databases.
 What you'll get in return

 #UnlockYourPotential : Play a role of autonomy with high visibility and exposure 
 #BalanceLifeAndCareer : Flexible working hours & working hybrid; 
 A professional but still friendly work environment ;

As an Applied AI Architect for the Meta Enterprise Platform, you will serve as a strategic technical leader for our most complex enterprise AI opportunities and help shape how customers adopt our Enterprise AI products, such as Model API. You will combine deep Generative AI expertise, enterprise architecture judgment, and executive-level communication to define AI strategies that translate into production adoption, sustained API usage, and measurable business value.
This role combines pre-sales technical leadership with post-sales adoption and expansion, with impact extending beyond individual accounts. You will own the technical strategy for a portfolio of strategic customers or a high-impact industry segment, lead the most ambiguous architecture and deployment challenges, and turn successful customer solutions into repeatable approaches that improve outcomes across the broader business.
You will remain hands-on in architecture, evaluation, prototyping, and technical problem-solving while multiplying the impact of other architects, customer teams, and partners. Through influence rather than formal people management, you will align Sales, Product, Engineering, and specialist teams around customer outcomes and strategic investments that advance the Meta Enterprise Platform.
Enterprise AI Strategy & Technical Discovery - Partner with enterprise executives, technology leaders, and Sales to identify the highest-value AI opportunities across business units. Translate ambiguous business objectives and complex technology environments into prioritized use cases, target architectures, and multi-year adoption roadmaps. Establish the technical decision criteria and trade-offs that guide investment and deployment Strategic Technical Account Ownership - Own technical strategy and success across a portfolio of strategic customers or a high-impact industry segment, from initial discovery through production adoption and expansion. Establish joint technical account plans, adoption milestones, and measures of value. Use API consumption, technical account health, evaluation results, and business outcomes to identify systemic blockers and new opportunities, mobilizing cross-functional teams to resolve them AI Architecture Leadership - Lead architecture decisions for the most complex enterprise AI deployments, spanning model selection, RAG, agentic workflows and tool use, data pipelines, and enterprise integration. Resolve cross-system trade-offs in quality, latency, reliability, security, and cost. Define reusable architecture patterns and technical standards that can be adopted across accounts and by other architects Evaluation & Proof of Value - Establish rigorous, use-case-specific evaluation approaches that connect model and application performance to customer business goals. Lead high-stakes technical evaluations and competitive proofs of value, define acceptance criteria, and use evidence to guide purchasing and production decisions. Turn successful evaluations into reusable benchmarks, reference implementations, and deployment guidance Enterprise Trust & Governance - Lead technical discussions on AI security, privacy, data governance, and responsible AI with enterprise stakeholders. Partner with customer and internal Security, Privacy, and Legal specialists to evaluate requirements and design appropriate controls, guardrails, and review processes. Convert recurring technical concerns into reusable deployment patterns and product feedback Hands-on Solutions & Production Adoption - Build targeted demos, prototypes, and reference implementations to resolve novel technical questions and demonstrate viable approaches. Guide customer engineering teams through production architecture reviews, integration, operational readiness, and adoption, addressing challenges involving legacy systems, identity, networking, observability, and application performance. Retain accountability for technical outcomes without assuming ownership of customer production application development Product & Go-to-Market Influence - Synthesize insights across customers to identify unmet needs, common integration barriers, and opportunities for differentiated solutions. Build evidence-based recommendations that influence Product and Engineering priorities, platform capabilities, and go-to-market strategy. Lead cross-functional initiatives from problem identification through delivery and validate their impact on customer adoption and business outcomes Scaled Solutions & Ecosystem Enablement - Convert strategic customer engagements into reusable reference architectures, evaluation assets, deployment playbooks, and industry-specific solution approaches. items.desc: Senior Remote Full-time B2B: UoP: A Forward Deployed Engineer at Synergy Codes works side by side with the client: you get to know their problem and build a working solution yourself. You own it from the first conversation all the way to production. What you will bring to the table About this job opening Our clients build complex applications: diagram editors, workflow builders, and tools for process modeling and data visualization. More and more often, they also want to add AI to them, such as agents, modeling assistants or process automation. Behind every one of these ideas, though, there is a specific process, specific data and specific people, and you need to understand them first. That's where you come in. You sit down with the client's team, see how they actually work, build a prototype and take it to production. Then you bring what you learned from each deployment back to our teams. What might surprise us What you will do Discovery with the client. You run workshops and observe how the client's team works. You look for manual workarounds and bottlenecks, then help the client understand what is really worth building. Prototypes that work. Within days of getting access, you build a prototype on the client's real data instead of a presentation. It might be an AI agent, a workflow that orchestrates the client's systems, or an interface to them, such as a diagram editor. The road to production. You take the solution to production: testing, monitoring, error handling, security and documentation, and for AI solutions also evaluations and model cost control. You make sure it works for the client, not just in the demo. Integrations. You connect agents and workflows to the client's systems, including ones they've relied on for years (APIs, databases, enterprise systems). You also choose models and their providers. Scaling up or handing over. When a project grows, you become the technical lead of the team that joins it. When the next client is waiting for you, you hand the project over so it runs without you. You leave the architecture and key decisions documented, agent instructions in the repository, and you introduce the client to their new point of contact. Value in numbers. At the start, you agree with the client how you'll both measure success, for example process handling time, the number of manual steps or cost. After deployment, you report the results using the same metrics, in terms that make sense to both the CTO and the business. Risks and limitations. You name the risks and limitations of the solution (data, security, model cost and quality) before the client runs into them. Product feedback. When several clients need the same thing, you don't build it from scratch again. You flag it to our product teams and add it to our best practices. Sales and estimation support. You join conversations with clients before the contract is signed and support our Solutions Engineer, especially with estimates. With existing clients, you spot the next problems worth solving. Who you'll work with: On a project, you work in tandem with a project manager: the PM owns the contract, budget and schedule, and you own the solution. You work closely with our CTO, the product team and the Solutions Engineer. A business analyst is sometimes on the project, but not always, so you can gather requirements on your own. Your work in detail What we expect Must have: At least 5 years of experience in software development, including as a senior engineer or tech lead. Several production deployments for clients, taken all the way from conversations with users to running in production. You're comfortable across the full stack, with backend as your strong suit: API design, databases, integrations (REST, webhooks) and the cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP). On our projects you'll work with Node.js, Python and PostgreSQL on the backend and TypeScript, React and Angular on the frontend. You don't need to know everything, but you pick up new technologies quickly. AI agents. By an agent, we mean software, not just a prompt or a subagent description: for example, an agent built with LangGraph or Pydantic AI, or a custom harness for a specific use case. You have experience building agents and have shipped at least one. You know tool calling, MCP, context management, RAG, multi-agent workflows and evaluations. Ideally, someone is actually using an agent you built. You build prototypes fast and know when "good enough" is enough. You can also estimate work and risks for a quote before the scope is fully defined. You speak fluent English (C1 or higher) and are comfortable talking to CTOs, product owners and business users, since most of our clients are based abroad. You explain what technology can and can't do without jargon. You protect client data. You use AI tools only within the scope the client has agreed to and design solutions with data security in mind. You're comfortable with ambiguity and take ownership of outcomes, not just tasks. Nice to have: …
